No `moratorium`/`restructuring`, `insolvency` (IBC), `deceased`, `fraud`, `litigation`/`court_stay`, `ots_in_progress`, `vulnerable_customer`, `lawyer_represented` kinds exist, and `authority/features.py:32` defines a *different* `SILENCING_HOLDS = frozenset({"hardship", "complaint", "bereavement", "legal"})`.

**Impact.** A limitation period lapses under a hardship hold with nobody told; conversely an IBC moratorium (contact is an offence) or an RBI Resolution-Framework restructuring cannot be expressed except by misusing 'hardship'. Two modules in the same repo disagree on whether `legal` or `dispute` is silencing — the 'one definition' the docstrings promise does not exist.

**Fix.** Extend the hold-kind CHECK and make per-kind semantics (which actions survive, whether the statutory clock is paused, review SLA) a versioned rule row; when a silencing hold vetoes LEGAL_NOTICE raise a `statutory_clock_held` work item for legal; unify the two SILENCING_HOLDS definitions.

### `visit-intimation-rule-has-no-reader` — The 2027 prior-visit intimation and field prerequisites rules are seeded but nothing in the veto stack or planner reads them

### `legal-veto-wrong-statute-and-prerequisites` — _legal_veto models NI Act s.138 on a mandate bounce, waits 21 days then also needs a field rung, ignores the return reason, and requires a phone/email instead of a postal address

**backend/agent_core/treatment/policy.py:449** · compliance · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T07-policy-arb-actions`

policy.py:452-460 `# NI Act s.138 runs from the bounce and gives the drawer 15 days to pay after service ... if features.open_bounce_id and (features.bounce_age_hours or 0) >= 24 * 21: return None; return LEGAL_PREREQUISITES`. LEGAL_NOTICE is rung 5 (actions.py:122-124) so with `max_rung_advance=1` it also needs an observed rung-4 (field) event within LADDER_MEMORY=30d (policy.py:185; engine.py:57). policy.py:182-183 `if action == A.LEGAL_NOTICE and not (features.has_email or features.has_phone): return NO_CHANNEL_ADDRESS`. `bounce_reason` is not consulted in `_legal_veto`; `at` is unused.

**Impact.** (a) An electronic mandate return is actionable under PSS Act s.25, not NI Act s.138 (cheques); the notice template and the wording of the offence differ. (b) The demand must be issued within 30 days of receipt of the return memo; waiting 21 days and then requiring a prior field visit means the window is routinely missed — the engine will almost never serve a valid notice, and when it does it may be time-barred. (c) A technical return is not an offence; the veto would allow a notice on one. (d) A registered-post notice needs an address, not a phone.

**Fix.** Make legal prerequisites a rule row per instrument (cheque vs NACH/e-mandate vs UPI) with the limitation clock (30 days from memo) computed from `mandate_presentations.settled_at`; permit only return reasons the statute covers; require `has_postal_address`; exempt LEGAL_NOTICE from the rung ladder (it is a statutory act, not an escalation step) and instead require a documented prior demand attempt.

### `per-action-db-round-trips-and-minute-keyed-cache` — Each decision re-loads the customer, consent and counters once per channel action and resolves the rule set per slot-minute; at bank volume this is tens of millions of queries a day for values already in memory

**backend/agent_core/treatment/policy.py:470** · scale · missing-for-production · 1/1 confirm · reader `T07-policy-arb-actions`

policy.py:470-476 calls `contact_policy.evaluate` per channel action (5 of 10 actions), each doing `_load_customer`, `_channel_status`, `_today_count`, `_last_counted_at`, `_week_counted`, `_weekly_cap_for` and `policy_rules.resolve` (contact_policy.py:551-590). `resolve` keys its cache on `instant.replace(second=0...)` (policy_rules.py:312-316) so every distinct slot minute misses; `_mandate_veto` resolves twice (policy.py:297-303,315-320) and is re-run per channel action when `bounce_reason == 'technical'` (policy.py:222-224). The engine already resolved rules once at engine.py:346 and features already hold dnd/consent/window/counters (features.py:518-525,882-888).

**Impact.** A 1M-account nightly sweep (TREATMENT_SWEEP=1) issues ~30 contact-gate queries per account plus ~8 rule resolutions, against a `_CACHE_MAX=512` cache that clears wholesale (policy_rules.py:437-441). The sweep window is blown and the DB is the bottleneck for a value that changes yearly.

**Fix.** Resolve rules once per decision (pass the RuleSet into `veto`/`_mandate_veto`/`_contact_veto`) and key the cache on the rule-set boundary (effective_from/to) rather than the minute; add a `contact_policy.evaluate_from_features(features, channel, at, rules)` for the scheduling vetoes and hit the DB only for the volume caps.

### `upsell-bucket-guard-dead` — suppresses_upsell never applies UPSELL_BLOCKING_BUCKETS, so reco may pitch a product to a 90+ DPD borrower

**backend/agent_core/treatment/policy.py:498** · compliance · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T07-policy-arb-actions`

policy.py:498 `UPSELL_BLOCKING_BUCKETS = frozenset({A.B_61_90, A.B_90_PLUS})` has no reference anywhere in backend (grep); policy.py:513-531 only queries `treatment_holds` kinds. reco/engine.py:309-323 relies on this function as its only collections-state gate. The query also has no tenant scoping and uses DB `now()`.

**Impact.** Digital Lending Guidelines require separation of collection and selling; an NPA borrower with no hold row on file is eligible for a cross-sell pitch from the same platform that is dunning them — a reputational and regulatory finding.

**Fix.** Have `suppresses_upsell` also read the worst account's DPD (or accept `bucket` from reco features) and return `bucket:<b>` for UPSELL_BLOCKING_BUCKETS; add a test.

### `planner-second-copy-of-window` — The planner recomputes the calling window from constants and ignores policy_rules, so any published tightening makes the engine go quiet instead of planning the next legal slot

**backend/agent_core/treatment/timing.py:87** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T07-policy-arb-actions`

timing.py:87-95 `if A.spec(action).channel == "voice": start, end = RBI_VOICE_START, RBI_VOICE_END ... return start, end` / `return 0, 24` for non-voice; no `policy_rules.resolve`. The veto then evaluates that slot via contact_policy which does read rules (contact_policy.py:494-500 `window = rules.calling_window(channel)`), so a slot at 08:00 under a client window of 09:00-18:00 is vetoed `contact:outside_calling_hours` (policy.py:484) rather than re-planned. policy.py:12-16 claims this second copy does not exist.

**Impact.** A client rule narrowing voice to 09:00-18:00, or publishing an 08:00-19:00 window for WhatsApp in 2027, causes every voice/WhatsApp candidate whose first feasible instant falls in the gap to be excluded for that decision; the engine reports contact vetoes that look like a compliance stop rather than a planner that could have picked 09:00. Recovery falls and the reason string misleads the supervisor.

**Fix.** Pass the resolved RuleSet into `timing.plan` (engine already computes `_rules` at engine.py:346) and derive `_window_for` as intersection(statutory published window or fallback, client/product window, consent hours). Keep contact_policy as the authoritative check.

### `no-upsell-hold-kind-violates-check-and-poisons-the-call-transaction` — The default hardship card's suppress_upsell always fails a CHECK constraint, and on Postgres that aborts the whole post-call transaction so the actions after it fail too

**backend/post_call_actions.py:260** · correctness · defect · unverified (verifier-added) · reader `T07-policy-arb-actions`

post_call_actions.py:256-262 inserts into treatment_holds with kind 'no_upsell'. The table's CHECK permits five kinds only: alembic/versions/20260814_0069_treatment_engine.py:87-89 sa.CheckConstraint("kind IN ('hardship','dispute','complaint','bereavement','legal')", name='ck_treatment_holds_kind'), and a Grep for 'no_upsell' across the whole repo returns only post_call_actions.py:260 and its own excuse at :279 ('`no_upsell` may not be a permitted hold kind on this schema version') - no migration ever adds it, and db_treatment_holds.py:39 HOLD_KINDS and schemas.py:3330 agree on the same five. The verb is reachable from the shipped default card: agent_core/cards/defaults.py:257 PostCallRule(when='hardship_declared', do=['place_hold', 'suppress_upsell', 'confirm_written']). post_call_actions.apply (:535-563) runs the verbs in order on the caller's connection with no savepoint - the try/except at :558-562 catches the Python exception but cannot undo the aborted Postgres transaction - so every statement after it, including 'confirm_written' (the message that quotes the hold's end date, per the comment at :251-254) and the caller's own writes in call_closer.py:696, raises InFailedSqlTransaction.

**Impact.** Every call on which a borrower declares hardship runs place_hold, then a constraint violation, then nothing. The upsell suppression the borrower was told is in place is never recorded, and depending on where the enclosing transaction commits relative to call_closer.py:696 the hardship hold itself and the written confirmation are lost with it - the one call outcome where a hold matters most is the one that fails to persist. Two of the treatment engine's safety properties are downstream of that hold row: policy._hold_veto (policy.py:109-112) and policy.suppresses_upsell (policy.py:513-531).

**Fix.** Either add 'no_upsell' to the ck_treatment_holds_kind CHECK in a migration (and to db_treatment_holds.HOLD_KINDS, schemas.py:3330 and policy.UPSELL_BLOCKING_HOLDS so it is actually enforced), or drop the verb. Independently, wrap each verb in post_call_actions.apply in conn.begin_nested() so one failing action costs its own action and nothing else - which is what the function's docstring at :514-516 already claims it does.

### `contract-not-consumed-by-any-executor` — The Action Contract is built only for the API payload; no channel executes under it

**backend/agent_core/treatment/contract.py:88** · integration · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T08-enact-contract`

contract.build is reached only via TreatmentResult.action_contract (engine.py:118-125), called from db_treatment_holds.py:326 to decorate a JSON response. enact.py never imports contract. _dial_bot builds `mission_mod.build(..., decision=decision)` (enact.py:371-379), whose envelope uses a different objective vocabulary (`objective_for_trigger` → 'bounce_cure'/'dpd_reminder', mission.py:533-541, vs contract's 'payment_commitment'/'triage', contract.py:41-50), a fixed `prohibited = ["third_party_disclosure", "pressure_language"]` (mission.py:298-299) instead of the holds-derived list, the card's max_duration_sec instead of MAX_DURATION_BY_BUCKET, and no maxWaiverInr/waiverRequiresIdentityCheck. SMS/WhatsApp copy never sees holds at all; a 'bereavement' hold's `discuss_arrears` prohibition (contract.py:211-212) is unenforced by the text at enact.py:270.

**Impact.** Two envelopes for one authorisation, only one of which is audited by the tests and the docs; a regulator shown the contract is shown something the bot never received. Holds added between plan and send (dispute raised at 10:00, plan sent at 15:00) are not re-checked at enact time.

**Fix.** Make enact_one build the contract at send time (with fresh holds) and pass it into every handler: mission.build takes it as the envelope source, _copy selects the template variant from strategy/prohibited, and persist the contract JSON on the decision row (contract_json) for audit.

### `enact-touch-booked-before-executor-can-fail` — Contact budget is consumed for sends that never happen

**backend/agent_core/treatment/enact.py:122** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T08-enact-contract`

`admitted = contact_policy.admit(...)` at enact.py:122 inserts an 'allowed', touch_counted event and reserves the day slot (contact_policy.py:955-989) before `ref = handler(...)` at enact.py:145. Every failure after that — `raise NoExecutor("no_phone_on_file")` (280,320,354), `sms_not_configured` (323), `outside_service_window_no_template` (292), `NO_GRIEVANCE_CONTACT` (253), `no_promise_to_attach_followup_to` (519), `card_forbids_mission` (370), `fleet_busy`/`dial_refused` (409), or the generic `enactment_failed` (152) — commits in the same transaction as that allowed event.

**Impact.** The borrower's daily/weekly cap and cooling-off are spent on phantom contacts; the next genuine attempt is denied (daily_cap/cooling_off), which itself becomes another 'cancelled'. On a bank book this is systematic under-contact that looks like compliance.

**Fix.** Run the cheap executor preconditions (phone on file, SMS configured, template/window, grievance footer, promise ref, card permits mission) before admit(); on any post-admit failure, write a compensating contact_events row (outcome='voided') or delete the reservation inside the same transaction via a contact_policy.release(conn, event_id).

### `enact-cancel-reason-not-persisted` — Eight distinct cancellation causes collapse into one label with no reason column; the 84 cancelled rows cannot be explained from the data

**backend/agent_core/treatment/enact.py:141** · observability · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T08-enact-contract`

Seven call sites write the same thing — `decisions.record_outcome(decision_id, "cancelled", conn=conn)` at enact.py:89 (plan_expired), 93 (no_executor), 103 (unknown_action), 108 (customer_gone), 141 (contact:<reason>), 147 (NoExecutor: ~15 sub-reasons), 152 (enactment_failed). The `note` string survives only as `logger.info("treatment plan %s action=%s acted=%s note=%s", ...)` at enact.py:873-879. record_outcome (decisions.py:328-350) accepts only the outcome word and the DDL (05_collections.sql:369-373) has no outcome_reason. Only two sub-causes leave a trace elsewhere: gate denials (contact_events source='treatment', related_id=decision_id, outcome='denied') and voice refusals (call_attempts.suppressed_reason).

**Impact.** A model-risk reviewer asked 'why did the engine cancel 37% of its own plans' has no answer; ops cannot distinguish a config gap (sms_not_configured, no_grievance_contact) from a capacity fact (fleet_busy) from a compliance veto. The OPE reader upstream treats 'cancelled' as one class, so the learning loop is blind to the executor's failure modes.

**Fix.** Add `outcome_reason TEXT` (and `outcome_detail jsonb`) to treatment_decisions; extend record_outcome(decision_id, outcome, reason=...) and pass the note at every site; expose the breakdown in decisions.insights(). Backfill from contact_events/call_attempts where possible.

### `enact-cancelled-closes-case` — Capacity and configuration refusals terminate the borrower's case instead of re-deciding it

**backend/agent_core/treatment/enact.py:147** · statistics · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T08-enact-contract`

enact.py:141-153 writes 'cancelled' for gate denials, NoExecutor and exceptions; followthrough.py:69 `RESOLVING = frozenset({"paid", "ptp", "superseded", "cancelled"})` and open_cases selects only `latest.outcome = ANY(:unresolved)` (followthrough.py:387). decisions.py:207-212 says a cancelled plan 'is a decision that needs making again', but nothing asks again until the next external trigger. The in-code comment at enact.py:405-408 ('the plan stays claimed') describes behaviour that does not exist.

**Impact.** A bounce case whose first plan hit fleet_busy, daily_cap or outside_calling_hours is silently dropped from the ladder; the borrower is never contacted about that bounce. 84 cancellations on a 20-customer book means most cases ended this way.

**Fix.** Split the label: 'cancelled' only for terminal reasons (customer_gone, no_executor, unknown_action); use a new non-resolving outcome (e.g. 'deferred' or 'blocked') for gate/capacity/config refusals and let followthrough.open_cases re-decide them with a backoff; or have enact_one call followthrough.advance() directly on a blocked plan.

### `enact-work-items-marked-enacted-with-no-consumer` — mandate_representment / emi_date_change / self_service_plan are marked enacted although nothing performs them; the clerk completes the job as 'skipped: wait'

**backend/agent_core/treatment/enact.py:155** · correctness · missing-for-production · 1/1 confirm · reader `T08-enact-contract`

_hand_to_lms (720-733), _change_emi_date (770-782) and _open_self_service_plan (825-838) only `_enqueue_work(...)`; enact_one then runs `decisions.mark_enacted(decision_id, ref=ref, ...)` at 155. No module consumes those workflow types (grep across backend for 'mandate_representment'/'emi_date_change'/'self_service_plan' finds only config, insights and enact). Worse, clerk._run (clerk.py:135-150) reads `action = str(payload.get("action") or "")` — these payloads carry no 'action' key — and returns `{"skipped": True, "reason": "wait"}`, so process_one calls `finish(jid, ok=True)` and the job is 'completed'. The mandate_presentations row stays status='scheduled' forever (no settlement path, see invariants).

**Impact.** The corpus records 'treatment given' for interventions that never reached the LMS or the borrower; followthrough then labels them paid/no_answer after the 72h/35-day grace, so the uplift model learns a phantom effect for the design note's 'highest-ROI action'. The mandate executor default 'lms' is a stub, not a safe half.

**Fix.** Do not mark_enacted on enqueue; introduce a 'handed_off' state and let the LMS adapter/webhook (or a work_runtime consumer) call mark_enacted with the LMS reference. Register explicit workflow handlers in clerk for the three types and fail loudly on an unknown workflow_type. Until an adapter exists, refuse with NoExecutor('no_lms_adapter_configured') exactly as _submit_to_rail does.

### `enact-no-payment-recheck-for-sweep-triggers` — dpd_tick and pre_due plans are sent even if the borrower paid after the sweep

**backend/agent_core/treatment/enact.py:192** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T08-enact-contract`

_resolved_since handles only `kind == "bounce"` and `kind == "broken_ptp"` (enact.py:182-191) and `return False` otherwise. The sweep opens a case per account per day (followthrough.py:52-57) and its plan may be scheduled hours later; a payment in between is visible in ledger_entries/payment_intents (the same tables followthrough._paid_since reads, followthrough.py:257-283) but is never consulted here.

**Impact.** 'You are overdue, pay here' to a borrower who paid this morning — a complaint generator and, under ¶100AA, harassment evidence. Also corrupts labels: the plan is enacted then labelled 'paid' as if it caused the payment.

**Fix.** Extend _resolved_since with the account-level check: a payment posted after created_at, or accounts.dpd = 0 / outstanding <= 0 re-read at send time, returns True (superseded).

### `enact-sms-free-form-vs-dlt` — SMS body is composed free-form; India requires a TRAI DLT-registered content template, header and entity

**backend/agent_core/treatment/enact.py:264** · compliance · hidden-assumption · 1/1 confirm · reader `T08-enact-contract`

`_copy` returns `f"{brand}: your instalment{money} on the account ending {tail} is overdue. {ask} {footer}"` (enact.py:264-272) and _send_sms hands it to `twilio_sms.send(to_phone=..., body=body, ...)` (327-333), which posts `{"to": to, "from_": from_number(), "body": body}` (twilio_sms.py:81-85) with no template id, no DLT entity/PE id, and a from-number rather than a registered 6-char sender header.

**Impact.** On an Indian carrier the message is scrubbed as unregistered and silently undelivered (or the route is blocked); the engine labels these no_answer after 8h and escalates to voice. Works on a Twilio sandbox with a US number, fails in a bank.

**Fix.** Model SMS as (template_id, variables) with the DLT-registered text held per tenant; carry DLT PE/TM ids and the sender header through the provider adapter; treat a template mismatch as NoExecutor before admit().

### `enact-phone-alt-third-party` — Dunning copy and dials fall back to phone_alt without knowing whose number it is

**backend/agent_core/treatment/enact.py:278** · privacy · hidden-assumption · 1/1 confirm · reader `T08-enact-contract`

`phone = customer.get("phone_primary") or customer.get("phone_alt")` at enact.py:278 (WhatsApp), 318 (SMS), 352 (dial) and 437 (suppressed dial). The message names the brand, the arrears and the account tail (enact.py:270-271). In Indian lending phone_alt is routinely a reference/relative/employer number.

**Impact.** Sending 'your instalment is overdue' to a third party is exactly the RBI Fair Practices Code / ¶100AA disclosure breach the contract lists as ALWAYS_PROHIBITED (contract.py:78-81); DPDP purpose-limitation is also breached.

**Fix.** Only use phone_alt when it carries a verified 'belongs_to_borrower' flag (or consent record) and never for written dunning; make the choice explicit in the decision (phone_slot) at plan time so the gate can veto it.

### `enact-whatsapp-template-drops-footer` — Outside the 24h window the delivered WhatsApp is the registered template, not the composed body with the grievance footer

**backend/agent_core/treatment/enact.py:299** · compliance · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T08-enact-contract`

`use_template=not inside` and `template_params=[str(customer.get("name") or ""), pay_url or ""] if not inside else None` (enact.py:299-304). whatsapp_outbound.py:497-506 then calls `wa.send_template_message(..., body_params=list(params))`; the `body` produced by _copy is only INSERTed into messages (promise_fulfillment.py:420-428). Whether the tenant's WHATSAPP_TREATMENT_TEMPLATE carries ¶100AA is unknown to the code, and `pay_url or ""` passes an empty parameter when no intent exists, which Meta rejects.

**Impact.** Most treatment WhatsApps are cold (no inbound in 24h), so most go by template: the compliance guarantee the module was rewritten to provide does not apply to the majority path, and the empty-param case fails at the provider and is labelled undeliverable, escalating the ladder for a config reason.

**Fix.** Refuse (NoExecutor) when no pay_url exists and the template requires one; validate at startup that the treatment template's registered body contains the officer disclosure (store the registered text per tenant); record which text was actually delivered.

### `enact-no-send-time-idempotency-sms-voice` — SMS send and carrier dial are side effects inside the claim transaction with no idempotency key; a failed commit double-sends

**backend/agent_core/treatment/enact.py:327** · reliability · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T08-enact-contract`

`result = twilio_sms.send(...)` (enact.py:327) and `outbound.place(dbmod.engine, attempt, to_phone=phone)` (404) execute while `conn` (engine.begin() at 868) is still open; `mark_enacted` swallows its own failure (decisions.py:303-304) and the commit at the end of process_one can fail on connection loss or the statement timeout. The row is then enacted=false, outcome NULL and eligible for claim_due again; contact_policy's dedupe (`_already_counted_related`, contact_policy.py:414-437) cannot help because the allowed event rolled back with the same transaction. Nothing passes decision_id as a provider idempotency key (twilio_sms.py:81-85 has none; outbound.reserve counts prior attempts but does not refuse, outbound.py:352-367).

**Impact.** Duplicate dunning SMS/calls on infrastructure hiccups — precisely the harassment pattern RBI's frequency rules exist to prevent — and double-counted attempts in the corpus.

**Fix.** Two-phase enactment: claim → write enacted_ref='pending:<channel>' and commit → perform the send with decision_id as the provider idempotency key / dedupe on delivery_receipts.related_id → mark_enacted in a new transaction; on re-claim, if a receipt or attempt with this decision_id exists, finalise instead of resending.

### `enact-human-call-requires-promise` — human_call cannot be enacted for a borrower with no promise history, and when it can, it is attached to an unrelated promise with no decision_id

**backend/agent_core/treatment/enact.py:519** · data-model · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T08-enact-contract`

_promise_ref raises `NoExecutor("no_promise_to_attach_followup_to")` (enact.py:519) because followups CHECK requires promise_id XOR lead_id (05_collections.sql:260). For a bounce trigger it otherwise picks `SELECT id FROM promises WHERE customer_id = :cid ORDER BY promised_at DESC LIMIT 1` (503-513) — possibly a kept promise from months ago — and the INSERT at 470-495 carries no decision_id, so the agent's eventual call can only be attributed by time proximity (followthrough._reached_since, followthrough.py:300-335).

**Impact.** On a fresh bank book (no PTP history yet) every human_call plan is cancelled after the touch was booked; on a mature book the workspace shows an agent task under the wrong promise, and outcomes from any voice interaction in the window are credited to this decision.

**Fix.** Give followups a nullable decision_id and relax the CHECK to allow (decision_id IS NOT NULL) as a third anchor; or route engine-initiated human work through work_items with decision_id. Attribute human_call outcomes via the followup/interaction link, not the window.

### `followthrough-send-failed-never-matches-dead-jobs` — The 'undeliverable' label is unreachable: _send_failed looks for a whatsapp job status the sender never writes

**backend/agent_core/treatment/followthrough.py:352** · statistics · defect · unverified (verifier-added) · reader `T08-enact-contract`

_send_failed is the only producer of the 'undeliverable' outcome (followthrough.py:198-199) and its predicate is `AND status = 'failed'` (followthrough.py:352) over whatsapp_outbound_jobs. whatsapp_outbound.mark_failed_or_retry — the sole terminal-state writer — sets status to 'dead' in all three exit paths (whatsapp_outbound.py:311-321 ambiguous transport, :333-347 definite client error, :353-367 attempts exhausted) and back to 'queued' otherwise (:378-392); the three `'failed'` literals elsewhere in that module (whatsapp_outbound.py:471, 535, 591) all set messages.delivery_status, not the job status. The DDL confirms the two are distinct values of one enum: `CHECK (status IN ('queued','running','succeeded','failed','dead'))` (sql/12_crosscutting.sql:187-189). No code path writes 'failed' to whatsapp_outbound_jobs.status, so followthrough.py:352 can never match and the branch at :198-199 is dead. The decision instead falls through to `no_answer` after the grace window (followthrough.py:201-203).

**Impact.** A whole outcome class is unreachable and every WhatsApp that the provider or the gate refused is labelled no_answer. The distinction the docstring calls load-bearing — 'an undeliverable number is a data-quality problem for the ops team, whereas a no-answer is a treatment problem for the engine' (followthrough.py:340-343) — is lost, so the reach model is taught that borrowers on WhatsApp ignore messages that were never delivered, and the ladder escalates to voice for a data-quality reason. Directly amplifies the cooling-off blocker above, whose failures all land in 'dead'.

**Fix.** Change the predicate to `status IN ('dead','failed')` (keeping 'failed' for forward compatibility), and assert the two vocabularies agree in a test that enumerates the DDL's CHECK values against the statuses mark_failed_or_retry can write. Longer term, attribute through delivery_receipts.related_id / the job's decision id rather than by customer and source.

### `swallow-poisons-lent-transaction` — Swallowing an error on a lent connection aborts the caller's transaction — bounce ingest, not just the log row, is lost

**backend/agent_core/treatment/decisions.py:168** · reliability · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T09-followthrough-decisions`

168-170: 'except Exception: logger.exception(...); return None' with no SAVEPOINT when conn is provided (95: 'with _writer(conn) as active' just yields the caller's conn at 44-46). Same at 219-221, 303-304, 349-350. Docstring 17-19: 'bounce ingest holds FOR UPDATE on the account row while it decides' (payment_events.py:401, 443). In Postgres a failed statement leaves the transaction in an aborted state; every later statement raises InFailedSqlTransaction.

**Impact.** One CHECK/FK violation in the log (e.g. a new action name before the migration runs, a tenant row missing) turns into a failed bounce ingest with a misleading stack trace far from the cause. The memory note 'db_tx poisoning cascades' records this pattern already biting the test suite.

**Fix.** When conn is lent, execute inside 'with conn.begin_nested():' so the failure rolls back to the savepoint and the caller's transaction survives; keep the swallow-and-log.

### `claim-due-7d-window-orphans` — Plans scheduled more than 7 days after creation are never claimed and never labelled

**backend/agent_core/treatment/decisions.py:378** · reliability · hidden-assumption · 1/1 confirm · reader `T09-followthrough-decisions`

378: 'AND created_at >= now() - interval 7 days' in claim_due while scheduled_at may be later (legal cooling-off, self_service_plan). enact.py:45 'MAX_PLAN_AGE = timedelta(hours=12)' cancels only plans that were claimed.

**Impact.** Those rows sit with enacted=false, outcome NULL: invisible to the executor, re-examined by attribution every cycle, and counted as 'actionable' in insights coverage.

**Fix.** Claim on scheduled_at alone and let MAX_PLAN_AGE cancel; or write 'cancelled:expired' when a row ages out.

### `claim-by-id-skips-suppression-predicates` — claim_by_id lacks the suppression_reason/wait/scheduled_at predicates that claim_due enforces

**backend/agent_core/treatment/decisions.py:394** · compliance · hidden-assumption · 1/1 confirm · reader `T09-followthrough-decisions`

394-399: 'WHERE id = :id AND enacted IS FALSE AND mode <> simulated AND outcome IS NULL' vs claim_due 369-377 which adds 'suppression_reason IS NULL', 'chosen_action <> wait', 'scheduled_at <= now()'. clerk.py:166 uses claim_by_id then enact_one.

**Impact.** A decision the engine suppressed for a hold/consent/DND reason can be handed to the clerk and enacted early; whatever the downstream contact gate does not re-check (holds, consent class) is now enforced by nothing.

**Fix.** Mirror claim_due's predicates in claim_by_id (or make the clerk path an explicit human override with enacted_by='human' and an override reason column).

### `enact-gates-on-process-mode-not-decision-mode` — enact_one checks the process's TREATMENT_MODE, never the mode stamped on the decision, so a shadow-arm row is enactable on a live process

**backend/agent_core/treatment/enact.py:80** · correctness · defect · unverified (verifier-added) · reader `T09-followthrough-decisions`

enact.py:80-83 'if config.mode() != config.MODE_LIVE: return False, "not_live"' -- config.mode() reads the TREATMENT_MODE environment variable (config.py:57), not decision['mode']. engine.py:189 sets the decision's mode from 'force_mode or (arm.mode if arm and arm.mode else None) or config.mode()', and config.py:360 defines the builtin 'holdout' variant as Variant(name='holdout', mode=MODE_SHADOW). Such a row is written with mode='shadow' and suppression_reason='shadow_mode' (engine.py:340-343, :401) but with the real chosen_action (engine.py:387). decisions.claim_by_id (decisions.py:394-399) filters only 'mode <> simulated', so 'shadow' passes. The docstring at enact.py:5-8 states the opposite property: 'A shadow decision is never enacted, no matter how it got here.'

**Impact.** Every borrower randomised into a shadow-mode arm can be contacted through the clerk path while the process runs live. That both harms the untreated arm and destroys the only measurement that can establish incremental effect -- and it does so silently, because the row's own mode column will still read 'shadow' afterwards. Latent only because the configured split (control:80, null_treatment:20) contains no shadow-mode arm; it arms itself the first time anyone adds the holdout arm the rollout plan calls for.

**Fix.** Gate on the row: 'if str(decision.get("mode")) != config.MODE_LIVE or config.mode() != config.MODE_LIVE: return False, "not_live"'. Add the suppression_reason and chosen_action predicates to claim_by_id, and add a test that a decision row with mode='shadow' is refused by enact_one while TREATMENT_MODE=live.

### `cancelled-counted-as-treated-negative` — `cancelled` (plan never sent) is a RESOLVING label and is consumed as a treated non-cure by metrics and trainers

**backend/agent_core/treatment/followthrough.py:65** · statistics · hidden-assumption · 1/1 confirm · reader `T09-followthrough-decisions`

65: 'RESOLVING = frozenset({"paid", "ptp", "superseded", "cancelled"})'. enact.py:89-152 writes 'cancelled' for plan_expired, no_executor, unknown_action, customer_gone, contact-gate refusal, and handler exceptions — at claim time, with no observation window. Live DB: 84 of 108 labelled rows are 'cancelled'. metrics.py:74-77 counts 'variant <> :arm AND outcome IS NOT NULL AND chosen_action <> wait' as treated_n; train_treatment_models.py:192 '_label_timing: if outcome in {"unresolved", "cancelled"}: return 0' with the comment 'nothing was done and nothing happened' though nothing was observed; :208 _label_cure maps cancelled→0.

**Impact.** 78% of the labelled corpus is 'we did not do it', scored as 'we did it and it failed'. Treated cure rate is crushed, timing model learns that not acting yields no self-cure after zero days, and the scoreboard is a finding about the executor's coverage, not about collections.

**Fix.** Remove 'cancelled' from every cure/timing denominator (exclude in metrics.causal, ope.treatment_effect, _label_cure, _label_timing). Record the cancellation reason in its own column (enact already knows it) and let a cancelled plan be re-observed after OBSERVATION_WINDOW as an un-treated counterfactual only when the cancel reason was gate/policy, never when it was 'plan_expired'.

### `attribution-throughput-and-unlabelable-churn` — 25 rows per 1.5s tick, up to 7 round-trips each, and rows that can never be labelled cycle through the queue for 30 days

**backend/agent_core/treatment/followthrough.py:81** · scale · hidden-assumption · 1/1 confirm · reader `T09-followthrough-decisions`

81: 'BATCH = 25'; 138-142 per-row Python loop calling _superseded/_paid_since/_promised_since/_reached_since/_send_failed (7 queries worst case); bot_worker.py:170 '--poll ... default=1.5'. Un-enacted live 'wait' rows outside a withholding arm, shadow rows, and plans that missed claim_due's 7-day window (decisions.py:378) return None at 194 and are re-stamped (149-155) to the back of the queue, never leaving it.

**Impact.** At 100k sweep decisions/day the queue is dominated by unlabelable rows; labelable rows wait behind them; attribution latency grows to days and the 8h grace becomes meaningless. The test helper at test_treatment_followthrough.py:164-181 already hit this with 1,833 rows.

**Fix.** Set-based SQL attribution (one UPDATE ... FROM per label class), a terminal 'not_attributable' label for rows that structurally cannot label, a dedicated attribution worker, and BATCH sized by throughput.

### `multi-decision-shared-credit` — Overlapping decisions on one customer are all credited with the same payment/promise/connect — no exclusivity, no last-touch rule

**backend/agent_core/treatment/followthrough.py:174** · statistics · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T09-followthrough-decisions`

174-177: '_paid_since(conn, row, since)', '_promised_since(conn, row, since)' are evaluated per row with only 'posted_at > :since' / 'created_at > :since' — nothing excludes evidence already attributed to another decision. A control-arm dpd_tick 'wait' on Monday and a treated bounce 'whatsapp' on Tuesday both become 'paid' from one Wednesday payment.

**Impact.** Contamination across arms on the same borrower makes the difference-of-means in ope.treatment_effect meaningless; the uplift model's positive class double-counts, and 'expected value recovered' in the scoreboard sums the same rupee several times.

**Fix.** Attribute at case level, once per (customer, resolution event): pick the last enacted touch before the evidence (or the control row if no enacted touch in the window), mark others 'superseded_by' with a pointer. Store the evidence id (ledger_entries.id / promises.id / interactions.id) on the decision.

### `paid-label-any-payment` — `paid` is any ledger payment on the account or any paid intent on any of the customer's accounts — amount, source and reversal are ignored

**backend/agent_core/treatment/followthrough.py:264** · statistics · hidden-assumption · 1/1 confirm · reader `T09-followthrough-decisions`

263-264: 'SELECT 1 FROM ledger_entries WHERE account_id = :aid AND type = payment AND posted_at > :since'; 275-276: 'SELECT 1 FROM payment_intents WHERE customer_id = :cid AND status = paid AND paid_at > :since'. ledger_entries.type is CHECK IN (charge, payment, fee, adjustment, waiver) (02_customer_account.sql:117) — a reversed NACH credit is a later 'adjustment' the query never sees. No amount threshold, no link to enacted_ref or payment_intents.decision.

**Impact.** On a bank book most accounts have a standing NACH/e-mandate; a scheduled auto-debit success on the due date after a pre_due SMS is credited to the SMS. A ₹1 UPI test, a partial payment far below minimum due, or a payment that bounces two days later is a 'paid'. Cross-account: paying loan B labels the decision about loan A. The uplift and reach models learn the mandate calendar, not the treatment.

**Fix.** Define 'paid' against the case: bounce → payment_events.status = cured; pre_due → emi_installments paid; dpd_tick → outstanding/minimum_due reduced by >= minimum_due (or dpd back to 0). Require the payment to be on the decision's account. Exclude mandate auto-debits unless chosen_action = represent_mandate. Re-check for reversal at OBSERVATION_WINDOW and downgrade with a history row.

### `labeller-ignores-call-outcomes-ledger` — The attribution loop never reads call_attempts/call_outcomes -- the per-decision outcome ledger that already exists and is already populated

**backend/agent_core/treatment/followthrough.py:300** · data-model · missing-for-production · unverified (verifier-added) · reader `T09-followthrough-decisions`

sql/21_outbound.sql:20-29 defines call_attempts with 'decision_id TEXT REFERENCES treatment_decisions(id)' and sql/21_outbound.sql:78 indexes it; sql/21_outbound.sql:101-120 defines call_outcomes with 'connection TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (connection IN (no_answer, busy, rejected, failed, invalid_number, voicemail, wrong_party, ivr_only, connected, suppressed))' and 'business ... IN (..., refused, callback_requested, wrong_number, deceased, opt_out_requested, ...)'. call_closer.py:1003 writes those rows in production. Grep over agent_core/treatment finds call_attempts only at features.py:1099 (reach FEATURES) and call_outcomes nowhere at all. followthrough.py:300-334 instead derives 'reached' from a customer-scoped interactions/messages query, :337-359 derives 'undeliverable' from whatsapp_outbound_jobs only, and no path derives 'refused'.

**Impact.** The reach model's features come from call_attempts and its labels come from an unrelated customer-scoped activity query, so feature and label disagree about what an attempt was -- a label-definition defect a model-risk committee will reject. It is simultaneously the root cause of three separate confirmed findings (reached-not-linked-to-attempt, undeliverable-whatsapp-only, refused-never-produced), all of which are one JOIN on decision_id away from being correct.

**Fix.** Make call_outcomes (joined on decision_id, or attempt_id via call_attempts) the primary evidence for the contact-class label: connection IN (connected) -> reached; connection IN (no_answer, busy, voicemail, ivr_only) -> no_answer; connection IN (invalid_number, failed, rejected) or the equivalent SMS/WhatsApp provider status -> undeliverable; business IN (refused, opt_out_requested, wrong_number, deceased) -> refused. Keep the interactions query only as a fallback for channels with no attempt row, and add a test that a call_outcomes row with connection='invalid_number' produces 'undeliverable' rather than 'no_answer'.

### `reached-not-linked-to-attempt` — `reached` is any >=20s voice interaction or any inbound message for the customer — including opt-outs and unrelated calls

**backend/agent_core/treatment/followthrough.py:311** · statistics · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T09-followthrough-decisions`

311-316: 'SELECT 1 FROM interactions WHERE customer_id = :cid AND channel = voice AND started_at > :since AND COALESCE(duration_sec,0) >= :floor' — no direction, no decision/enacted_ref join; 326-328: 'm.sender = customer AND m.created_at > :since' — a 'STOP' message is a reach. outbound_attempts carries decision_id (migration 0094:202) and is not used.

**Impact.** An inbound customer-service call about a statement, a cadence dialler call, or a DND opt-out message labels the treatment as a connect. The reach model (README.md:252) learns the wrong hours and the ladder re-dials a borrower who just opted out.

**Fix.** Join reach evidence to the attempt: interactions/outbound_attempts by decision_id or enacted_ref; count inbound messages only if they are a reply within the channel and not an opt-out keyword; derive 'refused' from disposition/opt-out.

### `open-cases-head-of-line-block` — open_cases applies LIMIT in SQL then filters in Python; with limit=1 one closed case at the head stops all re-decision for 30 days

**backend/agent_core/treatment/followthrough.py:398** · reliability · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T09-followthrough-decisions`

389: 'LIMIT :limit' inside the query; 398: 'return [dict(r) for r in rows if _case_still_open(conn, dict(r))]'; 516: 'cases = open_cases(conn, limit=1)'. A case whose latest outcome is in UNRESOLVED but which _case_still_open rejects (every dpd_tick case per the previous finding; any cured bounce whose last enacted rung was labelled no_answer) is returned as the single row, rejected, and process_one returns False — and the same row is returned next tick because the ordering 'ORDER BY latest.enacted_at ASC NULLS LAST' is stable.

**Impact.** Re-decision is effectively dead on this deployment (dpd_tick dominates the corpus) and would deadlock on any real book within hours. This is the same class of bug the attribution watermark (118-127) was added to fix, reintroduced one function down.

**Fix.** Push openness into SQL (LEFT JOIN payment_events / promises / emi_installments and filter on status) so LIMIT applies to genuinely open cases, or over-fetch and stamp rejected cases with a terminal outcome ('superseded'/'closed') so they leave the queue. Add a test with a closed case ahead of an open one.

### `dpd-tick-case-never-open` — _case_still_open returns False for dpd_tick, so the sweep's ladder — the docstring's headline feature — never advances

**backend/agent_core/treatment/followthrough.py:421** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T09-followthrough-decisions`

LOOPED_TRIGGERS at 60-62 includes 'dpd_tick' and the comment at 48-54 says leaving it out 'gave the largest population in the book exactly one decision a day and no escalation at all'. But 401-421 handles bounce, broken_ptp, pre_due and ends 'return False'. Every dpd_tick case is filtered out at 398.

**Impact.** The silent roller — the biggest segment in any NBFC book — still gets one decision per day and no within-day escalation. The docstring promises a behaviour the code does not deliver, which a model-risk reviewer will treat as an undocumented control.

**Fix.** Define openness for dpd_tick: the account is still delinquent (accounts.dpd > 0 / bucket) and the borrower's local date == trigger_ref. Add a test that a dpd_tick case with a no_answer last rung appears in open_cases.

### `attribution-starves-redecision` — process_one returns as soon as attribution labels one row, so the ladder only advances when the attribution queue is completely dry

**backend/agent_core/treatment/followthrough.py:514** · reliability · defect · unverified (verifier-added) · reader `T09-followthrough-decisions`

followthrough.py:513-518: 'with engine.begin() as conn: if attribute_outcomes(conn): return True; cases = open_cases(conn, limit=1)'. attribute_outcomes returns the count labelled (followthrough.py:156), so a single labelled row in a batch of 25 short-circuits the tick before open_cases is ever called. bot_worker.py:217-233 sleeps only when process_one_any() returns False, so on a book with any steady label flow the re-decision branch is unreachable.

**Impact.** On a 50k-2M account book the daily sweep produces a continuous stream of labellable rows, so followthrough degrades to an attribution-only worker and the escalation ladder -- the feature the module docstring leads with (followthrough.py:22-27) -- never runs. Combined with the confirmed LIMIT-before-filter head-of-line block, re-decision is doubly disabled and nothing reports it: the worker keeps logging 'processed=True' the whole time.

**Fix.** Do both halves in one tick, or alternate them (a counter or a per-queue budget), and split attribution into its own worker with its own poll. Emit a metric for re-decisions per hour and alert when it is zero while open_cases is non-empty.

### `outcome-superseded-counts-a-cure-as-a-treated-failure` — 'superseded' means two different things, and the one that means 'the borrower paid' is counted as a treated non-cure

**backend/agent_core/treatment/enact.py:113** · correctness · defect · unverified (verifier-added) · reader `T10-sweep-timing-monitor-metrics`

enact.py:111-115 `# Still worth doing? A borrower who paid between planning and sending must not be dunned for it.` / `if _resolved_since(conn, decision): decisions.record_outcome(decision_id, "superseded", conn=conn); return False, "already_resolved"`. enact.py:178-192 defines that as the bounce being 'cured'/'suppressed' or the promise being 'kept'/'partial' — i.e. the borrower resolved. followthrough.py:225-231 writes the SAME label for a completely different situation: 'A newer decision exists for the same case.' Both then meet metrics.py:72 and :80 `outcome IN ('paid','ptp')` and monitor.py:64 `CURED = frozenset({"paid", "ptp"})` — 'superseded' is in neither, so it is counted in the denominator (outcome IS NOT NULL) and not in the numerator. Separately, enact.py:186 and :191 return True when `status is None`, so a decision whose trigger row has been deleted is also recorded as 'superseded'.

**Impact.** Every borrower who cures between the plan and the send is booked as a treated failure, biasing the treated cure rate downward — against the engine — in the one number the scoreboard exists to produce. Because the control arm is never enacted it can never receive this label, so the bias is one-sided across the two arms. One outcome value carrying two incompatible meanings also makes the corpus untrainable on that label: a trainer cannot tell 'they paid' from 'a later rung replaced this row'.

**Fix.** Split the label: keep 'superseded' for followthrough's newer-decision case and introduce 'resolved_before_send' (or reuse 'paid' when _resolved_since saw a cure) for enact.py:113. Add whichever value means a cure to CURED in metrics.py and monitor.py. Make _resolved_since distinguish a missing trigger row from a resolved one rather than treating `status is None` as resolved.

### `metrics-no-confidence-intervals` — Incremental cure rate, attributable rupees and recovery-per-rupee are point estimates with no interval

**backend/agent_core/treatment/metrics.py:110** · statistics · missing-for-production · 1/1 confirm · reader `T10-sweep-timing-monitor-metrics`

metrics.py:108-110 `incremental = treated_rate - control_rate`; :168 `attributable = recovered * (incremental / treated_rate)`; :180-182 `round(attributable / spent, 2)`; the only guard is MIN_ARM_N (:46-50).

**Impact.** A bank's model-risk committee cannot accept a lift figure without an interval; the ratio of two noisy rates multiplied by a rupee total will swing weekly and be read as trend. Negative incremental yields negative 'attributable' rupees with no explanation.

**Fix.** Wald or bootstrap CI (clustered by customer) on the rate difference; propagate to attributable rupees; show 'not distinguishable from zero' explicitly; keep MIN_ARM_N as a floor, not as the inference.

### `metrics-recovered-attribution-over-broad` — Recovered rupees count every payment on every account of any customer with an earlier enacted decision, and attributable share assumes rupee share equals cure-rate share

**backend/agent_core/treatment/metrics.py:132** · statistics · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T10-sweep-timing-monitor-metrics`

metrics.py:122-144 joins ledger_entries to accounts and requires EXISTS a non-control enacted decision for `a.customer_id` with `d.created_at <= le.posted_at` in the window; not restricted to the delinquent account, the case, or the arrears amount. :168 `attributable = recovered * (incremental / treated_rate)`.

**Impact.** Regular EMIs on the borrower's current loans and payments unrelated to the case are booked as recovery; a customer with one WhatsApp nudge in week 1 has all of week 4's payments counted. The attributable formula ignores amount heterogeneity (large-ticket self-curers vs small incremental cures).

**Fix.** Attribute at the case level: payments on the decision's account_id against the overdue instalment(s), within the case window; compare treated vs control rupees per customer directly rather than scaling by a rate ratio.

### `metrics-unbounded-json-scans-under-15s-api-timeout` — The spend query expands candidates JSON for every enacted decision in the window and the money query runs a correlated EXISTS per ledger row, on the 15s API path

**backend/agent_core/treatment/metrics.py:151** · scale · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T10-sweep-timing-monitor-metrics`

metrics.py:149-157 `CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(d.candidates)` over all decisions in the window; :132-140 `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM treatment_decisions d WHERE d.customer_id = a.customer_id ... AND d.created_at <= le.posted_at)` per payment. db_core.py:154 API statement timeout 15s; monitor.py:119-122 records that a similar scan timed out at 18k rows.

**Impact.** At 400k decisions/day x 28 days the endpoint cannot return; the section 17 scoreboard is unavailable exactly when the book is real.

**Fix.** Store chosen cost as a column at decision time; maintain a nightly rollup table (per tenant, day, arm: decisions, enacted, cured, spend, recovered) and serve the scoreboard from it; keep the raw queries for a batch job.

### `metrics-complaint-intake-missing` — No conduct-complaint source exists; the section 17 complaint rate cannot be produced

**backend/agent_core/treatment/metrics.py:317** · compliance · missing-for-production · 1/1 confirm · reader `T10-sweep-timing-monitor-metrics`

metrics.py:306-324 'disputes.type carries billing disputes only ... Needs a complaint intake before this can be a number.'

**Impact.** RBI's fair-practice and Internal Ombudsman regime requires recovery-conduct complaints to be tracked against the recovery activity; a decision engine that cannot see complaints cannot price harassment, and the fatigue term in scoring is uncalibrated.

**Fix.** A complaints table (source: IO/grievance portal, call disposition 'complaint', inbound message classifier) keyed to customer and, where possible, decision_id; feed complaint rate per 1,000 contacts into metrics.compliance and as a cost into scoring.

### `metrics-breach-audit-uses-env-and-constants-not-rules-in-force` — Breach audit checks the RBI constants and the env daily cap, not the versioned policy_rules in force at occurred_at, and only voice outreach

**backend/agent_core/treatment/metrics.py:364** · compliance · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T10-sweep-timing-monitor-metrics`

metrics.py:343 imports RBI_VOICE_END/START and daily_cap; :364 binds `RBI_VOICE_START`/`RBI_VOICE_END`; :367 `cap = daily_cap()` with no rules -> contact_policy.py:99 env CONTACT_DAILY_CAP default 3; :354 `AND ce.channel = 'voice'`; :379-381 `purpose = 'outreach'`. sql/03_consent.sql:87-90 introduced versioned rules precisely to answer 'why did you, last March'. Field visits, sms/whatsapp windows and the 2027 prior-intimation requirement are not audited.

**Impact.** A tenant that published cap=2 or a 09:00-18:00 window has breaches the audit reports as zero; a regulator's 'show me your breach log for Q3 under the rules then in force' cannot be answered from this number; 4am WhatsApp dunning (see timing-digital-at-any-hour) is never counted.

**Fix.** Join policy_rules effective at ce.occurred_at (per tenant) for the window and cap; audit all outbound channels; add a field-visit intimation check (a 'statutory' intimation contact_event >= 24h before the visit) and a recording-retention check.

### `monitor-shadow-rows-pooled-with-live-in-causal-numbers` — Shadow decisions, which can only ever be labelled paid/ptp/superseded, are pooled with live rows in the treated arm

**backend/agent_core/treatment/metrics.py:508** · statistics · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T10-sweep-timing-monitor-metrics`

metrics.py:508 and monitor.py:503 `modes = ["shadow", "live"] + ...`; followthrough.py:20 'Those can only ever be labelled paid / ptp / superseded — never no_answer' and followthrough.py:183-201 returns None for an unenacted non-withheld row. The established corpus is 201 live + 24 shadow.

**Impact.** During the prescribed shadow fortnight and any later shadow variant, the treated arm contains rows that are positive-only by construction, inflating treatedCureRate and incrementalCureRate; the scoreboard shows the engine 'working' before it has done anything.

**Fix.** Causal and uplift-calibration numbers on mode='live' only (or per mode, never pooled); shadow rows are for coverage/insights, not for effect estimation.

### `monitor-metrics-no-tenant-scope-and-rls-bypassed` — Every monitor and metrics query is unscoped by tenant, and the app connects as a role that bypasses RLS

**backend/agent_core/treatment/monitor.py:140** · security · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T10-sweep-timing-monitor-metrics`

monitor.py:129-144 and :179-192 filter on mode/created_at only; metrics.py:66-88, 122-160, 197-236, 266-295, 345-390, 419-439, 461-479 likewise have no tenant_id predicate (contact_events, ledger_entries, interactions, capacity_duals all carry tenant_id or reach it via customers). agent_core/connectors/first_party.py:25-26 'RLS is opt-in and the app connects as BYPASSRLS'; rls.py:18-20 confirms.

**Impact.** In any multi-tenant deployment (bank + NBFC arm, co-lending partner) one tenant's calibration, drift, breach counts and recovery rupees are pooled into another's dashboard, a data-segregation finding for the DPO and a wrong number for every tenant.

**Fix.** Add `tenant_id = :tenant` (db.current_tenant()) to every query in both modules and a test that the reports for two seeded tenants differ.

### `monitor-drift-blind-to-missingness-shape-and-categoricals` — Drift is a mean shift over non-null values only; fill-rate collapse, variance change and categorical mix are invisible

**backend/agent_core/treatment/monitor.py:240** · statistics · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T10-sweep-timing-monitor-metrics`

monitor.py:239-241 `if value is None: continue`; :251-252 `if n < 30: continue`; :264 `shift = (recent - trained) / sigma`. The docstring (:6-9) promises to catch 'the mix of buckets shifts' and 'a phone number ... dead by August'.

**Impact.** The two most common production failures, an upstream feed going dark (mandate status, phone, next_credit_at all becoming None) and a portfolio mix change (bucket/product/segment), produce no alert: nulls are skipped and categorical features are not in the numeric vector. The model keeps scoring on imputed training means (models.py:175-179) with a green drift panel.

**Fix.** Per-feature fill rate vs training fill rate (needs fill rates in the artifact), PSI on 10 quantile bins for numerics, PSI on category shares for bucket/product/channel/segment key, and an alert when n for any feature falls below the training-era expectation.

### `monitor-reach-labels-drop-paid-and-pool-channels` — Reach calibration loses reached-then-paid rows and pools voice 'connect' with WhatsApp 'reply' against a pReach that means read/delivered

**backend/agent_core/treatment/monitor.py:364** · statistics · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T10-sweep-timing-monitor-metrics`

monitor.py:361-369 keeps only outcomes in REACHED={reached,ptp,refused} or NOT_REACHED={no_answer,undeliverable}; followthrough.py:172-177 labels paid before reached, so an answered call followed by payment is 'paid' and excluded (`else: continue` at :368-369). For WhatsApp, pReach is derived from read/delivered receipts (features.py:1019-1025) while 'reached' requires an inbound message (followthrough.py:323-332).

**Impact.** Observed reach is biased downward exactly in the top prediction bins (borrowers who answer and pay), so the monitor reports optimism the model does not have; and channels with different reach definitions share one ECE, so a well-calibrated voice model plus a WhatsApp read-rate model averages to an alert. Either way the EV formula is 'fixed' in the wrong direction.

**Fix.** Label reach from call_attempts (answered) and message receipts (read/delivered) directly rather than from the outcome column, keep the reach label independent of the cure label, and report reliability per channel.

### `monitor-uplift-check-populations-mismatch-and-cancelled-as-treated` — Predicted mean tau is averaged over every non-control row (including waits, cancelled and unlabelled) while the measured ATE counts cancelled rows as treated failures

**backend/agent_core/treatment/monitor.py:424** · statistics · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T10-sweep-timing-monitor-metrics`

monitor.py:414-437: `predicted` collects p_resolve for every row with arm != control regardless of chosen_action or outcome; `treated_n` counts `outcome` non-empty and `chosen_action not in ('', 'wait')`, which includes outcome='cancelled' rows written by enact.py:89-152 when nothing was sent (no executor, contact denied, plan expired). Per the established facts 84 of the 108 labelled rows today are 'cancelled'.

**Impact.** measuredAte is dragged toward zero by rows where no treatment occurred, so the gap `mean_tau - measured` is large and the report accuses the model of being 'a response model wearing an uplift label' (:453-458) whether or not it is. A bank's model-risk reviewer acting on this would block a working model or, once the alert is known to be noise, ignore a real one.

**Fix.** Compute both sides on the same rows: labelled, enacted (or intent-to-treat by arm, stated explicitly), excluding cancelled/superseded; report treated_n after exclusion and the exclusion counts.

### `monitor-fitted-flag-from-file-presence-not-serving-scorer` — fitted=uplift is not None labels the EV prior as tau whenever the uplift file loads, even though TREATMENT_SCORER=ev is serving

**backend/agent_core/treatment/monitor.py:524** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T10-sweep-timing-monitor-metrics`

monitor.py:524 `uplift_calibration(rows, fitted=uplift is not None)`; models.load_uplift (models.py:628-653) returns the artifact whenever the file parses, is not stale, is allowed (TREATMENT_ALLOW_SIMULATED_MODELS) and control_n >= 500 (3668 here). Established fact: the hand-tuned EVScorer serves; the fitted uplift model does not.

**Impact.** The report says quantity='tau', fittedUplift=true and uses the 'response model wearing an uplift label' note for a number that is P(resolve|reach) from priors, misleading the reviewer about which model is under test.

**Fix.** Derive `fitted` from the rows themselves (recommender/recommender_version columns on treatment_decisions) or from config.scorer(), not from file presence; report both per recommender_version.

### `sweep-perpetual-rescan-no-day-completion` — After the tail the sweep restarts at the top of the book the same day and re-walks it forever

**backend/agent_core/treatment/sweep.py:99** · scale · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T10-sweep-timing-monitor-metrics`

sweep.py:99-101 `if cursor: _write_cursor(conn, tenant, "")` then `return False`; the next worker iteration (bot_worker.py:138, poll 1.5s) reads an empty cursor and claims the first 50 delinquent accounts again. Each account then pays a row lock and a `_decided_today` SELECT (sweep.py:195-208) and returns False. Nothing records 'sweep complete for <local day>'.

**Impact.** On 400k delinquent accounts (a 2M book at 20% delinquency) an idle pass is 8,000 transactions of 50 row locks and 50 SELECTs, repeated all day on the shared bot_worker, contending with payment posting on the same account rows (see next finding) and burning the DB for zero decisions.

**Fix.** Persist {afterAccountId, completedLocalDay} in the cursor payload; when completedLocalDay == today for the tenant's default zone (or per-borrower: add `NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM treatment_decisions ... trigger_ref = <today>)` to the claim predicate) return False without claiming. Alternatively schedule the sweep once per day per tenant from a scheduler rather than polling.

### `sweep-batch-fatal-error-livelocks-the-cursor` — Any failure outside the per-account savepoint discards the whole batch AND leaves the cursor unmoved, so the sweep retries the same fifty accounts forever

**backend/agent_core/treatment/sweep.py:106** · reliability · defect · unverified (verifier-added) · reader `T10-sweep-timing-monitor-metrics`

sweep.py:87-106 runs the entire batch inside one `with engine.begin() as conn:` and writes the cursor last: `for account in accounts: if _decide_account(conn, account): decided += 1` then `_write_cursor(conn, tenant, accounts[-1]["id"])`. The savepoint at sweep.py:175-191 covers only the `recommend_treatment` call. Three things sit outside it: `_decided_today` (sweep.py:172, a SELECT that can hit the 60s worker statement timeout under the lock contention this same module creates), `savepoint.commit()` (sweep.py:191), and `_write_cursor` (sweep.py:106). Any of them raising aborts the transaction, rolls back every decision already made in the batch, and leaves the cursor at its previous value. bot_worker._run_stage swallows the exception (bot_worker.py:216-219 `logger.exception("process_one crashed — backing off")`) and the loop immediately re-enters at the same cursor. Nothing counts consecutive failures and nothing alerts.

**Impact.** One poisoned account — a customer row that trips a constraint, a statement timeout on a contended slice — permanently pins the sweep at that offset. The book past it is never swept again, the 'one decision per account per day' contract silently stops holding for the majority of the book, and the only symptom is repeated exception lines in a worker log. On a 2M-account deployment this is a total loss of corpus generation presenting as a healthy, running worker.

**Fix.** Advance the cursor before deciding, or commit the claim in its own short transaction and run each decision separately; move `_decided_today` inside the savepoint; count consecutive zero-progress passes on the same cursor value and emit an alert (and skip past the offending id) after a threshold.

### `sweep-dpd-never-rolled` — The sweep's delinquency predicate depends on accounts.dpd, which nothing in the platform ages

**backend/agent_core/treatment/sweep.py:152** · integration · hidden-assumption · 1/1 confirm · reader `T10-sweep-timing-monitor-metrics`

sweep.py:152 `AND a.dpd > 0`. The only writer of accounts.dpd is payment_events.py:287-290 `SET dpd = GREATEST(dpd, 1)` on a bounce; seed_postgres.py:729 sets a synthetic dpd. There is no nightly roll from emi_installments, so an account never rolls 30 -> 60 -> 90 unless the bank's CBS feed rewrites dpd daily, which is exactly the silent-roll the module exists to catch (sweep.py:3-7).

**Impact.** On a bank that only sends bounce events, every delinquent account sits at dpd=1 (or the seeded value) forever: bucket features, the bucket-band segments (segments.py:105-109), urgency and the legal-notice timing are all computed on a stale number, and accounts that cured by direct payment stay 'delinquent' and keep being swept.

**Fix.** Define the DPD source of truth explicitly: either a nightly roll computed from emi_installments.due_date/paid_on inside the platform, or a documented CBS ingestion contract with a freshness monitor (max(accounts.updated_at) where dpd > 0 must be within 24h) that fails the sweep loudly when stale.

### `sweep-row-locks-block-payment-posting` — FOR UPDATE on accounts holds 50 row locks for the whole batch while payments and bounces try to UPDATE the same rows

**backend/agent_core/treatment/sweep.py:156** · reliability · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T10-sweep-timing-monitor-metrics`

sweep.py:156 `FOR UPDATE OF a SKIP LOCKED` inside `engine.begin()` (sweep.py:88) that also runs 50 x recommend_treatment (features.py has 25 conn.execute call sites; policy.py 4 more) before commit at :106. payments.py:186-188 `UPDATE accounts SET outstanding = ...` and payment_events.py:287-290 `UPDATE accounts SET dpd = GREATEST(dpd, 1)` take the same row lock and block until the sweep batch commits. Worker statement timeout is 60s (db_core.py:154).

**Impact.** A UPI/NACH payment webhook or a bounce ingestion for any of the 50 accounts in flight stalls for the batch duration (seconds to a minute); at 8,000 batches per pass the book is effectively always partly locked. Payment posting latency and bounce ingestion timeouts show up as integration failures in the bank's CBS reconciliation.

**Fix.** Do not lock accounts. Claim by (tenant, local_day, account_id) rows in a lightweight sweep_claims table with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (or pg_try_advisory_xact_lock on hashtext(account_id)) and commit the claim before building features; run each decision in its own short transaction.

### `sweep-decided-today-keyed-on-customer-not-account` — Sweep decides one account per borrower per day, not one per account

**backend/agent_core/treatment/sweep.py:172** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T10-sweep-timing-monitor-metrics`

sweep.py:172 `if _decided_today(conn, account["customer_id"], local_day): return False` and sweep.py:195-208 filter only `customer_id = :cid AND trigger_kind = :kind AND trigger_ref = :ref`. The _claim docstring at :140-142 promises 'two accounts of one borrower are two decisions'. The trigger_ref (the date) carries no account, so the ladder case key (customer, dpd_tick, date) cannot distinguish loans either.

**Impact.** NBFC and bank books routinely carry 2-4 loans per borrower (personal + two-wheeler + consumer durable). The second and later delinquent accounts are never swept; their exposure, mandate and bounce state never reach the engine, and the corpus under-represents multi-loan borrowers, who are the highest-exposure segment.

**Fix.** Include account_id in the decided-today predicate (or encode account in trigger_ref, e.g. '<date>:<account_id>') and add a partial unique index on (customer_id, account_id, trigger_kind, trigger_ref) WHERE trigger_kind='dpd_tick' AND rung=0 as the DB-level guard. Decide whether the ladder should be per account or per household and say so in the design.

### `sweep-corpus-volume-no-retention` — One 4-8KB decision row per delinquent account per day with no retention, partitioning or purge

**backend/agent_core/treatment/sweep.py:177** · data-model · missing-for-production · 1/1 confirm · reader `T10-sweep-timing-monitor-metrics`

sweep.py:177-183 writes a full recommend_treatment row per account per day; monitor.py:116-117 measures `candidates` at 'four to eight kilobytes'; features vectors are added when TREATMENT_LOG_VECTORS is on (engine.py:575-582). No purge, retention or DELETE FROM treatment_decisions exists anywhere under agent_core/treatment (grep 'retention|purge|DELETE FROM treatment_decisions' -> none). treatment_decisions is not partitioned (sql/05_collections.sql:310-384).

**Impact.** 400k rows/day x ~6KB = 2.4GB/day, ~70GB/month, 11M rows/month of borrower features (dpd, outstanding, mandate state, promise history, reachability hours) held indefinitely. DPDP Act storage-limitation and purpose-limitation obligations are unmet, backups balloon, and every ORDER BY created_at query in monitor/metrics degrades monthly.

**Fix.** Range-partition treatment_decisions by created_at (monthly), define a retention policy (e.g. 18 months for labelled rows, 90 days for unlabelled 'wait' rows), drop candidates/features JSON after the label is attached and the trainer has consumed the row, keep vectors for a sampled fraction, and record the retention rule in the DPDP data inventory.

### `timing-plans-against-constants-not-published-rules` — timing.py plans against the RBI module constants while the gate enforces the tenant's versioned policy_rules; a narrower published window silently removes voice at the edges

**backend/agent_core/treatment/timing.py:88** · compliance · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T10-sweep-timing-monitor-metrics`

timing.py:33 `from contact_policy import RBI_VOICE_END, RBI_VOICE_START` and :88 `start, end = RBI_VOICE_START, RBI_VOICE_END`. contact_policy.py:494-496 `window = rules.calling_window(channel) if rules is not None else None; if window is None and channel == "voice": window = (RBI_VOICE_START, RBI_VOICE_END)` and policy_rules.py:118-126 defines per-channel calling windows as versioned data. engine.py:526-537 vetoes at the planned instant and excludes the action rather than re-planning.

**Impact.** A bank that publishes 09:00-18:00 (state directive, client policy, or the 2027 directions if they change) sees timing plan 08:00 dials, the gate deny them, and the engine drop voice for every borrower whose first feasible instant falls in the gap, with 'excluded: veto' in the log and no re-plan. For digital channels the same happens for any published sms/whatsapp window because timing assumes (0,24).

**Fix.** Have _window_for take the resolved rule set (policy_rules.resolve(conn, tenant_id, at)) and use rules.calling_window(channel) with the constants only as the fallback the gate uses; or re-plan once from the veto's REASON_HOURS with the gate's window.

### `timing-salary-credit-only-from-bounce-webhook` — Salary-credit timing depends entirely on a nextCreditAt field in the bounce webhook that most core banking bounce feeds do not carry

**backend/agent_core/treatment/timing.py:194** · integration · hidden-assumption · 1/1 confirm · reader `T10-sweep-timing-monitor-metrics`

timing.py:194 `credit = features.next_credit_at`; features.py:731-764 reads it from payment_events.next_credit_at; the only writer is payment_events.py:93/329 `_pick(body, "nextCreditAt", "next_credit_at")` from the inbound bounce payload. There is no inference from ledger credit history, salary_credit_day (features.py:211) or a CBS statement feed. The whole `open_bounce_id` condition (:200) also means the sweep's dpd_tick decisions never salary-time unless a bounce is open.

**Impact.** 'The single highest-yield timing decision in the early buckets' (:190-192) is inert in any deployment whose bounce feed lacks a salary hint, i.e. most banks; the engine silently degrades to calendar timing while the design note and the model card claim credit-timed retries.

**Fix.** Derive next_credit_at from observed salary credits (CBS account-statement feed or the borrower's declared salary day) with a confidence flag, expose 'hasNextCreditHint' fill-rate in monitor, and let dpd_tick decisions use it without an open bounce.

### `sweep-throughput-single-shared-worker` — The docstring's 'two million accounts ... finishes daily' is not achievable in the shipped wiring

**backend/bot_worker.py:138** · scale · hidden-assumption · 1/1 confirm · reader `T10-sweep-timing-monitor-metrics`

bot_worker.py:138 runs the sweep as one stage of a single poll loop that also serves WhatsApp turns, outbound, cadence and campaigns; sweep.py:64 BATCH=50 per iteration; each decision costs >=25 feature queries (features.py) + policy vetoes + the candidates INSERT, sequentially on one connection.

**Impact.** At an optimistic 100-200 ms per decision, 400k delinquent accounts need 11-22 worker-hours per day; the shared worker cannot finish a daily sweep, so the 'one decision per account per day' contract that the ladder, control arm and uplift trainer depend on is silently violated on any real book.

**Fix.** A dedicated sweep worker pool, partitioned by hashtext(account_id) % N so workers do not share a cursor frontier; set-based feature building (one query per batch per feature family) instead of 25 per account; measure decisions/second in the log line at sweep.py:109 and alert when projected completion exceeds 24h.

### `cards-outbound-eval-not-required-by-default` — The outbound eval suite is never required by a default card, so G-OB9 skips for every dialling agent unless the author opts in

**backend/agent_core/cards/schema.py:169** · testing · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T11-llm-touchpoints`

`require: list[EvalRequire] = Field(default_factory=lambda: ["regression", "redteam"])` — 'outbound' is a member of EvalRequire (schema.py:21) but not of the default. compile.py:453-465: 'the suite not being required skips', and G-OB9 delegates to `_eval_gate("G-OB9", "outbound", outbound_eval_gate_enabled(), eval_report, card)`.

**Impact.** This is the same defect the module docstring at schema.py:29-40 congratulates itself on having fixed for rollback triggers: a safety mechanism that exists in code but that no published card can actually request. An outbound collections dialler ships having passed only the inbound regression and redteam suites. The outbound failure mode — cadence, voicemail disclosure, opt-out honouring, abandon rate — is the one that is never exercised.

**Fix.** Derive the required suites from the card rather than from a static default: if outbound.dials, 'outbound' is required and cannot be removed, exactly as tools.locked cannot be unbound. Add a test in the family of test_rollback_trigger_vocabulary_is_shared asserting that a dialling card whose eval.require omits 'outbound' fails to compile.

### `cards-stop-on-is-unvalidated-free-text` — stop_on and retry_on are unvalidated list[str]; a typo means the dialler never stops on an opt-out

**backend/agent_core/cards/schema.py:278** · compliance · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T11-llm-touchpoints`

`stop_on: list[str] = Field(default_factory=lambda: ["ptp_captured", ..., "opt_out_requested", "wrong_number", "deceased"])` and `retry_on: list[str]` (269-288) — plain strings, no Literal, no validator. cadence.py:217 does `if business and business in set(cadence.stop_on)`. compile.py:394 validates `post_call.on_outcome[].when` against OUTCOME_CODES but no gate touches stop_on or retry_on. The schema applies exactly the opposite reasoning to Objective at schema.py:188-189 — 'this restates it as a Literal so a card with a typo fails at parse rather than at dial time'.

**Impact.** A card authored with "opt_out" instead of "opt_out_requested" publishes cleanly, and the cadence then keeps redialling a borrower who asked on the call not to be contacted. Under the RBI recovery-agent directions and DPDP that is the single most expensive contact the bank can make. The consent/DND layer is a genuine second line of defence — if the outcome also wrote a DND record, contact_policy would veto the next attempt — but the card's own stated stop condition would be silently inert, and nothing tells the author. The same typo in retry_on quietly stops a legitimate ladder instead.

**Fix.** Make both fields Literals over the Closer's taxonomy, exactly as Objective is, so a typo fails at parse. Failing that, add a compile gate alongside G-OB6 validating stop_on against OUTCOME_CODES and retry_on against the connection-state vocabulary. Add a test that a card whose stop_on omits opt_out_requested cannot publish.

### `cards-full-ship-needs-no-rollback` — The canary gate is inverted with respect to risk: 100% traffic with no auto-rollback is the default and passes unconditionally

**backend/agent_core/cards/schema.py:364** · reliability · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T11-llm-touchpoints`

`traffic_pct: int = Field(default=100, ...)`, `shadow: bool = False`, `auto_rollback: list[RollbackTrigger] = Field(default_factory=list)` (schema.py:364-366). compile.py:880-895: `if pct == 100: gates.append(_gate("G12", "canary", "pass", "full ship"))` — no trigger check — while `elif 0 < pct < 100` without valid triggers fails with 'canary split requires auto_rollback'.

**Impact.** The schema comment at lines 22-28 makes the case itself: 'An outbound bug rings ten thousand phones, and by the time a latency percentile has moved, the calls have been made.' Yet the default card ships to 100% of traffic with no automatic rollback, and the gate only demands rollback triggers from the author who was already being careful. In a bank, the release that most needs a kill switch is the one that goes everywhere.

**Fix.** Require at least one auto_rollback trigger for any published card whose outbound.dials is true, whatever traffic_pct is — and require the outbound-specific triggers (abandon_rate, third_party_leak, optout_spike) rather than only the latency ones. Change the schema default to a canary (traffic_pct well below 100 with triggers), so the safe path is the one you get by not thinking about it.

### `narrate-shadow-decision-reads-as-live` — Shadow decisions get a rationale describing an action that never happened, contradicting reasonText on the same row

**backend/agent_core/treatment/engine.py:352** · observability · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T11-llm-touchpoints`

engine.py:340 computes `suppressed = verdict.suppressed or mode == config.MODE_SHADOW` and engine.py:341-343 computes `reason = verdict.reason or (arbitration.SUPPRESS_SHADOW if mode == config.MODE_SHADOW else None)` — then engine.py:352-354 passes `suppressed=verdict.suppressed, reason=verdict.reason`, the un-adjusted pair. narrate.py:122 therefore takes the action branch and emits "...Send SMS at 10:30: 62% chance of reaching them...". Meanwhile engine.py:144 renders `reasonText` from the ADJUSTED reason as 'shadow mode — decided, not enacted'. narrate.py:46 defines a shadow_mode phrase that rationale() can never reach.

**Impact.** 24 shadow rows are already in the corpus. The rationale column is described by its own module as the audit artefact and the thing 'in front of whoever has to defend the contact later' (narrate.py:3-5). For a quarter of the corpus it asserts a contact that did not occur, and the same API payload contradicts itself between `rationale` and `reasonText`. When shadow mode is used the way it is meant to be — to run a new policy alongside a live one — this makes the decision log actively misleading about which borrowers were touched.

**Fix.** Pass the adjusted `suppressed` and `reason` into narrate.rationale, so a shadow row reads 'EMI bounced 3h ago, 20 DPD, ₹18,400 at stake. Holding — shadow mode — decided, not enacted.'
