Better still, give narrate an explicit `mode` parameter and render 'Would send SMS at 10:30' for shadow, so the counterfactual is preserved without claiming it happened. Add a test asserting a shadow decision's rationale does not contain an imperative verb.

### `rerank-no-model-version-on-the-decision` — The wrapper reports the base scorer's version, so the decision log cannot say which LLM ranked the action

**backend/agent_core/treatment/rerank.py:56** · compliance · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T11-llm-touchpoints`

`self.version = getattr(base, "version", "1.0.0")`. engine.py:368-369 records `recommender=scorer.name` (which does become `llm_rerank(ev)`) and `recommender_version=scorer.version` — the EV scorer's version. Nothing captures the Azure deployment name, the API version, the prompt text or a prompt hash. azure_openai.py:180-182 resolves the deployment from AZURE_OPENAI_CHAT_DEPLOYMENT at call time, and a deployment alias can be repointed at a new base model with no code change and no version bump.

**Impact.** RBI model-governance and any SR 11-7-style internal model risk function require that a decision be attributable to a model version. Here, an Azure-side model upgrade changes the ranking behaviour of a live collections policy with zero trace in the decision log and no change to recommender_version. When a borrower complains about a contact pattern in March, the bank cannot reconstruct which model produced it. It also makes A/B or before/after analysis of a model upgrade impossible.

**Fix.** Record on each decision row: deployment name, api_version, a sha256 of the exact prompt template, temperature, and the reranker's own semantic version — and make `LLMReranker.version` a composite of the base version and the reranker version, never the base's alone. Pin the deployment to an explicit model+version rather than an alias, and treat an unexpected model id in the response as a rerank failure.

### `rerank-does-not-scale-past-a-dev-book` — One synchronous LLM round trip per decision, with no batching, caching or budget — invisible on 20 customers, impossible on a real book

**backend/agent_core/treatment/rerank.py:68** · scale · hidden-assumption · 1/1 confirm · reader `T11-llm-touchpoints`

`base = self._base.score(...)` then an unconditional `_ask` for every decision with two or more scored actions (lines 71-77). No cache key, no batch, no per-sweep call budget, no sampling. The only concurrency control is the shared 6-slot semaphore at azure_openai.py:69-70.

**Impact.** The corpus grows 19-42 rows/day on a 20-customer book, so this is free today. A 200k-account NBFC book sweeping daily is on the order of 10^5 decisions; at ~700 prompt tokens each and six concurrent slots at ~800ms, one sweep is several hours of pure LLM wall clock and a five-figure monthly bill for a reordering with no demonstrated lift. It will also hit the deployment's TPM quota, and the failure mode there is the shared breaker opening on the live voice path (see rerank-no-timeout-shares-live-circuit).

**Fix.** Before scale matters, prove lift: run the reranker in shadow (compute both orders, log the disagreement rate and the outcome delta) for a fixed period and only enable it if it wins. Then bound it — a per-sweep call budget, a cache keyed on (bucket, dpd band, trigger kind, sorted action set) which will collapse most of the book onto a few hundred distinct prompts, and a rule that only decisions above an exposure threshold are eligible.

### `rerank-llm-sentence-is-discarded` — The whole rationale half of the reranker is dead: the fenced sentence is written to a field nothing persists or displays

**backend/agent_core/treatment/rerank.py:90** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T11-llm-touchpoints`

`reordered[0] = replace(reordered[0], explanation=why)`. `ScoredAction.to_log()` (scoring.py:156-167) emits action, channel, at, expectedValue, pReach, pResolve, cost, reasonCodes, components — and not explanation. engine.py:348 builds `line = narrate.rationale(...)` and engine.py:402 stores `rationale=line`. `to_payload` at engine.py:152 serialises alternatives with the same `to_log`. A Grep for `\.explanation` across backend/*.py returns a single hit: test_treatment_engine.py:869.

**Impact.** The system pays the full price of the LLM — latency, cost, a third-party processing event over borrower account state, prompt-injection surface, model-risk exposure — for an output that never reaches a human. Worse, narrate.py:8-9 tells the next engineer the sentence IS used, so the first person to wire it up will connect an unfenced-in-practice string to a screen believing the fence has been in production for months. The tests do not catch it: test_treatment_engine.py:869 asserts `"98765" not in out[0].explanation`, which passes trivially because the base EVScorer explanation is a different string entirely and would pass even if _safe_why returned garbage.

**Fix.** Decide the intent and make the code and docstrings agree. If the sentence is wanted: add an `llm_rationale` column (separate from the deterministic `rationale`, never replacing it), persist it, and label it in the UI as model-written. If it is not wanted: delete `_safe_why`, MAX_WHY_CHARS, `_digits` and the `why` half of the prompt, drop max_completion_tokens to ~60, and correct narrate.py:8-12. Replace the weak test with `assert out[0].explanation == base[0].explanation`.

### `rerank-mutates-propensity-without-record` — Reranking silently rewrites the exploration propensity and the draw seed, invalidating the off-policy corpus, and nothing records that it happened

**backend/agent_core/treatment/rerank.py:91** · statistics · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T11-llm-touchpoints`

`return reordered + tail` hands a permuted list to engine.py:306. arbitration then draws via `_chooser` (engine.py:450-488), and explore.choose assigns probability by POSITION: `weights = _rank_weights(len(eligible), greediness)` / `distribution = {action.action: weight for action, weight in zip(eligible, weights)}` (explore.py:124-127). The draw seed is `seed_for(..., actions=[s.action for s in scored])` (engine.py:470-475, explore.py:199-210), which hashes the list ORDER. engine.py:398 then writes `propensity=verdict.propensity` and engine.py:574 writes the per-action distribution into the candidate log.

**Impact.** TREATMENT_GREEDINESS=0.7 is live, so alpha=2.33 and rank position determines π. With the reranker on, the recorded π is a function of an LLM sample that is stored nowhere — not the response, not the model version, not even a boolean saying the reorder changed anything. Every IPS or doubly-robust estimate computed from treatment_decisions silently becomes invalid, and the corpus is the whole point of shadow mode (config.py:70-76). The explore.py claim that a replay reproduces the same choice (explore.py:35-36) also fails. A model-risk reviewer who discovers the logging policy was partly a hosted LLM will reject the entire uplift programme, not just the reranker.

**Fix.** Either (a) run the reranker AFTER the draw, purely as a display order, so it cannot touch π; or (b) keep it before the draw but persist the full LLM contribution on the decision row: a `rerank` JSON blob with the deployment name, the prompt hash, the raw order returned, the base order, and a boolean `changed`. Add an explicit `logging_policy_version` that increments when the reranker is toggled, and make trainers refuse rows whose logging policy included an unrecorded LLM.

### `rerank-no-dpdp-processing-record` — Borrower account state leaves the estate for a third-party processor with no consent check, no residency assertion and no processing record on the decision

**backend/agent_core/treatment/rerank.py:116** · privacy · missing-for-production · 1/1 confirm · reader `T11-llm-touchpoints`

`payload_json = json.dumps(payload)` plus the context dict at lines 117-128 send bucket, dpd, exact scheduled instants, promisesKept/promisesBroken, touchesToday and openDisputes to Azure OpenAI. No customer_id is included (good), but dpd + exposure-implying expectedValueInr + a precise ISO instant is a strong quasi-identifier when joined with the provider's own request logs. There is no tenant check, no consent check, no assertion that AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT resolves to an India region, and nothing written to the decision row saying this borrower's data was processed by a third party for this decision.

**Impact.** Under the DPDP Act the bank is the data fiduciary and must be able to enumerate processors and the purpose of each processing event. RBI's storage expectations for credit and payment data add a residency question this code cannot answer. A DPO asked 'which of our borrowers' delinquency data went to Microsoft, and when' has no query that answers it. The exposure scales with the sweep: every decision on the book is a separate transfer.

**Fix.** Gate the call on an explicit per-tenant `llm_processing_allowed` flag with a recorded lawful basis, assert the endpoint region at startup and refuse to run outside the permitted set, and write a compact processing record (processor, purpose, field list, timestamp) alongside each decision so the DPO's question is a SELECT. Strip `at` to a coarse bucket (morning/afternoon/evening) rather than an exact instant.

### `rerank-no-timeout-shares-live-circuit` — The rerank call passes no timeout and no profile, so it inherits a 20s budget with SDK retries on the same semaphore and circuit breaker the live voice turn depends on

**backend/agent_core/treatment/rerank.py:148** · reliability · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T11-llm-touchpoints`

`raw = azure_openai.chat_complete([{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], temperature=0.0, max_completion_tokens=250)` — no `timeout=`, no `profile=`. chat_complete forwards to chat_with_tools with profile defaulting to PROFILE_CHAT (azure_openai.py:606), which selects `get_client()` and `_azure_call` (azure_openai.py:643-645). Without `timeout` the `client.with_options(timeout=..., max_retries=0)` branch at azure_openai.py:660-673 never runs, so the call gets `_api_timeout_s()` = 20s (azure_openai.py:64-66) AND the SDK's default retries — the exact 26s-of-wall-clock failure the comment at azure_openai.py:666-671 documents. `_azure_call` acquires the MAIN semaphore, 6 slots, 10s bounded acquire (azure_openai.py:69-70, 83-101), and runs inside `circuit_breaker.get_breaker("azure_openai")` (azure_openai.py:148) — the same breaker azure_openai.py:154-157 explicitly says analysis traffic must not share with the live turn.

**Impact.** TREATMENT_SWEEP=1 means the sweep decides for the whole book. A degraded Azure deployment turns each decision into a ~60s stall; six concurrent sweep decisions consume every chat slot, so live voice turns start shedding with AzureBusyError (503) and the breaker opens on the path a borrower is speaking to. The module claims the fallback makes it 'safe to leave switched on' (rerank.py:18); that is true for the ranking and false for the platform. A collections floor loses telephony because a rationale-writer was enabled.

**Fix.** Route this call through `chat_with_tools(..., profile=PROFILE_ANALYSIS, timeout=<budget>)` — its own deployment, its own 2-slot semaphore, its own breaker and a 1s bounded acquire (azure_openai.py:104-137) — with an explicit budget of 300-500ms and max_retries=0. Add a wall-clock guard around the whole `_ask` like kb_rerank.py:236-244 does, so an over-budget rerank is discarded rather than waited on. Never let a decision-path LLM call share the live conversation's breaker.

### `rerank-injection-tripwire-is-only-a-log-line` — The only signal that a model named an unapproved action or invented a figure is a warning log — no counter, no alert, no row

**backend/agent_core/treatment/rerank.py:168** · observability · missing-for-production · 1/1 confirm · reader `T11-llm-touchpoints`

`logger.warning("treatment rerank returned unapproved actions %s — dropped", rejected)` at 168-170 and `logger.warning("treatment rerank rationale invented figures %s — dropped", sorted(invented))` at 190-192. The comment at 164-167 correctly calls this 'the failure that matters ... a prompt-injection attempt'. Nothing increments a metric; treatment/metrics.py contains no rerank counter; nothing is written to the decision row; nothing pages anyone.

**Impact.** The event this code exists to detect is invisible to operations. A model that starts naming field_visit on every account — whether from an upstream data-poisoning path, a deployment swap, or a genuine injection once free text is ever added to the prompt — is dropped correctly and reported to a log stream nobody has an alert on. A bank's security function will ask what detects this and the honest answer is 'grep'. The rejected string is also model-controlled and interpolated straight into a log line, which is a small log-forging surface.

**Fix.** Emit a counter per rejection kind and per tenant, alert on a nonzero rate, and persist a `rerank_rejections` field on the decision row so the tripwire has a queryable history. Truncate and repr() the model-supplied strings before logging. Consider a circuit that disables the reranker for the rest of the sweep after N rejections rather than continuing to trust it.

### `rerank-number-fence-is-digits-only` — The invention check only sees digits, and only checks provenance, not meaning — spelled-out amounts and mislabelled internal figures both pass

**backend/agent_core/treatment/rerank.py:188** · compliance · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T11-llm-touchpoints`

`invented = _digits(why) - known` with `_NUMBER = re.compile(r"\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?")` (line 36) and `known = _digits(payload_json) | _digits(json.dumps(context))` (line 187). Two holes. (1) "Offer a fifty percent waiver and settle for half the balance" contains no digit and passes untouched. (2) `payload_json` contains `expectedValueInr` and ISO instants, so "2026-09-05T14:30:00+05:30" alone seeds the known set with 2026, 09, 05, 14, 30, 00 — and a `why` reading "₹412 outstanding" passes whenever 412 happens to be the expected value, presenting the bank's internal net EV to an agent as the borrower's balance.

**Impact.** The docstring's own scenario — 'An agent reads "₹4,200 outstanding" as fact and repeats it to the borrower' (rerank.py:181) — is not actually blocked; only its digit-shaped spelling is. A spelled-out concession is worse than a wrong figure: an agent who repeats 'we can do a fifty percent waiver' has made an unauthorised settlement offer, which is a mis-selling event and, if the borrower relies on it, a promise the bank may have to honour. The authority engine exists precisely to bound concessions, and a free-text sentence routes around it.

**Fix.** Do not fence free text — constrain it. Have the model choose from a closed set of pre-written rationale templates keyed by reason code, or return only a template id plus slot values that the deterministic layer renders. If free text must survive, add (a) a spelled-out-number and percentage-word blocklist, (b) a concession-vocabulary blocklist (waiver, settle, discount, write off, part payment, moratorium) checked against the authority envelope, and (c) drop `expectedValueInr` and `cost` from the payload so internal economics can never be laundered into an agent-facing sentence.

### `tuner-decline-rate-has-no-counterfactual` — The tuner infers a weight direction from an outcome rate observed entirely under the current weights, with no propensity to correct for it

**backend/agent_core/tuner.py:48** · statistics · hidden-assumption · 1/1 confirm · reader `T11-llm-touchpoints`

`COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE presented AND response = 'declined') AS declined, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE presented) AS presented FROM offer_decisions` (tuner.py:48-53). offer_decisions carries no propensity, policy_version or explore_kind column, so there is no way to reweight. The treatment half is the same shape (tuner.py:117-121) despite treatment_decisions having all three.

**Impact.** A high decline rate is at least as likely to be about the offer catalogue, the segment being called, or the agents' pitch as about the fatigue weight. Acting on it as though it were a weight signal is a causal claim the data cannot support, and it will move the policy in the wrong direction as often as the right one. The treatment half is worse in one respect: it ignores propensity columns that exist and are non-degenerate.

**Fix.** For treatment, compute the suggestion from an inverse-propensity-weighted estimate over the logged distribution the engine already stores in the candidate log, not from a raw rate. For reco, add propensity, policy_version and explore_kind to offer_decisions (the treatment schema is the model to copy) before any tuning claim is made, and return `note="no_propensity"` until they exist rather than a suggestion.

### `tuner-global-knobs-no-tenant-scope` — Both queries aggregate across every tenant and portfolio, and the knobs they propose are process-global env vars

**backend/agent_core/tuner.py:51** · data-model · hidden-assumption · 1/1 confirm · reader `T11-llm-touchpoints`

`FROM offer_decisions WHERE created_at >= now() - (:d * interval '1 day')` (tuner.py:51-53) and `FROM treatment_decisions WHERE created_at >= now() - (:d * interval '1 day')` (tuner.py:121-123) — no tenant_id predicate, although decisions.record writes tenant_id on every treatment row (decisions.py:67, 100, 133). The knobs themselves are read from os.environ via reco_config/tcfg, so there is exactly one value per process.

**Impact.** This holds only because the dev book is one tenant with one product. A real NBFC runs a two-wheeler book and a personal-loan book with genuinely different fatigue economics and field-visit norms, and a platform deployment runs several lenders. The tuner would average them and propose one number, and there is no mechanism to apply a different number per book even if the analysis were right. Cross-tenant aggregation in a multi-lender deployment is also a data-segregation question a DPO will raise on its own.

**Fix.** Make the knobs per-tenant-per-product rows in a config table with a documented resolution order (product > tenant > global default), scope both queries by tenant_id and product, and return suggestions keyed by scope. Env vars stay as the bootstrap default only.

### `tuner-fires-on-noise` — Policy-change thresholds compare a point estimate from n=20 against a hard rate with no interval

**backend/agent_core/tuner.py:67** · statistics · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T11-llm-touchpoints`

`if presented >= 20 and declined / presented > 0.6:` and `elif presented >= 20 and declined / presented < 0.2:` (67, 71); `if actionable >= 20 and field_n / actionable > 0.15:` (134). No confidence interval, no minimum detectable effect, no comparison against a baseline period.

**Impact.** At n=20 the 95% interval on p̂=0.65 spans roughly 0.44 to 0.86 — the threshold at 0.6 is inside the noise, so the tuner will recommend a knob change on a coin flip. The treatment half is the reachable one today: the book already produces 19-42 decisions/day, so `actionable >= 20` clears within a day and a single day with four field visits out of twenty trips `high_field_share`. An operator who trusts the suggestion is being told to change collections policy because of one busy Tuesday.

**Fix.** Require a Wilson interval on the observed rate to sit entirely beyond the threshold before proposing anything, and set the minimum n from a power calculation for the effect size worth acting on (which for a 0.15 threshold is in the hundreds, not twenty). Report the interval in `evidence` so the human sees the uncertainty they are being asked to act on.

### `tuner-no-change-log-no-approval` — Suggestions are stateless — nothing records that one was made, who applied it, or whether it helped

**backend/agent_core/tuner.py:78** · compliance · missing-for-production · 1/1 confirm · reader `T11-llm-touchpoints`

`"applied": False` and `copyToEnv` (tuner.py:78-85, 149) hand the operator a list to paste. `current` is read live from `reco_config.weights()` / `tcfg.policy()` (29, 98), so the function has no memory of prior suggestions and no way to detect that its last one was applied. No row is written anywhere; the endpoint at main.py:1094-1098 is a pure GET.

**Impact.** A parameter of a live collections policy changes because someone read a webpage and edited an env file. There is no approver, no rationale of record, no before/after measurement, and no link from the running config back to the evidence that justified it. That is precisely the artefact a model-risk or internal-audit function asks for first, and its absence will block go-live independently of whether the suggestions are any good. It also means a bad suggestion cannot be rolled back to a known state.

**Fix.** Persist every generated suggestion with its evidence window, and give applying one a first-class path: a `policy_parameter_changes` table with proposer, approver, before, after, effective_from, and the decision-row range it is expected to affect. Read the running value from that table rather than from env, so the config has a history. Emit an automatic evaluation N days after each applied change comparing the metric the suggestion claimed to move.

### `tuner-treatment-deltas-are-unbounded` — The treatment half proposes unclamped knob increases, unlike the reco half, so repeated application drives every action below the value floor and silences the book

**backend/agent_core/tuner.py:135** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `T11-llm-touchpoints`

`proposed["TREATMENT_FATIGUE_COST"] = current["TREATMENT_FATIGUE_COST"] + 2.0` and `proposed["TREATMENT_FIELD_DIGITAL_EXHAUSTION"] = current["TREATMENT_FIELD_DIGITAL_EXHAUSTION"] + 1` — no ceiling. Compare the reco half fifty lines up: `min(0.25, current["RECO_W_FATIGUE"] + 0.05)` and `max(0.05, current["RECO_W_INTENT"] - 0.05)` (tuner.py:68-69). The suggestion is computed from the LIVE value (`policy = tcfg.policy()`, tuner.py:98), so applying it makes the next run propose another +2.0 from the new base.

**Impact.** fatigue_cost is subtracted inside the expected-value computation. Applied five weeks running it reaches +10 rupees per attempt, at which point every digital action on a small-balance account prices below zero and arbitration returns SUPPRESS_BELOW_FLOOR for the whole book. The failure is invisible — the engine reports healthy decisions, all of them 'wait' — and the operator who copied the suggestion each week has no record telling them the ratchet is theirs. On a real book that is weeks of unworked delinquency and no alert.

**Fix.** Clamp both treatment knobs the way the reco knobs are clamped, and derive the ceiling from config rather than a literal. Better: make every suggestion an ABSOLUTE proposed value computed from the evidence window, not a delta off the live value, so the function is idempotent — applying the same suggestion twice must be a no-op. Add a guard that refuses to propose any knob change that would push the projected suppression rate above a threshold, computed against the last window's scored candidates.

### `gateway-path-has-no-breaker-or-semaphore` — Turning on the LLM gateway removes the circuit breaker and the concurrency cap from every LLM call in the process, including the live turn, and adds up to 3x20s of retry

**backend/llm_gateway/client.py:112** · reliability · defect · unverified (verifier-added) · reader `T11-llm-touchpoints`

azure_openai.chat_with_tools:620-634 tries `llm_gateway.client.maybe_chat(...)` FIRST and returns its result if non-None, so when LLM_GATEWAY_ENABLED is set with a base URL, execution never reaches `_azure_call` (azure_openai.py:638-645) and therefore never enters `circuit_breaker.get_breaker("azure_openai")` (azure_openai.py:148) or `_azure_slot()`'s 6-slot bounded acquire (azure_openai.py:87-101). The gateway path is a bare `httpx.post(base_url() + "/chat/completions", ..., timeout=timeout or 20.0)` inside `for attempt in range(retries + 1)` with `retries = 2` (llm_gateway/client.py:112-131) — no semaphore, no breaker, and three attempts of a 20s timeout on any exception, not only on 5xx. The analysis profile's isolation (azure_openai.py:153-163) is likewise bypassed: gw_profile collapses to 'analysis' or 'text' (line 619) and both go down the same unguarded httpx path.

**Impact.** The gateway is the on-prem/no-egress route a bank deployment is most likely to enable, and enabling it silently deletes the two controls that keep a degraded model provider from taking the process down. A slow LiteLLM/vLLM endpoint gives every caller — including the live conversational turn — up to 60s of blocking wall clock with unbounded concurrency, where the Azure path would have shed with AzureBusyError after 10s and opened a breaker. The failure is invisible in code review because the caller signature and the docstrings are unchanged; the only symptom is that a flag flip changes the reliability posture of every LLM call in the platform.

**Fix.** Wrap the gateway call in the same `_azure_slot()`/`_analysis_slot()` and a `get_breaker("llm_gateway_<profile>")` before returning it from chat_with_tools, so the guard is a property of the call site rather than of the backend chosen. Retry only on 5xx and on connect errors (the current `except Exception` retries on a 4xx-derived raise_for_status too), and cap total wall clock rather than per-attempt timeout. Add a test asserting a hung gateway sheds within the acquire timeout instead of blocking a worker.

### `causal-headline-metric-never-rendered` — incrementalRecoveryPerRupee — the declared headline of the whole scoreboard — is fetched and dropped

**Habibi/src/api/treatment.ts:152** · statistics · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U01-treatment-ui`

`incrementalRecoveryPerRupee?: number | null;` is declared at treatment.ts:152 and appears nowhere in treatment.lazy.tsx. The backend calls it the headline: 'its headline is incremental recovery per rupee against the control arm, never a collections rate' (db_treatment_holds.py:449). Likewise `attributableRecoveryInr` and `incrementalCureRate` (metrics.py:176-182) are neither typed nor rendered, while the Efficiency panel does render `recoveredInr` (treatment.lazy.tsx:506) — the gross figure the backend explicitly warns 'belonged to borrowers who would have paid anyway' (metrics.py:164-168).

**Impact.** The console shows the number the design note says not to trust (gross recovered) and hides the number it says to trust (attributable recovery per rupee). A collections head will build the business case on the wrong figure, and the response-model error the whole engine was designed to avoid re-enters through the dashboard.

**Fix.** Make 'Incremental recovery per rupee' the single largest number on the Insights tab, with attributable vs gross recovery shown side by side and the backend's `note` string printed underneath. Move gross `recoveredInr` into a subordinate hint.

### `mock-shapes-diverge-from-backend` — The mock corpus was written to the TypeScript types, not to the backend — so dev looks complete and prod renders blanks

**Habibi/src/api/treatment.ts:378** · testing · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U01-treatment-ui`

mockModelHealth (treatment.ts:378-420) supplies `psi`/`drifted` on drift features (lines 406-411), a numeric `bin` on calibration rows (lines 390-394), and `{metric, message}` alerts (lines 415-418) — none of which the backend emits (monitor.py:272-281, 327-335, 552-583). mockMetrics.causal is `available:false` (line 425), so the broken available branch is never exercised in mock either. Dev defaults to mock ON (config.ts:26).

**Impact.** Every panel that is broken against the live backend looks perfect in the demo. The mock is not a test double, it is a second, incompatible implementation of the contract, and it actively conceals the defects above. This is how a system passes every internal demo and fails on the customer's first real day.

**Fix.** Generate the mock from the backend's actual response shapes (a recorded fixture from a live call, or types generated from the OpenAPI schema), and add a contract test that asserts the mock and the TypeScript types both match a captured backend payload. Make the mock's causal branch `available:true` so that path is exercised.

### `browsing-writes-decision-rows` — Operator browsing injects live decision rows into the corpus every statistic is computed from

**Habibi/src/api/treatment.ts:1056** · statistics · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U01-treatment-ui`

useTreatmentNext fires on row selection with `staleTime: 30_000` (treatment.ts:1063) and inherits the app-wide `retry: 1` (router.tsx:9); each call writes a decision row (main.py:4772-4776). Radix TabsContent unmounts inactive tabs, so returning to Cases after 30s refetches. Nothing in insights(), metrics.causal() or monitor.report() filters on trigger_kind — every query is `FROM treatment_decisions WHERE created_at >= ...` (decisions.py:436-437, metrics.py:82-85). With TREATMENT_MODE=live these rows land in the borrower's assigned A/B arm with a propensity attached.

**Impact.** On a ~20-customer book growing 19-42 decisions/day, an analyst clicking through the Cases tab for ten minutes is a material fraction of the daily corpus. Those rows inflate the decisions/coverage/latency denominators, enter the null_treatment vs treated split that the causal ATE is computed from, and carry propensities into any off-policy estimate — all describing questions a human asked, not actions the engine took. The corpus that is supposed to be evidence becomes partly a record of dashboard usage.

**Fix.** Give UI-originated queries their own trigger kind (e.g. 'console_query') or an `origin` column, exclude that origin from insights/metrics/monitor/causal by default with a toggle to include it, and set `retry: 0` on useTreatmentNext. Longer term, split /treatment/next into a non-writing preview and an explicit 'log this question' action.

### `no-frontend-tests-for-the-console` — Zero tests cover 2,710 lines of decision-intelligence UI

**Habibi/src/routes/treatment.lazy.tsx:1** · testing · missing-for-production · 1/1 confirm · reader `U01-treatment-ui`

No test file references treatment: a glob over Habibi/src/**/*treatment* returns only treatment.tsx, treatment.ts and treatment.lazy.tsx, and none of the 19 existing .test files mentions treatment. The repo does test wire-type nullability against backend schemas (api/types/nullability.test.ts) and keyboard alternatives (components/keyboard-alternatives.test.tsx) — the treatment console is excluded from both, and both would have caught defects listed here.

**Impact.** Every shape-drift defect in this report — the blank alerts, the all-green drift board, the em-dash calibration bins, the empty causal panel — is the kind a single contract test would have caught at authoring time. 216 backend tests pass while the surface an operator actually reads is untested.

**Fix.** Extend nullability.test.ts to pin every field in treatment.ts against the producing Python module, and add rendering tests for the four tabs against captured live-backend payloads (not the mock), asserting that no panel renders an all-em-dash column or an empty alert.

### `serving-drifted-renders-neutral` — 'A different model is serving than the one that was approved' renders as a grey neutral lozenge

**Habibi/src/routes/treatment.lazy.tsx:226** · compliance · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U01-treatment-ui`

`const SERVING_TONE: Record<string, LozengeTone> = { ok: "success", unregistered: "warning", stale: "warning", missing: "danger" };` (treatment.lazy.tsx:226-231) and `<Lozenge tone={SERVING_TONE[s.state] ?? "neutral"}>` (line 777). registry.verify emits `"drifted"` when the serving file's SHA differs from the promoted artifact's, and `"absent"` when neither exists (registry.py:414, 434). Neither is in the map, so both render grey. `"stale"` is in the map and in the TS union (treatment.ts:257) and is never emitted by the backend.

**Impact.** The one state this panel was built to catch — someone replaced the model file under a promoted version, so every log line names an approved model while different coefficients decide who gets called — is displayed in the least alarming colour available, quieter than 'unregistered'. That is a model-governance breach rendered as a footnote. The unrendered `version`, `promotedAt` and `promotedBy` that verify() also returns (registry.py:435-437) would have named the approver.

**Fix.** Map drifted→danger and absent→warning, delete the phantom 'stale', and derive the union from the backend's TARGETS/states rather than by hand. Render version, promotedAt and promotedBy on each serving row, and raise a page-level banner (not a list item) when any target is drifted.

### `timestamps-have-no-timezone-and-no-year` — Every timestamp in the console renders in the browser's timezone with no zone label and no year

**Habibi/src/routes/treatment.lazy.tsx:249** · compliance · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U01-treatment-ui`

`return d.toLocaleString("en-IN", { day: "2-digit", month: "short", hour: "2-digit", minute: "2-digit", hour12: false });` (treatment.lazy.tsx:249-255). No `timeZone`, no `timeZoneName`, no `year`. This one function formats every decision time, hold start, SLA due date, expiry, release time, model registration and model promotion in the console (lines 837, 840, 1019, 1079, 1236, 1239, 1242, 1258). The en-IN locale controls formatting only; the clock is whatever the browser is set to.

**Impact.** The RBI calling window is 08:00-19:00 IST. A console that prints '22 Aug, 05:31' with no zone, on a locked-down VDI whose TZ may well be UTC, makes it impossible to verify from the screen whether a contact was inside the window — the exact question an inspection asks. The missing year turns the model registry, which is an approval record, into ambiguous evidence: '18 Aug, 09:31' does not say which year a model was promoted.

**Fix.** Format all timestamps in a single explicit tenant timezone (Asia/Kolkata) with `timeZone` and `timeZoneName: 'short'` set, include the year on anything older than the current one, and show the raw ISO instant on hover. Put a 'times shown in IST' note in the page header.

### `no-arm-or-exploration-visibility` — The randomised holdout and the exploration policy are invisible in the console

**Habibi/src/routes/treatment.lazy.tsx:423** · statistics · missing-for-production · 1/1 confirm · reader `U01-treatment-ui`

The Insights tab's only split is by mode: `<Panel title="Mode split" description="Shadow decides and logs; live also acts.">` (treatment.lazy.tsx:423-435) over `data.byMode` (shadow/live). There is no split by `variant`, though 97 of 225 decision rows sit in the null_treatment arm under TREATMENT_AB_SPLIT=control:80,null_treatment:20. `propensity` is rendered for exactly one decision (line 1080) and nowhere in aggregate; TREATMENT_GREEDINESS=0.7 and explore_kind appear nowhere in the file.

**Impact.** Twenty percent of the book is being deliberately withheld from collections outreach so that a causal number can exist, and neither the collections head who owns recovery nor the model-risk reviewer who owns the experiment can see that from this console. Arm imbalance, assignment leakage and a collapsed propensity distribution are the three ways an A/B result silently becomes noise, and none is observable here.

**Fix.** Add an Experiment panel: arm sizes and shares over the window, arm balance on key covariates (DPD, exposure, bucket), propensity distribution histogram, exploration rate and explore_kind mix, and the current greediness setting. Alert when an arm's share drifts from its configured split or when the propensity distribution degenerates.

### `outcomes-panel-mixes-enactment-failures-with-borrower-outcomes` — 'cancelled' — an enactment abort — is displayed as a borrower outcome beside 'paid' and 'ptp'

**Habibi/src/routes/treatment.lazy.tsx:437** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U01-treatment-ui`

The Outcomes panel renders every distinct `outcome` value as a peer bar: `rows={data.outcomes.map((o) => ({ key: o.outcome, label: humanise(o.outcome), count: o.count }))}` (treatment.lazy.tsx:449-453), described as 'Labelled results, once a case has moved' (line 439). The corpus today holds 84 'cancelled' (set by enact.py when enactment aborts), 14 no_answer, 10 ptp, 7 paid, 4 superseded. Because the backend filters `outcome IS NOT NULL` (decisions.py:476), the BarList denominator is 119 and 'Cancelled' renders as ~71% of the panel — labelled as an outcome, in the same neutral bar as 'Paid'.

**Impact.** Two thirds of this engine's labelled rows are the engine failing to execute its own decision, and the console presents that as a borrower behaviour alongside a 6% payment rate. A collections head reads a busy outcomes chart as the engine working. Worse, an enactment failure rate of that magnitude is the loudest operational signal in the system and it has no alert, no trend and no drill-down.

**Fix.** Split the panel in two: 'Borrower outcomes' (paid, ptp, no_answer, refused) with the correct denominator stated, and 'Execution failures' (cancelled, superseded) rendered as a danger-toned health metric with its own trend line and an alert threshold. Add a drill-down to the cancellation reasons from enact.py.

### `causal-panel-renders-fields-backend-never-sends` — The causal panel goes blank the moment the arms are thick enough to report a causal number

**Habibi/src/routes/treatment.lazy.tsx:471** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U01-treatment-ui`

`<Stat label="Treatment effect" value={fmtRate(m.causal.ate ?? null)} />` / `<Stat label="Standard error" value={fmtRate(m.causal.stderr ?? null, 2)} />` (treatment.lazy.tsx:471-472). The backend's available branch returns controlN, treatedN, controlCureRate, treatedCureRate, incrementalCureRate, recoveredInr, attributableRecoveryInr, spendInr, incrementalRecoveryPerRupee, note (metrics.py:170-187) — no `ate`, no `stderr`, no `significant` under any branch (the unavailable branch, metrics.py:96-106, returns only available/reason/controlN/treatedN). Today this is invisible because the control arm holds 97 labelled rows against MIN_ARM_N, so the unavailable path renders instead.

**Impact.** The panel that exists to answer 'is the engine paying for itself, causally?' will render 'Treatment effect —' and 'Standard error —' beside two arm counts as soon as the corpus grows past the minimum. The empty state is the only state that has ever been exercised. A collections head who waited months for the arms to fill will get two em dashes.

**Fix.** Render what the backend actually computes: incremental cure rate as the headline, control and treated cure rates beside it, attributable recovery and spend, and incrementalRecoveryPerRupee as the ratio. If a standard error and a significance verdict are wanted (they should be), add them to metrics.causal in the backend first and render them second — never type a field the producer does not emit.

### `compliance-denial-reasons-never-rendered` — The Conduct panel shows a denial count and hides why contacts were denied

**Habibi/src/routes/treatment.lazy.tsx:514** · compliance · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U01-treatment-ui`

The Conduct panel renders attempts, allowed, denied, worst-day touches, opt-outs and total breaches (treatment.lazy.tsx:514-528). `m.compliance.denialsByReason` (typed at treatment.ts:170, populated by metrics.py:303) is never rendered. The window/cap breach split (`windowBreaches`, `capBreaches`, typed at treatment.ts:171-172, produced at metrics.py:395-396) is collapsed into the single `breaches` total at line 527.

**Impact.** '14 contacts denied' without reasons is a number nobody can act on. Whether the denials were quiet_hours, dnd_registry, or consent-withdrawn determines who gets called next and which regulator cares. And a window breach (a contact outside 08:00-19:00) and a cap breach (a fourth touch in a day) are different regulatory failures with different remediations, presented as one figure.

**Fix.** Render denialsByReason as a BarList inside the Conduct panel, split windowBreaches and capBreaches into separate stats with distinct tones, and make any non-zero breach count a page-level danger banner with a link to the offending contact-ledger rows.

### `model-health-alerts-shape-drift` — Every model-health alert renders with an em-dash title and an empty body against the live backend

**Habibi/src/routes/treatment.lazy.tsx:619** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U01-treatment-ui`

`title={isObject ? humanise(alert.metric) : "Model alert"}` and `{isObject ? alert.message : alert}` (treatment.lazy.tsx:626, 628), typed as `Array<{ metric: string; message: string } | string>` (treatment.ts:134). The backend emits `{"level": ..., "check": "feature_drift", "detail": "dpd has moved +0.62σ from training (...)"}` (monitor.py:552-583). So `alert.metric` is undefined → humanise(undefined) returns '—' (treatment.ts:1197), `alert.message` is undefined → the SectionMessage body is empty, and `key={alert.metric}` (line 623) is undefined for every alert. `variant="warning"` is hardcoded, so a level:'alert' renders identically to a level:'warn'.

**Impact.** The alert banner is the only place the console says 'the reach model is 12 points optimistic' or 'the contact-history feature has drifted'. On the live backend it renders as a stack of blank amber boxes titled '—'. A model-risk reviewer will read that as a rendering glitch, not as a suppressed alert, and the EV formula keeps multiplying rupees by a miscalibrated probability.

**Fix.** Change the type to `{ level: 'warn'|'alert'; check: string; detail: string }`, render `humanise(alert.check)` as the title and `alert.detail` as the body, map level→variant (alert=error, warn=warning), and key on `${alert.check}-${i}`. Add a runtime shape assertion in the fetcher so a future backend rename fails loudly instead of rendering blanks.

### `calibration-bin-field-absent` — The reach-calibration table's Bin column is entirely em-dashes and every row shares an undefined React key

**Habibi/src/routes/treatment.lazy.tsx:703** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U01-treatment-ui`

`{h.reachCalibration.bins.map((b) => (<TableRow key={b.bin}>` ... `{fmtRate(b.bin, 0)}` (treatment.lazy.tsx:703-707), typed `{ bin: number; n; predicted; observed }` (treatment.ts:96-101). reliability() emits `{"range": "0.0-0.1", "n", "predicted", "observed", "gap"}` (monitor.py:327-335) — there is no numeric `bin`, and `gap` (observed − predicted, the actual finding per bin) is neither typed nor rendered. `reachCalibration.level` (monitor.py:339-345) is also dropped.

**Impact.** The calibration table — the evidence that P(reach) means what it says before it is multiplied by rupees — renders four numbers and a column of dashes, with React reconciling rows by index under duplicate undefined keys. A validator cannot tell which probability band is miscalibrated, which is the only thing the table is for.

**Fix.** Type the bin as `{ range: string; n: number; predicted: number; observed: number; gap: number }`, key on `range`, render the range string and the signed gap, and colour the gap cell by magnitude. Surface `reachCalibration.level` as a lozenge on the panel header.

### `uplift-calibration-vanishes-when-it-becomes-available` — The most important model-risk check in the package renders only while it cannot be computed, and disappears the moment it can

**Habibi/src/routes/treatment.lazy.tsx:729** · statistics · defect · unverified (verifier-added) · reader `U01-treatment-ui`

`{h.upliftCalibration.available ? null : (<SectionMessage variant="information" ... title="Uplift calibration is unavailable">{h.upliftCalibration.reason ...} Treated {fmtNum(h.upliftCalibration.treatedN)}, control {fmtNum(h.upliftCalibration.controlN)}.</SectionMessage>)}` (treatment.lazy.tsx:729-740). The available branch is literally `null` — nothing is rendered. When uplift_calibration CAN report, it returns quantity, fittedUplift, predictedMeanTau, measuredAte, gap, treatedN, controlN, level and note (monitor.py:472-486), and none of it reaches the screen. The type is wrong too: treatment.ts:121 declares `predictedTau` while the producer emits `predictedMeanTau` (monitor.py:479), and gap/level/note/quantity/fittedUplift are not modelled at all. The module's own docstring calls this 'The only calibration check available for a causal estimate, and the most important one in the package' and explains that a model claiming far more uplift than the arm measured 'is not a miscalibrated uplift model. It is a response model' (monitor.py:403-412).

**Impact.** The single check that catches the failure mode the whole engine was designed to avoid — an uplift model that is really a response model, ranking borrowers who would have paid anyway — is displayed only in the state where it says nothing, and silently vanishes the instant it has an answer. A model-risk reviewer watching the panel sees the 'unavailable' notice disappear and reasonably reads that as the problem resolving, when it means the check just produced a result nobody can see. Combined with the alerts finding, a level:'alert' uplift gap would also render as a blank amber box titled '—'.

**Fix.** Render the available branch: predicted mean tau against measured ATE with the signed gap as the headline, the `quantity` string ('tau' vs 'p_resolve_prior') as the panel subtitle so a reader knows which quantity is being scored, `note` beneath it, and `level` as the lozenge tone (ok=success, warn=warning, alert=danger). Correct `predictedTau` to `predictedMeanTau` and add fittedUplift, gap, level and note to the type.

### `no-model-approval-workflow` — The model ledger is read-only and hides who approved each model and why

**Habibi/src/routes/treatment.lazy.tsx:787** · compliance · missing-for-production · 1/1 confirm · reader `U01-treatment-ui`

The 'Champion / challenger ledger' table (treatment.lazy.tsx:798-845) renders target, version, status, corpus, samples, holdout AUC, segments, registered_at and promoted_at. `promoted_by`, `reason`, `control_n`, `retired_at` and `evaluation` are all typed (treatment.ts:232-245) and none is rendered. There is no promote, reject, or roll-back action anywhere in the file, and no such endpoint exists in main.py (grep for 'promote' finds only /kb/gaps/{id}/promote-skill and /gateway/canary/{id}/promote).

**Impact.** Model approval in an Indian bank is a committee act with a named approver, a rationale, a validation report and a rollback plan. This console shows the timestamp of an approval and hides the approver and the justification. There is no way to promote a validated challenger or to roll back a champion from the UI, so every model movement is a shell operation with no first-class record — which is precisely the gap a model-risk audit is designed to find.

**Fix.** Render promoted_by, reason, control_n, retired_at and the evaluation blob (as an expandable panel) in the ledger. Add permission-gated Promote / Reject / Roll back actions behind maker-checker, requiring a rationale, writing to the registry, and attaching the validation artefacts. Show a diff of champion vs challenger metrics beside the button.

### `no-pagination-on-cases-and-holds` — Cases and Holds silently truncate at 200 rows with no pagination and no truncation notice

**Habibi/src/routes/treatment.lazy.tsx:922** · scale · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U01-treatment-ui`

`const cases = useTreatmentCases({ openOnly });` (treatment.lazy.tsx:922) and `const holds = useTreatmentHolds({ activeOnly });` (line 1153) — neither passes limit or offset, though both are supported by the fetchers (treatment.ts:1029-1041, 938-950). With limit omitted the backend clamps to DEFAULT_LIST_LIMIT = 200 (db_core.py:211). The UI has no page controls, no total count, no 'showing N of M', and no infinite scroll.

**Impact.** This holds on a 20-customer dev book and fails on the first real portfolio. A collections head on a 200,000-account book opens Cases, sees the newest 200 rows, and has no indication that 199,800 are missing. Any judgement made from that table — 'the ladder mostly stops at WhatsApp', 'nobody is over five contacts' — is drawn from an arbitrary recent slice presented as the whole. The same applies to Holds, where a missing hold is a compliance event.

**Fix.** Return a total count from both endpoints, render 'showing 1-200 of N' with pagination or virtualised infinite scroll, and make truncation impossible to miss. Note that the model-health endpoint already models this correctly with `truncated`/`sampleLimit` (monitor.py:519-520) — reuse that pattern.

### `no-search-or-filter-on-cases` — The Cases table has one boolean filter and no search, sort, or column filtering

**Habibi/src/routes/treatment.lazy.tsx:926** · scale · missing-for-production · 1/1 confirm · reader `U01-treatment-ui`

There is no borrower search, no trigger filter, no suppression-reason filter, no DPD or exposure filter, and no sortable columns — the order is fixed at `ORDER BY max(td.created_at) DESC` (db_treatment_holds.py:404). The same is true of the Holds table.

**Impact.** The stated purpose of this tab is the floor lead's question 'what has been tried on this account and what is left' (main.py:4869-4871) — which starts with naming an account. There is no way to name one. On a real book the table is a reverse-chronological firehose, and answering a specific borrower's complaint from this console is impossible.

**Fix.** Add borrower search (name/id/account, typeahead against the customers endpoint), filters for trigger kind, suppression reason, last outcome and DPD bucket, and sortable columns for decisions, attempts and last-decided. Reflect the filter state in the URL so a supervisor can share a link to a case.

### `no-decision-drilldown` — No decision id, no policy version, and no way to look up a decision that already happened

**Habibi/src/routes/treatment.lazy.tsx:1077** · observability · missing-for-production · 1/1 confirm · reader `U01-treatment-ui`

`decisionId` (treatment.ts:59) and `policyVersion` (treatment.ts:61) appear nowhere in treatment.lazy.tsx — the Next-best-treatment stat grid renders expected value, scheduled time, propensity and latency (lines 1077-1082) and drops both. The Cases table columns (lines 962-971) never render `c.rationale`, though the payload carries it (treatment.ts:326). There is no decision-history view; the only way to see a decision is to make a new one.

**Impact.** A borrower complains 'why did you call me four times about this?' A supervisor cannot pull up the four decisions, cannot see which policy version produced them, and cannot quote a decision id in the grievance response. The engine writes a fully attributable audit corpus and the console throws away the keys to it. Under RBI grievance redress and DPDP's right to information about processing, 'we cannot show you what the system decided' is not an acceptable answer.

**Fix.** Add GET /treatment/decisions?customerId=&triggerKind=&triggerRef= and a per-case decision timeline: id, timestamp, policy version, arm, chosen action, propensity, explore kind, suppression reason, rationale, alternatives, exclusions, outcome. Render decisionId and policyVersion (copyable) on the Next-best-treatment panel, and make each case row expand into its decision history.

### `alternatives-drop-reason-codes-and-timing` — The 'alternatives considered' table drops the reason codes, the components, the timing and the contract

**Habibi/src/routes/treatment.lazy.tsx:1100** · observability · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U01-treatment-ui`

The table renders action, expectedValue, pReach, pResolve, cost (treatment.lazy.tsx:1100-1116). `reasonCodes: string[]` and `components: Record<string, number>` and `at: string | null` are all on TreatmentCandidate (treatment.ts:40, 45-46) and none is rendered. `contract?: Record<string, unknown>` (treatment.ts:70) — the Action Contract that authorises the action — is typed and never displayed.

**Impact.** 'Why was human_call not chosen?' is answered with four numbers and no reason code, when the backend supplies 'agent_minutes_priced' / 'lower_net_value' — the actual mechanism. The `at` field is half the decision (the engine's whole timing model exists to pick the hour), and comparing alternatives without their proposed times makes the ranking unreadable. Without the contract, an operator cannot see what the engine was authorised to do.

**Fix.** Add a 'Scheduled for' column and a reason-code lozenge row per alternative, expose `components` in an expandable row (reach × resolve × exposure − cost, shown as the arithmetic), and render the contract as a labelled key/value block on the chosen action.

### `no-aggregate-exclusion-view` — Actions vetoed before scoring are visible one decision at a time and never in aggregate

**Habibi/src/routes/treatment.lazy.tsx:1122** · observability · missing-for-production · 1/1 confirm · reader `U01-treatment-ui`

The `excluded` map is rendered only inside the per-decision panel (treatment.lazy.tsx:1122-1137). The Insights tab has a suppression mix (why an actionable decision did nothing) and an action mix (what was chosen), but nothing that reports which actions were never candidates. represent_mandate has been excluded on all 225 decisions — 124 no_mandate_on_file, 97 control_arm — and no view in this console would reveal that.

**Impact.** A whole channel can be dark for weeks and the console will show a healthy action mix over the remaining channels. Mandate re-presentation is typically the cheapest recovery action in an Indian collections book; the engine has never once considered it, and the operator has no way to discover that short of clicking through individual decisions and noticing a repeated string.

**Fix.** Add an 'Actions never considered' panel to Insights: per action, the number of decisions where it was excluded and the reason breakdown, with a 'never a candidate in this window' flag. Alert when an action's candidacy rate drops to zero over a window it was previously eligible in.

### `insights-counts-simulated-rows-that-the-panels-below-it-exclude` — Two halves of the Insights tab are computed over different decision populations, with nothing on screen saying so

**backend/agent_core/treatment/decisions.py:437** · statistics · defect · unverified (verifier-added) · reader `U01-treatment-ui`

insights() takes only `days` and applies no mode predicate anywhere: totals `FROM treatment_decisions WHERE created_at >= now() - interval '{window}'` (decisions.py:436-437), suppression (444-447), byAction (456-458), byMode (466-467) and outcomes (475-476) are all unfiltered, and the route exposes no includeSimulated parameter (main.py:4782-4789). metrics.report by contrast builds `modes = ["shadow", "live"] + (["simulated"] if include_simulated else [])` and defaults include_simulated to False (metrics.py:506-508, main.py:4795), as does monitor.report (monitor.py:503). InsightsTab renders both on one screen — `useTreatmentInsights(days)` and `useTreatmentMetrics(days)` (treatment.lazy.tsx:340-341) — so the Decisions / Actionable / Coverage / Borrowers / Expected value tiles (355-363) count simulated-corpus rows while the Causal, Efficiency, Borrower-experience and Capacity panels directly beneath them (462-596) do not.

**Impact.** The simulated corpus is written by scripts/simulate_treatment_corpus.py and is large by design — the artifacts on disk report n of 5,256, 3,668 and 14,331. If any of it is in the window, the top of the Insights tab reports a decision volume and a coverage rate that no panel below it agrees with, and the Mode split BarList sprouts a 'Simulated' bar with no explanation of why the scoreboard beneath ignores it. A collections head quoting 'the engine made N decisions this fortnight at X% coverage' is quoting a figure that includes synthetic traffic, and there is no toggle and no on-screen statement of which population either half used.

**Fix.** Give /treatment/insights the same includeSimulated parameter and the same `mode = ANY(:modes)` filter the other two endpoints use, defaulting to shadow+live, and echo the effective mode list in the response so the console can state the population it is reporting on. Surface one includeSimulated control in the page header that drives all three queries together.

### `nba-engine-down-looks-identical-to-engine-up` — Client-derived fallback recommendations render as authoritative engine output, and the 'unavailable' notice sinks to the bottom

**Habibi/src/components/customer360/NextBestActionCard.tsx:62** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

Card header: `<div className="text-body-small text-text-subtlest">Ranked for this account right now</div>`. On the fallback path (api/customers.ts:44-58) `deriveCustomerInsights` produces items with no `source` and no `advisory`, so neither chip at NextBestActionCard.tsx:75-78 renders. Worse, the fallback's own warning `{ id: "nba-engine-unavailable", ... priority: "low" }` (customerInsights.ts:269-278) is then re-sorted by `p[a.priority] - p[b.priority]` (customerInsights.ts:338-341), so it drops below every high/medium case-handling item and the PRIMARY card becomes e.g. 'Review open dispute before hard collect'.

**Impact.** During a treatment-engine outage, a backend 500, or a ResponseValidationError, the floor keeps seeing a confident ranked 'Next best action' generated by five if-statements in the browser, and the only disclosure is a grey low-priority row near the bottom of the list — which `.slice(0, 5)` can drop entirely. In a bank this is a model-governance breach: recommendations attributed to a validated engine are actually produced by unvalidated client code, with no audit trail and no decision id.

**Fix.** Give NextBestActionCard the same explicit state prop OverviewTab already uses for authority ('unavailable' | 'pending' | 'ready', OverviewTab.tsx:31-35). In 'unavailable', render a SectionMessage banner across the whole card ('Decision engine unreachable — case handling only'), suppress the 'Next best action' framing, and never rank a fallback item as #1. Pin the engine-unavailable notice above the sort rather than sorting it by priority.

### `nba-scheduled-at-dropped` — The engine's recommended contact TIME is never shown, though 'when' is half the decision

**Habibi/src/components/customer360/NextBestActionCard.tsx:80** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

The primary block renders only `{primary.title}` (line 80) and `{primary.reason}` (line 82). `scheduledAt` (customerInsights.ts:44, populated from `treatment.get("at")` at customer_insights.py:224) is never rendered anywhere in Habibi/src/components. The timing model (models/treatment_timing.json, AUC .81) exists precisely to pick this hour.

**Impact.** The engine chooses an action AND an hour, constrained by the RBI 08:00-19:00 window and the borrower's reachability. Suppressing the hour means the agent picks their own, which discards the timing model's entire contribution and can put the contact outside the statutory window. It also makes the 'callback'/'schedule' recommendations meaningless — the time IS the recommendation.

**Fix.** Render `scheduledAt` as a formatted local time chip on the primary row ('Best time: today 15:00-16:00'), pass it through onAction so the callback/composer sheets pre-fill it, and mark a manually-chosen time as a timing override in the feedback payload.

### `nba-no-decision-feedback-loop` — The card never posts anything back against decisionId — the only human who sees the decision produces no label

**Habibi/src/components/customer360/NextBestActionCard.tsx:89** · statistics · missing-for-production · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

`onClick={() => onAction(primary.action)}` — the handler receives only an `NbaActionKind`. `primary.decisionId` (typed at customerInsights.ts:45 and populated by customer_insights.py:225) is never read by any component; grep for `decisionId` across Habibi/src/components returns hits only in OverviewTab/CustomerContextPanel for the AUTHORITY engine. There is no accept, no override, no 'why not' reason capture, and no dismiss.

**Impact.** The treatment corpus is 225 rows with 106 null outcomes, and the 84 'cancelled' outcomes come from enact.py aborting — not from a human. A system sold as self-improving has, at its one human touchpoint, a write-only display. Without an agent-accept/agent-override label the uplift model can never be fit on real data (it is currently fitted on `corpus: simulated`), the propensity logging cannot be validated against realised behaviour, and a model-risk reviewer has no evidence that the engine's recommendations were ever followed. Overrides are also the highest-signal training data the bank owns.

**Fix.** Add `onDecision(decisionId, verdict, reasonCode?)` to the card. Fire 'accepted' when the CTA is clicked, 'overridden' with a required reason code when the agent takes a different action on the same customer within the session, and 'dismissed' with a reason on an explicit dismiss control. POST to a new /treatment/decisions/{id}/feedback that writes agent_verdict, agent_user_id, reason_code and ts onto treatment_decisions. Mirror it for offer_decisions (which today has no propensity/policy_version/explore_kind columns at all).

### `board-subtotals-over-one-page` — Column counts and money subtotals are computed over one 200-row page and presented as stage totals

**Habibi/src/components/upsell/LeadBoard.tsx:42** · scale · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

`const subtotal = items.reduce((s, l) => s + leadValue(l), 0);` then rendered at :70 as `{items.length} · {fmtMoney(subtotal)}`. `items` comes from the `leads` prop = `filtered` = the raw result of GET /leads, which api/upsell.ts:160-166 requests with no limit/offset; db_core.py:211 clamps to DEFAULT_LIST_LIMIT=200. **Impact.** Past 200 leads the board's five column subtotals and the KPI strip's pipeline value disagree on one screen, with no caveat on the columns — the honest 'Showing N of M' caption (routes/upsell.tsx:186-188) sits in the header and does not reach the columns. On a real NBFC book (tens of thousands of leads) the board is a random 200-row sample presented as the pipeline, and stage columns are drawn from whatever the server's ORDER BY happened to return. There is also no pagination or virtualisation, so the fix is not merely cosmetic.

**Fix.** Take per-stage count and amount from GET /leads/metrics `perStage` (already in LeadMetrics, api/upsell.ts:180) for the column headers, and render the cards as a paged/virtualised window with an explicit 'showing 200 of 4,812 in this column' footer. Add a per-column offset query.

### `sheet-followup-default-lands-outside-the-calling-window` — The follow-up picker defaults to tomorrow at the current hour, has no min/max, and surfaces the policy rejection as a raw error string

**Habibi/src/components/upsell/LeadSheet.tsx:104** · compliance · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

`const [fuDate, setFuDate] = useState(() => { const d = new Date(); d.setDate(d.getDate() + 1); d.setMinutes(0, 0, 0); return d.toISOString().slice(0, 16); });` — the HOUR is left at 'now'. The input at :497-502 is `<input type="datetime-local" ...>` with no min, no max, no step and no window hint. The server does enforce it (db.py:5405-5416 -> `raise ValueError(f"contact_policy:{blocked}")`), and the failure reaches the agent as `toast.error(error.message)` (:130) = 'POST /leads/L-1/followups failed: contact_policy:outside_window'. The same codebase's callback sheet gets this right: NewCallbackSheet.tsx:62 uses `localTomorrowAt(11, 0)`.

**Impact.** An agent on an evening shift (very common in Indian collections) opens the drawer at 20:15 and the picker pre-fills 20:00 tomorrow, guaranteeing a rejection on the RBI 08:00-19:00 window that becomes binding 2027-01-01. The rejection reads as a system error, not a rule, so the agent will retry, escalate, or route around it — and nothing on screen tells them what the legal window even is.

**Fix.** Default to the next slot inside the window (reuse localTomorrowAt), set min/max on the input from a server-provided window, grey out disallowed hours, and map `contact_policy:*` errors to plain-language copy ('Cannot schedule at 20:00 — calls are permitted 08:00 to 19:00'). Ideally pre-fill from the treatment engine's timing model rather than a constant.

### `sheet-success-toast-before-the-write-lands` — Won, Lost, owner, team and follow-up-done all toast success synchronously, before the mutation resolves

**Habibi/src/components/upsell/LeadSheet.tsx:204** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

`leadMutation.mutate({ stage: "won", wonAmount: n }); setWonOpen(false); toast.success(`Marked won · ${fmtMoney(n)}`);` (lines 202-204). The same pattern at :212-214 (lost), :368-369 (owner), :387-390 (team) and :569-570 (follow-up done). The mutation's own onError (:123) then fires a SECOND toast, so a failed write shows 'Marked won · ₹15.00 L' AND 'PATCH /leads/L-1 failed: …'. Contrast doStage at :161-164, which correctly puts its toast in `{ onSuccess: ... }`.

**Impact.** The agent's confirmation that a disbursement was booked is not evidence it was booked. The drawer closes (setWonOpen(false) runs first), the card visually stays where it was, and the two contradictory toasts stack. In a bank this is the difference between a lead recorded as won and a lead lost from the book with the agent believing otherwise — and the follow-up case is worse: markLeadFollowUpDone throws 'Follow-up id missing' outright in live mode when the API omits ids (api/upsell.ts:293), after the success toast has already claimed it was marked done.

**Fix.** Move every one of these into the mutation's onSuccess callback, as doStage already does. Keep the drawer/section open until the write confirms, and disable the confirm buttons while isPending.

### `ohp-zero-responses-invisible` — The 'dark engine' guard covers zero decisions but not zero outcomes — a permanently broken feedback loop stays green

**Habibi/src/components/upsell/OfferHealthPanel.tsx:46** · observability · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

With one decision in the window this panel shows a green 'mode · live', a green 'p99 in budget', and dashes in the funnel, which reads as 'quiet week' rather than 'the outcome pipeline has never worked'.

**Fix.** Add a second darkness test — presented > 0 && responded === 0 over the window — and surface it as a server-side alert ('no offer outcome has ever been recorded; the engine cannot learn'). Render responseRate and declineRate as tiles. Show days-since-last-response next to lastDecisionAt.

### `ohp-no-arm-no-scorer-no-variant` — The panel shows mode but hides scorer, A/B split and byVariant — so every rate on it is uncontrolled and nothing says so

**Habibi/src/components/upsell/OfferHealthPanel.tsx:78** · statistics · missing-for-production · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

Established state: RECO_SCORER unset -> RuleScorer, RECO_AB_SPLIT unset -> no holdout arm, and observability.py:249 filters `d.variant IS NOT NULL`, so byVariant is empty by construction.

**Impact.** A collections head reads 'Interest 16.3%' and 'coverage +2.0%' as evidence the recommender is working. With no control arm those numbers measure the book, not the engine, and the panel offers no way to discover that. The treatment engine at least logs a null_treatment control arm (97 of 225 rows); the offer engine has none, and the health panel is where that should be impossible to miss.

**Fix.** Render an 'Experiment' row: scorer name, A/B split (or a red 'no control arm — deltas are not attributable' lozenge when abSplit is empty), and the byVariant table with per-arm coverage and interest rate. Make an empty abSplit an alert from the server, not a silent omission.

### `ohp-rates-without-denominators` — Rates render to one decimal place with no sample size, and the Interest tile's hint is not its denominator

**Habibi/src/components/upsell/OfferHealthPanel.tsx:110** · statistics · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

`<Metric label="Interest" value={<Rate value={data.funnel.interestRate} />} hint={`${data.volume.customers} customers`} />`. observability.py:465 computes `interestRate = _ratio(interested, presented)` — the denominator is `presented`, not `customers`. Meanwhile `latency.samples` (api/offer-health.ts:66) is never rendered beside the p99 badge, and `fmtRate(value, digits = 1)` prints '33.3%' for 1-of-3 as readily as for 1000-of-3000.

**Impact.** offer_decisions holds 16 rows lifetime with 0 responses ever. On this book the panel can print a one-decimal interest rate from a denominator of two while captioning it with an unrelated customer count. Anyone reading the tile computes the wrong confidence and the wrong denominator at once. Model-risk sign-off on a rate with no n is not obtainable.

**Fix.** Make the hint the actual denominator ('of 41 presented'). Suppress the rate and show 'n too small (n=2)' below a configured minimum. Render `latency.samples` next to the p99 badge.

### `nba-treatment-snapshot-never-rendered` — Alternatives, excluded reasons, propensity and policy version are computed, typed and thrown away

**Habibi/src/lib/customerInsights.ts:93** · observability · missing-for-production · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

`export type TreatmentSnapshot = { ... propensity?: number | null; policyVersion?: number | null; variant?: string | null; latencyMs?: number | null; alternatives?: TreatmentAlternative[]; excluded?: Record<string, string>; }` at lines 93-112, documented at :89-92 as 'what a supervisor overriding the decision needs, and they are already computed server-side'. backend/schemas.py:357-387 ships all of it. No component reads `insights.treatment`.

**Impact.** This is the explainability payload a model-risk function will ask for on day one, and it is already free. Its absence also hides the single most important fact in the established corpus: represent_mandate has been excluded on all 225 decisions (124 no_mandate_on_file, 97 control_arm). `excluded` would have shown that on every card from day one; instead it took a database query. The same blindness will hide the next systematically-vetoed action.

**Fix.** Add a collapsible 'Why this?' section to NextBestActionCard fed by `insights.treatment`: the top three alternatives with their expectedValue/pReach/pResolve/cost, the `excluded` map rendered as 'action — veto reason', and a footer line with decisionId, policyVersion, variant and propensity. Gate the numeric internals behind the supervisor role; show the excluded reasons to everyone.

### `nba-engine-vocabulary-is-a-dead-end` — Every action the treatment engine can actually recommend falls through to 'coming soon'

**Habibi/src/routes/customers.$customerId.lazy.tsx:202** · integration · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

`} else toast.info("Opens Callback Manager — coming soon.");` — the else arm of onNbaAction (lines 184-203) catches `callback, message, mandate, schedule, plan, field, legal, wait`. Cross-referenced with backend/customer_insights.py:134-148, the treatment engine's ten actions map to: mandate (represent_mandate), schedule (emi_date_change), plan (self_service_plan), message (sms, whatsapp), field (field_visit), legal (legal_notice), wait (wait) — seven of ten land in 'coming soon'. Only voice_bot/human_call -> 'call' opens a real sheet, and that sheet (setSheet("call")) merely LOGS a call after the fact; it does not place one.

**Impact.** The treatment engine is live (TREATMENT_MODE=live, 201 live decisions) and its rank-1 recommendation on Customer 360 is unactionable for seven of its ten actions. An agent clicks a bold 'Take action' button under a recommendation worth a stated rupee amount and is told a feature is coming soon. On a real book this trains the floor to ignore the card within a week, and it guarantees the corpus's 106 null outcomes stay null because no human action is ever taken through the surface that shows the decision.

**Fix.** Make the handler total over NbaActionKind (a `switch` with no default, so a new engine action is a compile error like ACTION_ICON already is). Wire each arm to a real destination: message -> the outbound composer with the engine's channel and template pre-filled; schedule -> the EMI-date-change request flow; plan -> self-service plan issuance; field -> field-visit allocation with the RBI prior-intimation record; legal -> the legal-notice queue with a maker-checker gate; mandate -> re-presentment; callback -> Callback Manager with the engine's `scheduledAt` pre-filled. Where a destination genuinely does not exist yet, do not render an enabled CTA — render a disabled button with the specific reason.

### `board-drop-to-won-fabricates-a-disbursed-amount` — Dragging a card into the Won column books an indicative estimate as the won amount — zero when the estimate is null

**Habibi/src/routes/upsell.tsx:125** · data-model · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

`wonAmount: next === "won" ? moneyValue(lead.estimatedValue) : undefined,` — reached from LeadBoard's drop handler (LeadBoard.tsx:52-57 -> onDropStage -> routes/upsell.tsx:136-149; 'won' is a droppable column because STAGE_ORDER includes it, upsell-seed.ts:954). `moneyValue` returns 0 for null (upsell-seed.ts:127-129) and `Lead.estimatedValue` is explicitly `number | null` (api/types/upsell.ts:86, 'Null when the product has no ticket band'). The same app's drawer path refuses to proceed without a typed disbursed amount: LeadSheet.tsx:196-201 `if (!n || n <= 0) { toast.error("Enter disbursed amount"); return; }`.

**Impact.** Two paths to the same terminal state, one of which fabricates the money. A drag books the marketing estimate as revenue, or books ₹0 when there was no ticket band, and both flow straight into 'Won (7d)' amount, pipeline value, conversionRate and any downstream incentive or cross-sell MIS. In a bank, a booked disbursement figure that nobody typed is a data-integrity finding, and ₹0 wins silently corrupt the conversion denominator forever because there is no way to tell them from real ones.

**Fix.** Make the Won column reject drops the same way the Lost column already does (routes/upsell.tsx:144-148): open the drawer and require an explicit disbursed amount. Never derive wonAmount from estimatedValue anywhere.

### `elig-unknown-persisted-as-failed` — lead_eligibility drops `status` and `blocking`, so every non-blocking 'unknown' check is stored and displayed as a failure

**backend/capture.py:1116** · data-model · defect · unverified (verifier-added) · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

evaluate_product_eligibility emits honest-unknown flags with `"blocking": False, "passed": False, "status": "unknown"` — capture.py:636-646 (KYC current, 'KYC status not captured on profile - skipped (unknown)') and :647-657 (Bureau score). insert_lead_eligibility then persists only six columns: `INSERT INTO lead_eligibility (id, lead_id, rule_id, label, passed, reason, created_at)` (capture.py:1116-1117) with `"passed": bool(flag.get("passed"))` at :1130 — `status`, `blocking` and `code` are discarded. db.py:2714 reads them back as `SELECT lead_id, label, passed AS ok, reason AS detail`, and LeadSheet.tsx:119 computes `const failing = useMemo(() => lead.eligibilityFlags.filter((f) => !f.ok), [lead]);`. The backend itself insists on the distinction at capture.py:1136-1143: 'Hard-block only on explicit fail of a blocking rule. Unknown never blocks.'

**Impact.** Every lead carries at least two unknown flags by construction, so LeadSheet's eligibility banner at :442-450 always reads 'N flags need review before disbursement' and the green 'All eligibility checks passed' at :443-445 is unreachable on live data — each unknown also draws a red XCircle at :476-480 on an amber card. The agent cannot distinguish a consent/DND block (which stops the contact) from an uncaptured bureau score (which does not), so the tab degrades to permanent cry-wolf and the compliance signal it exists to carry is lost. The same distinction is modelled correctly one screen away in the offer-health payload (`eligibility: {flags, unknown, failed, unknownRate}`, api/offer-health.ts:105-110, observability.py:516-521), which is evidence the fidelity loss is accidental. It also refutes the 'stale green shield' premise of the reader's sheet-revalidate-is-advisory-only.

**Fix.** Add `status` and `blocking` columns to lead_eligibility, persist them in insert_lead_eligibility, surface them on LeadResponse.eligibilityFlags, and render three states in the drawer — pass / unknown (grey, 'not captured') / blocking failure (red) — counting only blocking failures in the banner and in `failing.length`. Add a test asserting that a lead with only unknown flags renders as eligible.

### `bounce-voice-starves-treatment-queues` — One bounce dial per worker tick, and it short-circuits every treatment queue below it

**backend/bot_worker.py:107** · scale · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W01-triggers`

`if _run_stage("bounce_voice", lambda: payment_events.process_one_voice(db.engine)): return True` (bot_worker.py:107), above call_closer (114), cadence (119), campaigns (121), treatment_enact (126), treatment_followthrough (131) and treatment_sweep (138). process_one_voice returns True whenever it claimed a row (payment_events.py:962), and it holds the transaction open across the synchronous carrier dial.

**Impact.** At 08:00 the overnight backlog of scheduled bounce dials is drained one per tick, each returning True, so treatment_enact and treatment_followthrough never run while the backlog lasts. Plans whose moment has arrived are not enacted and outcomes are not attributed — precisely during the busiest hour. The single-process, single-threaded worker means dial latency directly sets the throughput of every other queue.

**Fix.** Move all carrier dialling into its own worker/process with its own concurrency, or make process_one_voice non-short-circuiting (drain a bounded batch, return False). At minimum, do not hold a DB transaction across the carrier call.

### `hold-active-flag-lies` — The `active` field returned to the UI ignores starts_at and expires_at

**backend/db_treatment_holds.py:116** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W01-triggers`

`"active": r["released_at"] is None` (db_treatment_holds.py:116) and `"active": row["released_at"] is None` (line 279), while the same function's active_only filter uses the full predicate `h.released_at IS NULL AND h.starts_at <= now() AND (h.expires_at IS NULL OR h.expires_at > now())` (71-74). GET /treatment/holds accepts activeOnly=false (main.py:4830).

**Impact.** The two answers disagree inside one function. On the customer 360 with activeOnly=false, a future-dated or long-expired hold renders as active, so a supervisor deciding whether they may call this borrower reads a green flag that the engine does not honour. Either direction of the disagreement causes a wrong human decision about contacting a protected borrower.

**Fix.** Compute `active` from the same predicate in SQL (`(h.released_at IS NULL AND h.starts_at <= now() AND (h.expires_at IS NULL OR h.expires_at > now())) AS active`) and return `releasedAt`/`expiresAt` alongside so the UI can explain why.
