The only stage-change affordance is the drag/drop pair at LeadBoard.tsx:46-57 plus `draggable` on LeadCard (LeadCard.tsx:49-53). The columns are plain divs with no role/aria-label, the cards carry no aria-grabbed or move menu, and there is no Escape/arrow-key alternative.

**Impact.** Indian bank and PSU procurement routinely requires WCAG/GIGW conformance, and a collections floor includes users who cannot drag accurately for a full shift. The drawer's stage stepper (LeadSheet.tsx:288-302) is the only accessible path, and it is two clicks deep with no discoverability from the board.

**Fix.** Add a per-card 'Move to…' menu (keyboard reachable) that calls the same onDropStage, give columns role="list" with aria-labels, and announce moves via a live region.

### `sheet-stale-offer-fields-lost-update` — Offer editor state initialises once and never resyncs, so Save offer can overwrite another user's edit

**Habibi/src/components/upsell/LeadSheet.tsx:94** · data-model · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

`const [productId, setProductId] = useState(lead.offer.productId);` plus :95-96 for amount and roi, and :99 for wonAmt. Only fuChannel has a resync effect (:115-117). routes/upsell.tsx:228 renders `<LeadSheet lead={openLead} ... />` with no `key`, and openLead is re-derived from a refetched list (:91), so the component receives new props and keeps stale local state. There is no version/ETag on the PATCH (api/upsell.ts:236-249) and no If-Match header.

**Impact.** Two supervisors with the same lead open: A changes the indicative amount, B — whose drawer has been open since before A's change — clicks Save offer and silently reverts it, with no conflict and no audit signal beyond an offer_edited event. On a shared collections floor with a single lead pool this is routine, not exotic.

**Fix.** Key the drawer on lead.id and reset the editor state from props whenever lead.updatedAt changes; or better, add an updatedAt/version column, send it on PATCH, and return 409 on mismatch so the drawer can show 'this lead changed while you were editing'.

### `sheet-datetime-local-assumes-browser-tz-is-bank-tz` — The follow-up instant is computed from the browser's timezone, while the calling window is enforced in IST

**Habibi/src/components/upsell/LeadSheet.tsx:183** · correctness · hidden-assumption · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

`at: new Date(fuDate).toISOString(),` — `fuDate` comes from a `datetime-local` input, which carries no offset, so `new Date()` interprets it in the BROWSER's local timezone. The server's window check (db.py:5410-5416 -> contact_policy) reasons in IST (db_core.py exports `_IST`). Nothing in the UI states which timezone the displayed time is in.

**Impact.** Holds today because every workstation is on IST. It breaks for an offshore or BPO agent desk, a VDI image left on UTC, or a laptop whose clock a user changed: the agent picks 15:00, the system books 20:30 IST, and the RBI window check is applied to an instant the agent never saw. The same assumption sits in the display path (`fmtDateTime` uses `toLocaleString(undefined, ...)`, upsell-seed.ts:140-147).

**Fix.** Render and accept times explicitly in the bank's operating timezone with the label on screen ('15:00 IST'), convert in one place, and have the server echo back the interpreted instant so the confirmation shows what was actually booked.

### `sheet-won-amount-unvalidated` — The disbursed amount accepts any positive number with no sanity band and no comparison to the offer

**Habibi/src/components/upsell/LeadSheet.tsx:197** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

`const n = Number(wonAmt); if (!n || n <= 0) { toast.error("Enter disbursed amount"); return; }` — that is the entire validation. The input is a plain text `<Input>` (:619-623), so '150000' and '1500000' differ by one keystroke, and neither is checked against `lead.offer.indicativeAmount` or the product's minTicket/maxTicket (both available: Product carries them at api/types/upsell.ts:18-19).

**Impact.** A single mistyped zero moves pipeline value, 'Won (7d) amount' and every conversion figure by an order of magnitude, with no confirmation step and no reviewer. Collections MIS is reported upward from these numbers.

**Fix.** Use a numeric input with grouping, show the indicative amount beside it, and require an explicit confirm when the entered figure is outside the product's ticket band or differs from the indicative amount by more than a configured factor.

### `sheet-not-a-dialog` — The drawer is a bare div with a backdrop click-to-close: no role, no focus trap, no Escape, and it discards typed input

**Habibi/src/components/upsell/LeadSheet.tsx:218** · ux · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

`<div className="fixed inset-0 z-50 flex justify-end bg-black/30" onClick={onClose}>` — no role="dialog", no aria-modal, no aria-labelledby, no focus management, no keydown handler for Escape. Clicking anywhere outside the panel calls onClose immediately, including while the Loss-reason input (:642-647) or the follow-up note (:514-520) holds unsaved text. The rest of the app uses a real Dialog primitive (components/ui/dialog, imported by routes/treatment.lazy.tsx:33).

**Impact.** Keyboard and screen-reader users cannot escape or navigate the drawer, and focus stays behind it on the page underneath — a straightforward accessibility conformance failure in a procurement review. Operationally, a mis-click while typing a loss reason silently discards it, and the agent re-types or gives up and writes something useless, degrading the loss-reason data that routes/upsell.tsx:140-143 went out of its way to protect.

**Fix.** Use the existing Dialog/Sheet primitive: role=dialog, aria-modal, labelled by the customer name, focus trap, Escape to close, and a confirm-on-dismiss when a form field is dirty.

### `sheet-raw-transcript-on-a-shared-surface` — Verbatim call transcript snippets render unredacted next to the customer's name on a board anyone with lead access can open

**Habibi/src/components/upsell/LeadSheet.tsx:318** · privacy · missing-for-production · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

`“{lead.transcriptSnippet}”` at :317-319, with `{lead.customerName}` at :231 and `#{lead.accountTail}` at :254 on the same header. The same snippet is rendered on every card on the open board (LeadCard.tsx:93-95). No redaction pass is applied anywhere in this component, though the repo has one (Habibi/src/api/redaction.ts, components/redaction/).

**Impact.** A transcript snippet captured mid-collections-call can contain salary, health, family or other DPDP-sensitive personal data, and here it is displayed beside an identifiable customer on a screen that is routinely projected in floor huddles and screen-shared to team leads. There is also no field-level access control on this drawer and no record that the snippet was viewed.

**Fix.** Route transcriptSnippet through the existing redaction pipeline before display, mask by default with a role-gated 'reveal' that writes an access-audit row, and truncate to the consent-relevant clause rather than free text.

### `sheet-owner-select-misreports-the-owner` — An owner absent from the live staff roster silently displays as whoever is first in the list

**Habibi/src/components/upsell/LeadSheet.tsx:366** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

`<select value={lead.owner ?? "Unassigned"} ...>` with options from `leadOwnerOptions(staff)` = `[...humanNames(staff), "Unassigned"]` (api/upsell.ts:75-78). A React select whose `value` matches no option renders the first option. The same class of bug on the Team select at :385 (`value={lead.team ?? ""}` — the empty string matches no option in teamNames(teams)).

**Impact.** A lead owned by someone who has left the bank, been deactivated, or been assigned by a bot displays as owned by the alphabetically-first active rep. Ownership drives queue routing, incentive attribution and accountability in a collections org; a silently wrong owner is worse than a blank. The drawer's own comment (:84-86) records that this exact area already shipped a live-mode bug once.

**Fix.** Detect the mismatch and prepend a disabled option ('Priya Nair (no longer active)') so the current value renders truthfully, or show a warning lozenge. Do the same for team.

### `sheet-priority-looks-interactive-and-is-not` — Priority is rendered as a segmented control that cannot be changed, and no API accepts a priority change

**Habibi/src/components/upsell/LeadSheet.tsx:407** · ux · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

Three Lozenges with the unselected ones at `opacity-60` (`className={cn("capitalize", lead.priority !== p && "opacity-60")}`, :412) — the exact visual language the file's own stage picker uses for a real segmented control (:74-80, with a comment explaining the styling choice). They have no onClick. `patchLead`'s patch type (api/upsell.ts:212-220) has no `priority` field at all.

**Impact.** Priority sorts the board (LeadBoard.tsx:36-37) and the table (routes/upsell.tsx:155-156), so it drives what the floor works first — and it is frozen at capture with no way for a supervisor to change it. Agents will click the greyed lozenges, nothing will happen, and the workaround is to not trust the priority ordering at all.

**Fix.** Either make it a real control (add priority to the PATCH contract and the endpoint) or restyle it as a static read-only chip with a 'set at capture' caption. Do not ship a control that looks selectable and is not.

### `metrics-no-minimum-n` — 'Conversion (30d)' is printed as a whole-percent rate with no minimum sample size

**Habibi/src/components/upsell/MetricsStrip.tsx:76** · statistics · hidden-assumption · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

`value={m?.conversionRate == null ? "—" : `${m.conversionRate}%`}` — no n guard. The denominator is captured30d, which on the established book (~20 customers, 16 offer decisions lifetime) is a single-digit number.

**Impact.** One won lead out of three captured prints '33%' with the same visual weight as a rate over 3,000. Collections MIS gets reported upward from tiles like this. On a 20-customer pilot every number on this strip is noise presented as signal.

**Fix.** Suppress the percentage below a configurable minimum denominator and render 'n=3' instead. Show a Wilson interval, or at minimum the denominator, in the sub-line at all times.

### `ohp-error-state-collapses-every-failure` — 403, 404, 500 and a dead network all render one sentence with no retry

**Habibi/src/components/upsell/OfferHealthPanel.tsx:32** · observability · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

`if (isError || !data) { return (<div ...>Offer-engine health unavailable.</div>); }` — the caught error is discarded. api/config.ts:134-141 defines `ApiError` carrying `status`, `detail` and `path` precisely so callers can distinguish these, and its docstring (config.ts:118-133) names 'absence and failure rendered identically, and always as absence' as the codebase's #1 failure mode. GET /offers/health requires ANALYTICS_READ (backend/authz.py:267), so an agent without that scope sees the same sentence as an outage.

**Impact.** An SRE paged about 'the offer panel is blank' cannot tell from the screen whether the backend is down, the analytics query timed out, or the user simply lacks a scope. In a bank the scope case is the common one and it will be reported as an outage.

**Fix.** Branch on ApiError.status: 401/403 -> 'You do not have analytics access'; 404 -> 'This build has no /offers/health endpoint'; 5xx/network -> the error detail plus a Retry button that calls refetch().

### `ohp-thresholds-in-the-component` — A 25-second AHT threshold lives in a className ternary, contradicting the module's own contract

**Habibi/src/components/upsell/OfferHealthPanel.tsx:124** · observability · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

`(data.guardrails.ahtDeltaSec ?? 0) > 25 ? "text-text-warning" : "text-text"` — while api/offer-health.ts:8-11 states 'Thresholds are NOT evaluated here... because a threshold that lives in a chart config is a threshold nobody reviews'. The AHT-delta guardrail produces no server-side alert at all (observability.py:388-442 has no AHT alert), so 25s is the only AHT threshold in the system and it exists solely as a text colour.

**Impact.** Average handle time is the guardrail that decides whether upselling during a collections call is costing the contact centre money. Its only threshold is invisible to configuration, to the weekly report and to any reviewer who does not read TSX. It will be silently wrong for a different bank's call profile, and nobody will notice because it changes a font colour.

**Fix.** Move the AHT-delta budget to observability.py alongside LATENCY_P99_BUDGET_MS, emit it as a real `alerts` entry with a severity, and let the panel colour from the alert rather than from a local number. Do the same for `dark` (line 46) — it belongs in the payload as an engine-state field.

### `ohp-alerts-have-no-severity` — An informational 'RECO_MODE=shadow' notice wears the same warning triangle as a latency breach

**Habibi/src/components/upsell/OfferHealthPanel.tsx:154** · ux · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

`{alerts.map((a) => (<li key={a.metric} className="flex items-start gap-075 text-body-small text-text-warning"><AlertTriangle .../>...`. `OfferHealthAlert` is `{ metric, message }` only (api/offer-health.ts:20-23). observability.py:442 emits `alert("engine", "RECO_MODE=shadow — decisions are scored and logged but never spoken")` with the source comment 'Not a fault. Stated anyway' — and it renders in amber with a warning triangle, identical to :405's p99 budget breach.

**Impact.** Alert fatigue on the one panel that is supposed to distinguish a healthy engine from a dead one. The collapsed header lozenge just counts them ('3 alerts'), so a floor lead sees the same count whether the engine is fine-and-shadowed or breaching its latency budget.

**Fix.** Add `severity: 'info' | 'warn' | 'critical'` to the OfferHealthAlert contract, set it at each emit site in observability.py, and render tone and icon from it. Count only warn/critical in the collapsed header lozenge.

### `tuner-merges-two-engines-under-one-heading` — Reco and treatment knobs are concatenated into one unlabelled list, captioned with only the reco engine's note

**Habibi/src/components/upsell/OfferHealthPanel.tsx:187** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

`const items = [...reco, ...treatment];` (line 187) where `reco = tuner?.copyToEnv` and `treatment = tuner?.treatment?.copyToEnv` (185-186). The strip is titled 'Shadow tuner' inside a panel headed 'Offer engine · 30d' (line 64), and its provenance caption is `{tuner?.note ?? "loading"}` (line 193) — the RECO note only. `tuner.treatment.note` and both `evidence` blocks are never rendered.

**Impact.** agent_core/tuner.py:134-137 raises TREATMENT_FATIGUE_COST and TREATMENT_FIELD_DIGITAL_EXHAUSTION with note='high_field_share', derived from treatment_decisions. Meanwhile the reco tuner independently returns note='insufficient_log' from offer_decisions. The panel then displays `TREATMENT_FATIGUE_COST=12.0 (now 10.0)` captioned 'insufficient_log', under a heading that says 'Offer engine'. An operator copying that line into env is changing how often the collections engine sends a field agent to a borrower's home — on evidence the screen has attributed to the wrong engine and the wrong verdict. Field visits are the most physically intrusive action in the whole system and carry an RBI prior-intimation obligation from 2027-01-01.

**Fix.** Split the strip into two labelled groups ('Offer engine (RECO_*)' and 'Collections treatment engine (TREATMENT_*)'), each with its own note and its own evidence line (presented/declined/days vs actionable/fieldVisits/days). Better still: move the treatment tuner onto the treatment console and leave this panel single-engine.

### `tuner-says-loading-forever-on-error` — A failed tuner query renders 'loading' permanently and the list falsely reads 'No weight changes suggested'

**Habibi/src/components/upsell/OfferHealthPanel.tsx:193** · reliability · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

`<span className="text-body-tiny text-text-subtle">{tuner?.note ?? "loading"}</span>` — only `tuner.data` is passed into TunerStrip (line 167: `<TunerStrip tuner={tuner.data} />`); `tuner.isError` and `tuner.isPending` are discarded. On error `data` stays undefined, so `items` is `[]` and line 196-198 renders 'No weight changes suggested.' beside the word 'loading'.

**Impact.** The absence-vs-failure bug the codebase explicitly hunts (api/config.ts:118-133), reproduced here. An operator concludes the tuner has nothing to suggest when in fact the endpoint is failing.

**Fix.** Pass the whole query result into TunerStrip and render three states. On error show the ApiError detail with a Retry.

### `nba-loading-renders-derived-list` — Every page load flashes a browser-derived recommendation before the engine's arrives

**Habibi/src/routes/customers.$customerId.lazy.tsx:114** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

`const insights = insightsQuery.data ?? deriveCustomerInsights(customer);` — `insightsQuery.isPending` is never consulted. During the first fetch the NBA card is fully populated from the offline builder, including the 'Recommendation unavailable' row, and then silently swaps to the engine's ranking when the query resolves.

**Impact.** On a slow branch link an agent reads and acts on the pre-engine list. Two agents on the same account can act on different #1 recommendations depending on network timing, and neither is recorded. It also masks a genuinely failing endpoint: a permanently-pending query and a healthy one both render content.

**Fix.** Render a skeleton while `insightsQuery.isPending`. Use the derived list only when `insightsQuery.isError`, and pass state='unavailable' with it.

### `hold-active-predicate-has-four-variants` — Four different SQL definitions of an active hold, and the authority matrix uses a fifth-of-a-rule that ignores starts_at

**backend/agent_core/authority/features.py:139** · maintainability · defect · unverified (verifier-added) · reader `W01-triggers`

The reader identified three consumers agreeing on `released_at IS NULL AND starts_at <= now() AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > now())`, but the authority matrix does not agree: agent_core/authority/features.py:139-146 reads `WHERE customer_id = :cid AND released_at IS NULL AND (account_id IS NULL OR account_id = :aid) AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > now())` — no starts_at clause. Alongside it sit agent_core/treatment/policy.py:513-521 and agent_core/treatment/features.py:1170-1180 (full predicate), db_treatment_holds.py:70-74 (full predicate for filtering) and db_treatment_holds.py:116 / :279 (`released_at IS NULL` alone for the reported flag), plus the dedupe SELECT at :153-166 and the unique index at sql/05_collections.sql:302-304 (both `released_at IS NULL` alone).

**Impact.** A future-dated hold — the natural way to express 'stop contact from Monday, when the bereavement leave starts' — is honoured by the authority matrix and ignored by nothing else, while an expired hold is honoured by the dedupe and the UI and ignored by the engine. Four definitions of one control mean no single answer to 'was this borrower protected at 14:00 on Tuesday', which is the question a conduct-risk reviewer asks and the question the hold table exists to answer. Every future change to hold semantics has to be made in six places or it drifts again.

**Fix.** Export one ACTIVE_HOLD_PREDICATE constant (or one `active_hold_kinds(conn, customer_id, account_id, at)` helper) from a single module and use it in all six sites, including the `active` field returned to the UI. Add a test that greps for `treatment_holds` in SQL across the backend and fails on any hand-rolled predicate.

### `statutory-allowed-when-customer-unreadable` — If the customer row cannot be read, admit() allows the statutory send rather than denying it

**backend/contact_policy.py:911** · compliance · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W01-triggers`

`customer = _load_customer(conn, cid); if customer is None: if purpose == "outreach": return Decision(False, REASON_NO_CUSTOMER, ...); return Decision(True, daily_cap=cap)` (contact_policy.py:910-914). Reached from payment_events._admit (line 585) and promise_fulfillment._admit_channel (595). Note the contrast with evaluate(), which fails closed on an exception: `return Decision(False, REASON_UNREADABLE, ...)` (contact_policy.py:592-594).

**Impact.** Fail-open on the path that skips DND, hours and cap. A customer row that is missing, soft-deleted, or invisible because of an RLS/tenant mismatch (see webhook-binds-no-tenant) is exactly the state in which we know least about consent — and it is the state in which the code decides to send anyway. Two defects on this surface compose into an unconsented send.

**Fix.** Fail closed for every purpose when the customer cannot be loaded; return a distinct reason ('customer_unreadable') so the suppression is visible rather than looking like an opt-out.

### `customer-360-decision-row-rolled-back` — The customer-360 treatment snapshot pays for a full decision and then silently discards the row it claims to be writing deliberately

**backend/db.py:960** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W01-triggers`

`with engine.connect() as conn:` (db.py:960) — not engine.begin() — wraps `treatment = _treatment_snapshot(conn, customer_id)` (968), whose docstring says '`recommend_treatment` writes a decision row, and that is deliberate' (991-994). SQLAlchemy 2.0.51 (requirements.txt:7) is commit-as-you-go: an implicit transaction on a Connection is rolled back at close. Contrast db_treatment_holds.next_treatment, which uses engine.begin() (line 302) and does commit.

**Impact.** Two costs. The stated design intent — build the shadow corpus from the questions people actually ask — is not delivered on the highest-traffic surface in the product, and nobody knows because the failure is silent. Meanwhile every customer-360 open runs the full feature build, candidate generation, veto ladder and scorer, and throws the result away, so page latency and DB load scale with a write that never lands. Two sibling call sites, identical docstrings, opposite behaviour, is also exactly the kind of inconsistency that makes an auditor distrust the rest.

**Fix.** Decide once. If inspection rows should exist, use engine.begin() and tag them decision_source='inspection' (see the previous finding). If they should not, delete the claim from the docstring and pass a read-only flag so the engine skips the log write entirely — and stop paying for a decision the page does not use.

### `hold-source-is-caller-asserted` — The caller declares who placed the hold, including source='regulator'

**backend/db_treatment_holds.py:143** · security · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W01-triggers`

`source = str(payload.get("source") or "manual").strip().lower()` validated only against HOLD_SOURCES (db_treatment_holds.py:143-145), and schemas.py:3332 exposes `source: Literal["manual","bot","system","regulator"] = "manual"` on the public POST body. Nothing correlates the claimed source with the authenticated actor (placed_by is filled separately from _actor_user_id(), line 193).

**Impact.** 'Who placed this hold' becomes self-reported. A hold claiming regulator provenance carries different escalation and different release rules, and here anyone with a write key can assert it — or, more likely in practice, a UI bug quietly mislabels every manual hold and the compliance report becomes meaningless.

**Fix.** Derive source from the authenticated actor kind (bot session -> 'bot', user session -> 'manual', internal job -> 'system') and allow 'regulator' only from a role that carries that authority. Keep the field non-nullable so the derivation is always recorded.

### `hold-expiry-untyped-and-unbounded` — expiresAt and slaDueAt are untyped strings passed straight to Postgres, with no bound and no review SLA enforcement

**backend/db_treatment_holds.py:196** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W01-triggers`

`"sla_due_at": payload.get("slaDueAt"), "expires_at": payload.get("expiresAt")` (db_treatment_holds.py:195-196), typed as `slaDueAt: str | None` / `expiresAt: str | None` in schemas.py:3335-3336. No validation that expires_at is in the future, no maximum duration, and nothing anywhere acts on sla_due_at.

**Impact.** A malformed string is a 500 rather than a 400. A hold created with expires_at in the past is inert the moment it is written while reading as active (see hold-active-flag-lies). And a hardship hold with expires_at NULL is a permanent stop on collections with an SLA field that nothing enforces — a borrower silently parked forever, which the collections head discovers as a hole in the book.

**Fix.** Type them as datetime in the request model, reject past values, cap the duration per kind (e.g. hardship 90 days) with an explicit renewal action, and add a worker that raises a work item when sla_due_at passes without release.

### `next-treatment-second-connection-for-contract` — next_treatment commits the decision, then builds its Action Contract on a second connection and swallows the failure

**backend/db_treatment_holds.py:324** · reliability · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W01-triggers`

The decision commits at db_treatment_holds.py:302-311; then `try: with engine.connect() as conn: contract = result.action_contract(conn=conn) except Exception: logger.exception(...); contract = result.action_contract()` (324-329). The fallback path drops the authority-matrix enrichment silently.

**Impact.** Two pooled connections per request on a pool of 5+10 (db_core.py:149-150) shared across uvicorn workers — a screen that polls this will exhaust the pool before anything else does. And a committed, actionable decision whose contract quietly lost its fee-waiver ceiling means the executing channel is authorised with a narrower envelope than the decision assumed, with only a log line to say so. The degradation direction is safe (concede less), but it is invisible to the operator.

**Fix.** Build the contract inside the same transaction as the decision, before commit. If it must degrade, put the degradation in the payload (`contractDegraded: true` plus the reason) so the channel and the supervisor can see it.

### `cases-never-close-on-cancelled` — list_treatment_cases only closes a case on paid or ptp, so cancelled and superseded cases accumulate forever

**backend/db_treatment_holds.py:369** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W01-triggers`

`"NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM treatment_decisions r WHERE ... AND r.outcome IN ('paid','ptp'))"` (db_treatment_holds.py:369-373). The live corpus has 84 'cancelled' and 4 'superseded' outcomes against 10 ptp and 7 paid (established fact) — cancelled is by far the most common terminal state, written by enact.py when enactment aborts.

**Impact.** The floor lead's open-case list is dominated by cases that can never progress: 84 of 108 outcomes are a state the view treats as still open. The screen that exists to answer 'what has been tried and what is left' becomes unusable at the first real book, and the team stops looking at it — which removes the only human check on the engine.

**Fix.** Close on any terminal outcome (paid, ptp, cancelled, superseded, refused, undeliverable) and add an explicit 'stalled' state for cases whose last decision was cancelled, so the 84 become a queue somebody owns rather than noise. Better: derive case state from a case table rather than re-deriving it by aggregate on every request.

### `emi-fallback-marks-a-future-instalment-overdue` — When no instalment is due by the event date, ingest attaches the bounce to the next future EMI and marks it overdue

**backend/payment_events.py:513** · correctness · defect · unverified (verifier-added) · reader `W01-triggers`

_resolve_emi's first fallback correctly bounds the search — `WHERE account_id = :aid AND status IN ('upcoming','partial') AND due_date <= :occurred ORDER BY due_date ASC LIMIT 1` (payment_events.py:497-510) — but when that returns nothing the second fallback drops the date predicate entirely: `WHERE account_id = :aid AND status IN ('upcoming','partial') ORDER BY due_date ASC LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE` (:513-526). ingest then treats that row as the bounced instalment: `if emi is not None and emi["status"] != "paid": UPDATE emi_installments SET status = 'overdue' WHERE id = :id AND status <> 'paid'` (:268-278), bumps `dpd = GREATEST(dpd, 1)` and sets bucket '0-30' (:284-294), writes emi_installment_id on the event (:352) and quotes that instalment's due_date in the borrower-facing copy (:570-576, via _bounce_copy at :162-165).

**Impact.** A bounce whose occurredAt is early or wrong — routine given occurred-at is unvalidated — or an event that arrives before any instalment has fallen due marks a not-yet-due EMI as overdue, advances DPD and bucket on a current account, and sends the borrower a demand naming a future due date they have not missed. DPD and bucket are the inputs to collections strategy and, in a bank, feed asset-classification reporting; silently ageing a current account on a data-quality event is the kind of thing an internal auditor treats as a control failure rather than a bug. It also consumes the account's one open-EMI slot (uq_payment_events_open_emi), so the genuine bounce on that instalment later hits the swallow path.

**Fix.** Return None from _resolve_emi when nothing is due by occurred_at rather than reaching forward, and let ingest record the bounce against the account with emi_installment_id NULL plus a data-quality work item. Never write status='overdue' on an instalment whose due_date is in the future.

### `admit-before-send-writes-phantom-contacts` — The contact ledger records an allowed WhatsApp contact that is then never sent, in both trigger paths

**backend/payment_events.py:603** · compliance · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W01-triggers`

payment_events.py:603-605 calls `_admit("whatsapp")` — which inserts an outcome='allowed' contact_events row and reserves a daily slot (contact_policy.py:977-998) — before the code checks whether a send is even possible. Only afterwards, at 628-664, does it discover the 24h service window is closed and no template is configured, and fall through to SMS at 657-662. The identical shape is in promise_fulfillment.py:607-618 (admit) versus 655-687 (service-window/template check).

**Impact.** contact_events is the record the bank produces when a borrower says 'you harassed me' or a regulator asks how often we contacted someone. It now contains WhatsApp contacts that never happened, plus the real SMS that did — over-reporting our own contact frequency in the one ledger that is read adversarially. It also burns a slot in the daily reservation, so genuine later outreach is capped earlier than the policy intends.

**Fix.** Decide first, admit last. Resolve channel viability (service window, template, phone) before calling admit, and call admit exactly once for the channel actually used. If a pre-check is needed, use contact_policy.evaluate (the non-reserving read at contact_policy.py:529) and keep admit for the moment of send.

### `no-clerk-job-cancellation-on-cure` — Curing a case supersedes un-enacted decisions but never cancels the clerk work item or an already-enacted scheduled plan

**backend/payments.py:268** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W01-triggers`

_close_treatment_cases calls followthrough.resolve_case only (payments.py:281-296), and resolve_case updates `WHERE ... AND outcome IS NULL AND enacted IS FALSE` (agent_core/treatment/followthrough.py:486-490). Nothing touches the work item created by enqueue_from_treatment (payment_events.py:452 / promise_fulfillment.py:842), and nothing revokes a decision that was already enacted and scheduled.

**Impact.** The borrower pays. The un-enacted plan is superseded, correctly — but the bounce_chase work item is still queued and an already-enacted plan (a scheduled dial, a queued WhatsApp job) still fires. So we still contact someone about a debt they have settled, which is the exact failure the surrounding code says it exists to prevent. On the hosted-pay-link path this is a bug; combined with the missing CBS credit feed it is the default behaviour.

**Fix.** Have resolve_case also cancel the work item by idempotency key and mark any enacted-but-not-yet-executed plan as revoked, and have the whatsapp/outbound drains re-check case state immediately before sending.

### `followup-id-single-shot-but-plan-recomputed` — The follow-up id is deterministic per promise, so a second break inserts nothing — but the decision and the clerk job are created anyway

**backend/promise_fulfillment.py:931** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W01-triggers`

`"id": f"FU-{row['id']}"` with `ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING` (promise_fulfillment.py:927, 931). `plan = _next_action(conn, row)` runs first (line 917) and unconditionally writes a treatment_decisions row and enqueues a clerk job (832-849).

**Impact.** A promise that breaks, is revived by a part payment or a supervisor, and breaks again produces a decision row and a clerk job but no visible follow-up task — the queue silently loses the second break while the corpus gains a decision whose consequence nobody can see. It also means the ON CONFLICT is doing double duty as both a retry guard and a business rule, and the two want different answers.

**Fix.** Generate a fresh followup id per break and de-duplicate on (promise_id, status='open') instead, or reopen the existing followup and append the new note. Either way, compute the plan after deciding whether a follow-up is actually needed.

### `sms-sent-inside-open-transaction` — The reminder drain calls Twilio inside the claiming transaction, so a commit failure re-sends the SMS

**backend/promise_fulfillment.py:1014** · reliability · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W01-triggers`

process_one_reminder opens `with engine.begin() as conn:` (promise_fulfillment.py:1046), claims the row FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, and calls `_send_reminder_copy` which does `twilio_sms.send(...)` at line 1014 — a network side effect — before the status UPDATE at 1068-1084 and the commit. The same pattern is in _first_touch's SMS branch (payment_events.py:670-677).

**Impact.** If the commit fails (connection drop, statement timeout, deadlock, worker kill) the SMS has gone out and the row is still 'queued'; the next tick sends it again. The borrower gets duplicate dunning messages, we pay twice, and the contact ledger under-reports because admit ran once. It also holds a row lock and a pooled connection across an external HTTP call, so a slow Twilio blocks the queue.

**Fix.** Two-phase it: claim and mark 'sending' in one transaction, send outside any transaction, record the result in a second transaction keyed on a provider idempotency key. Twilio supports client-supplied idempotency; use the reminder id.

### `contact-events-has-no-retention-or-partitioning` — An append-only ledger with four indexes, no partitioning and no retention policy

**backend/alembic/versions/20260813_0066_contact_events.py:115** · scale · missing-for-production · 1/1 confirm · reader `W02-contact-policy`

contact_events is a plain table with idx on tenant_id, (customer_id, occurred_at), (customer_id, session_key, occurred_at) and (customer_id, source, related_id) (lines 98-113), described as 'Append-only — no updated_at' (line 9). contact_day_counters likewise has no pruning (lines 115-126).

**Impact.** At a mid-size NBFC — 2 million delinquent accounts, several admits per account per day including denials — this is on the order of a billion rows a year across four indexes. The per-customer queries stay fast on the composite index, but ledger_usage's `customer_id = ANY(:ids)` with a large id list and the unbounded `DISTINCT ON (customer_id) ... WHERE outcome = 'denied'` (lines 1067-1077) degrade, vacuum and backup windows grow, and DPDP erasure has no mechanism at all. The dev book's handful of rows cannot show any of this.

**Fix.** Range-partition contact_events by occurred_at (monthly), add a retention rule resolved from policy_rules so the retention period is itself versioned and auditable, and bound the deny lookup in ledger_usage with an occurred_at predicate. Prune contact_day_counters beyond the weekly horizon.

### `no-whatsapp-session-window-or-template-gate` — The shared veto knows nothing about WhatsApp's 24-hour window, DLT templates, or NDNC categories

**backend/contact_policy.py:40** · compliance · missing-for-production · 1/1 confirm · reader `W02-contact-policy`

CHANNELS treats whatsapp, sms and email as interchangeable strings (line 40). The only session concept is `session_window()` = 30 minutes (line 120), used for coalescing, not for provider eligibility. There is no template check, no DLT entity/template id, no NDNC/TRAI preference category, and dnd_registry is a single boolean (line 293) OR-ed into REASON_CUSTOMER_DND (line 487).

**Impact.** TRAI DLT requires a registered template and header per SMS, and NDNC preferences are per-category and per-time-band, not a single flag. Meta requires an approved template outside the 24-hour customer-service window. A gate that says 'allowed' and hands the message to a provider that rejects it turns a compliance decision into a delivery failure with no policy record. The 16 offer_decisions and 0 responses in the corpus mean none of this has ever been exercised.

**Fix.** Model per-channel eligibility as its own rule kind: whatsapp needs last_inbound_at within 24h or an approved template id; sms needs a DLT template reference; email needs an unsubscribe basis. Return distinct reasons so the denial is attributable. Replace the dnd_registry boolean with a per-channel, per-category preference table.

### `product-scope-unreachable-from-the-gate` — _rules_for never passes product_id, so the product layer never resolves

**backend/contact_policy.py:88** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W02-contact-policy`

`return policy_rules.resolve(conn, tenant_id=customer.get("tenant_id"), at=at)` (line 88). resolve defaults product_id to None (policy_rules.py:301) and the SQL predicate is `(s.scope = 'product' AND s.tenant_id = :tid AND s.product_id = :pid)` (lines 348-349), which is never true when :pid is NULL.

**Impact.** Three scopes are documented and designed for (policy_rules.py:15-23); two work. A client who publishes a stricter window for, say, credit cards versus secured loans will see it accepted, versioned, shown in provenance tooling — and ignored by the gate. Silent non-enforcement of a published policy is the worst possible failure mode for a rules table.

**Fix.** Thread product_id (available on the account, and already passed to admit as account_id) through admit/evaluate into _rules_for. Until then, make resolve() log a warning when product-scope rows exist for the tenant but no product_id was supplied, so the gap is visible rather than silent.

### `unknown-channel-fails-open-into-its-own-budget` — normalize_channel passes through arbitrary strings and defaults None to 'voice'

**backend/contact_policy.py:143** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W02-contact-policy`

`ch = (raw or "").strip().lower(); if ch in {"call","voice","pstn"}: return "voice"; if ch in CHANNELS: return ch; return ch or "voice"` (lines 143-149). A typo like 'wa' or 'Whatsap' returns itself, unvalidated against CHANNELS.

**Impact.** An unrecognised channel gets its own weekly budget in _week_counted (which groups by the literal channel string, line 377), no statutory window (only 'voice' is special-cased at line 495), and no consent lookup match in _channel_status (line 308) — so it is admitted, uncapped and unvetted. The contact_events CHECK constraint would then reject the insert, sending the whole admit into the except handler and returning REASON_UNREADABLE, which masks a routing bug as a database error. Separately, `raw=None` silently becomes a voice dial — the most regulated channel chosen as the fallback.

**Fix.** Return a sentinel for unknown input and make _veto deny on it with a new REASON_UNKNOWN_CHANNEL, and make `raw=None` a denial rather than a voice dial. Assert `normalize_channel(x) in CHANNELS` at the top of admit and evaluate.

### `zone-python-and-sql-disagree` — _zone does not apply the parenthetical-strip rule that safe_tz_sql documents as shared

**backend/contact_policy.py:156** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W02-contact-policy`

`def _zone(name): label = (name or "").strip() or DEFAULT_TZ; try: return ZoneInfo(label) except ...: return ZoneInfo(DEFAULT_TZ)` (lines 156-161). safe_tz_sql's docstring claims 'Same policy as _zone, expressed once here so both paths agree' (line 180) and then implements `btrim(split_part(COALESCE(expr, ''), '(', 1))` (line 195) which _zone lacks. Seeded data stores 'Asia/Kolkata (IST)' (line 174-175).

**Impact.** For any non-IST borrower whose timezone carries a display suffix — an NRI book, a Gulf-remittance segment, a bank operating in Nepal or Sri Lanka — the gate evaluates the calling window in IST while the Consent screen's 'today' (ledger_usage, line 1056-1060) evaluates it in the borrower's real zone. The two disagree about which local day a touch fell in, and the gate permits calls outside the borrower's statutory window in their own jurisdiction.

**Fix.** Factor one `_canonical_tz_label(raw)` used by both: strip at the first '(', btrim, then validate. Have _zone call it before ZoneInfo(), and generate the SQL fragment from the same constant. Add a test asserting `_zone('America/New_York (EST)').key == 'America/New_York'`.

### `duplicated-hours-regex` — The window regex is re-implemented rather than imported, with a different absent-value contract

**backend/contact_policy.py:215** · maintainability · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W02-contact-policy`

`m = re.search(r"(\d{1,2}):(\d{2}).*?(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})", str(raw))` (line 215) is character-identical to contact_window._WINDOW_RE (contact_window.py:41), while _parse_days one function later delegates properly (line 229). The two differ in what absence means: None here, (9, 20) there.

**Impact.** The module docstring for contact_window claims one implementation imported from both sides; for hours that is false. Any fix to the regex — am/pm, minutes, ordering — must be made twice, and the two will drift in the exact way the module was created to prevent.

**Fix.** Make _parse_hours a thin delegate to a new contact_window.parse_window_hours(raw) -> tuple | None, and have window_hours() be that function plus the default substitution. One regex, two documented contracts, one place.

### `window-bounds-are-whole-hours-only` — Minutes are parsed and discarded, so a 10:30 start permits a 10:00 call

**backend/contact_policy.py:218** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W02-contact-policy`

`return int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(3))` (line 218) — groups 2 and 4, the minutes, are captured and dropped. The comparison is `now_local.hour < start_h or now_local.hour >= end_h` (lines 499, 520). narrow_window is hour-only by construction too (`_hour(value)`, lines 656-661).

**Impact.** Truncating the start hour loosens the borrower's stated window by up to 59 minutes: 'do not call before 10:30' becomes callable at 10:00. Truncating the end hour tightens it, so the error is asymmetric and always in the direction of contacting earlier than the borrower asked. RBI's window is on the hour so the statutory bound is unaffected, but the borrower-preference bound — the one para 100Y's 'unless the borrower has asked otherwise' is about — is not.

**Fix.** Carry (hour, minute) tuples through _parse_hours, _preferred_hours, _veto and narrow_window, comparing on local time-of-day rather than the hour integer. Round in the strict direction if a minute-level comparison is genuinely unwanted: start rounds up, end rounds down.

### `unparseable-consent-hours-silently-dropped` — _preferred_hours discards an unreadable consent window instead of failing to the default

**backend/contact_policy.py:259** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W02-contact-policy`

`consent = _parse_hours(customer.get("allowed_hours")); stated = _parse_hours(customer.get("preferred_window")); if consent is None: return stated` (lines 259-262). _parse_hours returns None for unparseable as well as for absent (lines 212-218). The docstring claims the intersection is 'the only combination that cannot produce a call neither column would have permitted on its own' (lines 260-263).

**Impact.** If allowed_hours holds an operator-typed string the regex cannot read and preferred_window holds '18:00-21:00 IST', the deliberately-captured consent is discarded and the CRM preference alone governs — intersected only with the statutory bound on voice, and with nothing at all on WhatsApp or SMS. The stated invariant is violated in exactly the data-quality case it was written for.

**Fix.** Distinguish absent from unparseable in _parse_hours (return None vs raise/return a sentinel) and, on unparseable, substitute contact_window.window_hours(None) so the intersection still happens against a real default. Log the raw value at WARNING for data-quality triage.

### `related-id-dedupe-has-no-time-bound` — _already_counted_related matches an event from any point in history

**backend/contact_policy.py:422** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W02-contact-policy`

The query is `SELECT 1 FROM contact_events WHERE customer_id = :cid AND source = :src AND related_id = :rid AND outcome = 'allowed' AND touch_counted LIMIT 1` (lines 424-436) with no occurred_at predicate, unlike its sibling _session_coalesced which does bound on `occurred_at >= :cutoff` (line 405).

**Impact.** Combined with the phone-number fallback for related_id, a borrower who was dialled once becomes permanently exempt from counting on that source. The exemption never expires and grows monotonically over the life of the deployment, so cap enforcement decays silently as the book ages — exactly the failure a 20-customer dev book with 225 decisions cannot surface.

**Fix.** Bound the lookup to the same local day as the reservation (or to session_window(), matching _session_coalesced), and add `AND occurred_at >= :day_start` using the customer-local midnight already computed at line 917.

### `non-voice-channels-unbounded-by-statute` — With no published rule, only voice gets the statutory window; every other channel gets 09:00-20:00

**backend/contact_policy.py:495** · compliance · hidden-assumption · 1/1 confirm · reader `W02-contact-policy`

`if window is None and channel == "voice": window = (RBI_VOICE_START, RBI_VOICE_END)` (lines 495-496). For whatsapp/sms/email/chat/field the only bound is `_preferred_hours(customer) or contact_window.window_hours(None)` (line 517), i.e. 09:00-20:00 — an hour past the 19:00 voice cut-off, and starting an hour later than 08:00.

**Impact.** A WhatsApp dunning message or an SMS demand at 19:45 is outside the hours the 2027 circular sets for collections communication, and the deployment has no published rule row (policy_rules resolves to EMPTY on a fresh install, which is the documented and expected state). Whether the circular's window covers non-voice is precisely the question a bank's compliance officer will decide conservatively — the safe default should be the conservative one.

**Fix.** The mechanism already supports this: a statutory rule row with channel NULL applies to every channel via RuleSet._params' fallback (policy_rules.py:108-114). Ship that row in the seed and make the *code* default `window = (RBI_VOICE_START, RBI_VOICE_END)` for all channels, letting a published rule relax it per channel if a client's counsel signs that off.

### `no-holiday-or-regional-calendar` — There is no calendar: only a weekly day mask, with no holidays and no regional variation

**backend/contact_policy.py:518** · compliance · missing-for-production · 1/1 confirm · reader `W02-contact-policy`

The day rule is `days = _parse_days(customer.get("allowed_days"))` compared against `now_local.isoweekday() % 7` (lines 518-524). policy_rules has no holiday rule kind (the KIND_ constants are lines 60-69). Nothing consults a calendar table.

**Impact.** Indian collections practice and most bank codes of conduct suppress contact on national and state holidays and on religious festivals, which vary by state and by year. A dunning call on Diwali or Eid is the archetypal complaint that reaches an ombudsman. A borrower-level weekly mask cannot express any of this, and the only alternative available today is to suppress the campaign by hand each time.

**Fix.** Add a holiday calendar keyed on (tenant, region, date) with a suppression class, resolved through policy_rules so it inherits versioning and provenance, and check it in _veto for purpose='outreach'. Derive the borrower's region from the address/state already on the customer record.

### `evaluate-and-admit-can-disagree` — evaluate() takes no source/related_id, so the dry run does not model the gate's dedupe path

**backend/contact_policy.py:529** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W02-contact-policy`

evaluate's signature (lines 529-538) has session_key but no source or related_id, and its body never calls _already_counted_related — while admit's decision hinges on it (line 960). evaluate also never accepts a promo-related related_id and blocks_scheduling (line 750) never forwards data_purpose, so REASON_NO_PROMO_CONSENT (which is absent from SCHEDULING_VETOES, line 602-613) can never surface at scheduling time.

**Impact.** The UI preview, the treatment engine's veto (treatment/policy.py:470) and the enforcing gate compute different answers for the same contact. A plan the engine believes is permitted is denied at enact time, which shows up as the 84 'cancelled' outcomes already in the corpus — attributing an execution problem to the model. It also means an offer scheduled for a borrower with no promotional consent is booked and refused later.

**Fix.** Give evaluate the same keyword surface as admit (source, related_id, data_purpose) and share one _would_allow() core between them, with admit adding only the reserve-and-log side effects. Add REASON_NO_PROMO_CONSENT to SCHEDULING_VETOES and forward data_purpose through blocks_scheduling.

### `narrow-window-hardcodes-ist-and-collapses-provenance` — narrow_window writes an 'IST' literal and bakes the statutory bound into the consent column

**backend/contact_policy.py:698** · data-model · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W02-contact-policy`

`value = f"{start:02d}:00-{end:02d}:00 IST"` (line 698) written into consent_records.allowed_hours, where start/end are `max(current[0], statutory[0], want_start)` / `min(current[1], statutory[1], want_end)` (lines 684-685). The activity note records only the new value: `f"Calling window narrowed to {value}"` (line 719).

**Impact.** Three problems in one write. (1) A non-IST borrower's window is labelled IST, and _parse_hours ignores the suffix so the mislabel is silent until someone reads the column. (2) The statutory bound is frozen into consent data — when the 2027 circular changes the window, the borrower's row still carries the old one, and policy_rules' entire versioned-rules design is defeated for that borrower. (3) The prior value is not recorded, so an audit cannot show what changed from what, on a field written from an LLM's reading of a live call.

**Fix.** Write only the borrower's stated bound, not the intersection — the veto already intersects at read time (lines 494-521). Use the customer's resolved zone label instead of the literal. Record old and new values in record_activity, plus the transcript reference and the confidence, so a disputed narrowing is reviewable.

### `reserve-day-assumes-read-committed` — ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING neither returns nor locks the row the next statement depends on

**backend/contact_policy.py:814** · reliability · hidden-assumption · 1/1 confirm · reader `W02-contact-policy`

`INSERT INTO contact_day_counters ... ON CONFLICT (customer_id, local_date) DO NOTHING` (lines 814-820) is followed by a separate `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` (lines 822-832) with `current = int(row["outreach_sessions"] or 0) if row else 0` — the None branch silently assumes zero.

**Impact.** Correct only under READ COMMITTED, where the SELECT takes a fresh snapshot after the INSERT waited out the concurrent inserter. A bank DBA who sets default_transaction_isolation = 'repeatable read' (common where auditors ask for consistent reporting reads) makes the SELECT miss the concurrently-committed row, `row` is None, `current` is 0, the UPDATE matches nothing, and admit returns allowed with a today_count that was never persisted. The cap becomes advisory, and nothing raises.

**Fix.** Use `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (customer_id, local_date) DO UPDATE SET outreach_sessions = contact_day_counters.outreach_sessions RETURNING outreach_sessions` so the row is locked and returned in one statement, then decide and increment. Treat a missing row after that as an error, not as zero. Assert the isolation level at startup.

### `now-is-an-unvalidated-caller-parameter-that-moves-the-whole-veto` — admit(now=...) relocates the statutory window, the cooling-off gap and the ledger timestamp with no bound or record

**backend/contact_policy.py:902** · correctness · hidden-assumption · unverified (verifier-added) · reader `W02-contact-policy`

`instant = _aware(now or datetime.now(timezone.utc))` (contact_policy.py:902) drives the local hour used for the statutory and preference windows (916-917, 926), the day-of-week check (contact_policy.py:524), the cooling-off comparison `instant - last < cool` (968), the week start (970), the day counter's local_date (935, 973) and the ledger row's `occurred_at=instant` (997). Nothing clamps it to a tolerance around the wall clock, and _insert_event stamps the supplied value rather than now() (contact_policy.py:805, against the column's own `server_default=now()` at migration 20260813_0066:69).

**Impact.** Any caller that passes a stale, mis-zoned or naive `now` silently moves the statutory calling window for that contact and writes a contact_events row whose occurred_at is the fictional instant — so the compliance ledger records a dial at a time it did not happen, and the cooling-off and weekly reads for the next contact are computed against that fiction. payment_events.py:595 already threads its own now. There is no live abuse path today, but 'the clock is a parameter and nobody checks it' is not a property a model-risk reviewer will accept on the control that evidences RBI calling hours.

**Fix.** Reject or log a `now` more than a small tolerance (say five minutes) from the wall clock in admit, keeping the parameter for evaluate and for tests. Stamp contact_events.occurred_at from the database clock and carry the caller's instant, if it differs, in a separate as_of column so a replay is distinguishable from a real contact.

### `weekly-cap-is-per-channel-daily-is-not` — The advertised weekly cap of 8 is 8 per channel, i.e. up to 48 touches a week

**backend/contact_policy.py:970** · correctness · hidden-assumption · 1/1 confirm · reader `W02-contact-policy`

`week_n = _week_counted(conn, cid, channel, ...)` filters `AND channel = :ch` (line 374) and `_weekly_cap_for(conn, cid, channel, rules)` is looked up per channel (lines 322-348). The daily counter, by contrast, is cross-channel (`contact_day_counters` keyed on customer_id + local_date only). The module docstring says 'daily/weekly cap' without distinguishing (line 14).

**Impact.** Six channels x cap 8 = 48 permitted touches per borrower per week, held down in practice only by the cross-channel daily cap of 3 (which yields 21). An operator reading CONTACT_WEEKLY_CAP=8 believes the borrower receives at most 8 contacts a week. On a 20-customer book with 16-225 decisions this never binds; on a real book with a multichannel cadence it binds constantly and in the wrong direction.

**Fix.** Add an explicit cross-channel weekly cap alongside the per-channel one, check both, and rename the env var and the accessor so the axis is unmistakable (CONTACT_WEEKLY_CAP_PER_CHANNEL vs CONTACT_WEEKLY_CAP_TOTAL). Document which one the docstring means.

### `ledger-usage-shows-the-env-cap-not-the-tenant-cap` — The Consent list reports dailyCap from the environment, ignoring published rules

**backend/contact_policy.py:1031** · ux · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W02-contact-policy`

`cap = daily_cap()` (line 1031) is called with no rules argument, so it returns `max(1, env_int("CONTACT_DAILY_CAP", 3))` (line 99). admit and evaluate both call `daily_cap(rules)` after resolving (lines 559, 919).

**Impact.** A tenant whose published rule set lowers the daily cap to 2 sees '0 of 3' on every row of the Consent screen while the gate enforces 2. The screen is the artefact a compliance officer screenshots; it will be wrong for exactly the clients who bothered to tighten policy.

**Fix.** Resolve the rule set once per tenant in ledger_usage (the ids are already grouped by customer, and policy_rules caches for 60s) and report the resolved cap per customer. Return the statutory version alongside so the screen can show which policy the number is under.

### `two-definitions-of-this-week-in-one-module` — ledger_usage counts a rolling UTC 7x24h; the gate counts 7 local days from midnight

**backend/contact_policy.py:1040** · observability · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W02-contact-policy`

ledger_usage: `AND occurred_at >= (now() - interval '7 days')` (line 1040). _week_counted: `start = local.replace(hour=0, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0) - timedelta(days=6)` then converted to UTC (lines 366-368). These are different intervals by up to 24 hours, and only one of them is timezone-aware.

**Impact.** The number the Consent screen shows as this week's usage is not the number the gate enforces against. An agent sees 6/8 and is refused; or sees 8/8 and the gate allows. Every such discrepancy becomes a support ticket and erodes trust in the one control the collections head has to demonstrate.

**Fix.** Extract one `week_start(now, tz)` helper and use it in both, doing the timezone resolution in SQL via the existing safe_tz_sql fragment. Add a test that asserts ledger_usage's per-channel number equals _week_counted for the same customer and channel.

### `contact-window-hardcodes-ist` — contact_window evaluates the window in a fixed +05:30, contact_policy in the customer's zone

**backend/contact_window.py:29** · correctness · hidden-assumption · 1/1 confirm · reader `W02-contact-policy`

`IST = timezone(timedelta(hours=5, minutes=30))` (line 29) with the docstring 'Contact windows are expressed in IST, not in the customer's tz column' (line 28). outside_preferred_window does `hour = at.astimezone(IST).hour` (line 70). contact_policy._veto compares against `now_local.hour` where `local = instant.astimezone(_zone(customer['timezone']))` (contact_policy.py:916-917).

**Impact.** There are three timezone authorities for one rule: fixed IST (contact_window), the customer column (contact_policy), and the SQL zone lookup (ledger_usage). A callback booked for 09:30 in a borrower's own zone is in-window to one and out-of-window to another. This is the exact class of bug contact_window.py was created to eliminate, reintroduced one layer up. It is invisible on an all-India dev book and immediate on a multi-region one.

**Fix.** Give window_hours/outside_preferred_window an explicit `tz` parameter (defaulting to IST for backward compatibility) and pass the resolved ZoneInfo from every call site. Better: move the comparison itself into contact_policy and leave contact_window as a pure parser with no clock.

### `comma-plus-range-silently-drops-days` — 'Mon-Fri, Sat' parses to three days instead of six

**backend/contact_window.py:107** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W02-contact-policy`

`if "-" in text_val and "," not in text_val:` (line 107) disables the range branch as soon as a comma appears. The token loop then splits on `[,\s]+` and matches the three literal names: mon, fri, sat -> [1, 5, 6]. Tue/Wed/Thu are dropped with no error.

**Impact.** Fail-closed in direction (the borrower is under-contacted) but silently wrong, and 'Mon-Fri, Sat' is a natural way for an operator to type six days. On a real book this suppresses contact on three days a week for an unknown fraction of borrowers, and it presents as poor reach rather than as a bug — which will be blamed on the treatment model.

**Fix.** Split on commas first, then apply the range parser to each comma-separated part and union the results. Add cases for 'Mon-Fri, Sat', 'Mon - Wed, Fri' and 'Sat,Sun' to the parser tests.

### `allowed-days-collapses-empty-to-none` — The documented None-vs-[] distinction is destroyed by the return expression

**backend/contact_window.py:119** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W02-contact-policy`

The docstring states 'None is deliberately distinct from []: absent consent days and a string that named no recognisable day are different facts, and only the caller knows which default its screen or its gate should apply' (lines 92-96). The implementation is `return days or None` (line 119).

**Impact.** No caller can ever apply the different defaults the docstring promises, which is the direct cause of the fail-open above. It also means a data-quality dashboard cannot count unparseable consent strings — they are indistinguishable from empty ones.

**Fix.** `return days if days else ([] if text_val else None)` — or simply `return days` after establishing that raw was non-empty at line 104, since the empty-raw case already returned None. Then update the two callers to branch on the three states.

### `screen-and-gate-substitute-different-day-defaults` — The consent screen shows Mon-Fri for a string the gate treats as 'any day'

**backend/db.py:1843** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W02-contact-policy`

db.py:1843 `return contact_window.allowed_days(raw) or [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]` feeds the consent API at db.py:2097 (`"days": _parse_allowed_days(r["allowed_days"])`). contact_policy.py:518-524 substitutes no restriction for the same None. contact_window's own docstring sanctions this: 'Callers that need one substitute it themselves, visibly' (line 95).

**Impact.** The Consent screen an agent or a DPO looks at says 'Mon-Fri' while the gate that actually dials says 'any day'. When a borrower complains about a Sunday call, the screen exonerates the system. Consolidating the parser without consolidating the default is the drift the module was built to stop, one level up.

**Fix.** Move the default into contact_window as a named constant (DEFAULT_CONTACT_DAYS) and have both the screen and the gate use it. If they must genuinely differ, name the two constants and assert their relationship in a test.

### `clerk-dead-hitl-constants` — The goodwill HITL gate can never fire and the authority_hitl workflow has no producer

**backend/agent_core/clerk.py:33** · maintainability · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W03-workers`

`HITL_ACTIONS = frozenset({A.FIELD_VISIT, A.LEGAL_NOTICE, "apply_goodwill"})` (clerk.py:33). payload['action'] is a treatment action set by enqueue_from_treatment from recommend_treatment's result; the treatment action catalog (agent_core/treatment/actions.py:47-56) has no 'apply_goodwill' - that string is a voice bot tool name (bot_tools.py:777). `AUTHORITY_HITL = "authority_hitl"` (clerk.py:31) is referenced only at clerk.py:144; nothing anywhere enqueues that workflow type.

**Impact.** The code reads as though goodwill waivers and authority overrides are gated by human approval. They are not - the gate is unreachable. A reviewer auditing 'which actions require a second pair of eyes' will read this frozenset and get the wrong answer.

**Fix.** Delete the unreachable members, or wire the authority engine to enqueue AUTHORITY_HITL jobs with an action the gate actually matches. Assert at import that every member of HITL_ACTIONS is a key in treatment.actions.SPECS.

### `clerk-approvedby-is-client-supplied` — The maker-checker control keys on an approver id the caller sends in the request body

**backend/agent_core/clerk.py:145** · compliance · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W03-workers`

clerk.py:145 trusts `job.get("approvedBy")`. That column is set at work_runtime/adapter_pg.py:126 from `payload.get("userId") or payload.get("user_id")` - i.e. the JSON body of POST /floor/approvals/{job_id}/signal (main.py:1501-1510), which performs no role check and does not consult db._actor_user_id() (db_core.py:356-361). Any holder of an API key can approve any parked legal notice and name any user as the approver.

**Impact.** The only human-in-the-loop control over the two most legally exposed actions in the system (field visit and legal notice) can be satisfied by a forged field, with no segregation of duties (the requester can approve their own), no role check, and no independent audit row. Under RBI fair-practice expectations and any internal audit, an approval record that the approver cannot be held to is worse than no approval record.

**Fix.** Derive approved_by from actor_context/db._actor_user_id() in the route, never from the body; require a role (supervisor/manager) on the route; reject approval when approver == requester; and write an immutable audit row (who, when, which decision, which policy_version) in addition to the job column.

### `worker-import-time-blast-radius` — Every domain module is imported at module scope, so one bad import stops all queues - while the clerk is imported defensively

**backend/bot_worker.py:33** · reliability · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W03-workers`

Lines 33-46 import azure_openai, bot_jobs, cadence, call_closer, campaigns, db, outbound, payment_events, the three treatment modules, promise_fulfillment, webhooks_dispatch and whatsapp_outbound at module scope, whereas the clerk is imported inside the loop under try/except (bot_worker.py:146-160). With `restart: unless-stopped` an import error becomes a silent crash loop.

**Impact.** A migration that lands ahead of code, or an optional dependency missing in the customer's image, takes down WhatsApp outbound and PTP reminders because an unrelated treatment module failed to import - and the container restart-loops with the failure only visible in stdout.

**Fix.** Import stage modules lazily inside _run_stage (or guard each with try/except at startup and disable just that stage), and log a single explicit 'stage disabled: <name>: <reason>' line that a healthcheck can see.

### `ops-unknown-severity-becomes-low` — Any unrecognised alert severity silently degrades to the lowest level

**backend/ops_screens.py:265** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W03-workers`

```def _severity_num(raw): v = (raw or "medium").strip().lower(); if v in {"critical", "high", "3"}: return 3; if v in {"medium", "warn", "2"}: return 2; return 1``` (ops_screens.py:265-271). 'urgent', 'sev1', 'P1', 'severe' - and a NULL-ish empty string - all return 1.

**Impact.** criticalAlerts (line 755) and the barge recommendation (326) both key on this number, so a compliance or abuse alert emitted by a producer using a different vocabulary is displayed as low priority and never escalates. Silent downgrade of a safety signal is worse than an error, because the screen still looks correct.

**Fix.** Constrain severity at the write side (DB CHECK or an enum), and make the reader map unknown values UP to the highest severity with a logged warning, never down.

### `ops-floor-heuristics-unversioned` — Composite risk and recommended action are hand-tuned integer thresholds with no version, no tenant config and no calibration

**backend/ops_screens.py:335** · statistics · hidden-assumption · 1/1 confirm · reader `W03-workers`

_composite_risk adds fixed points (`if sentiment <= -0.35: score += 3`, `if trend <= -0.15: score += 2`, `if duration_sec >= 480: score += 1`, `if dnd: score += 1`) with cut-offs at 5 and 2 (ops_screens.py:335-371); _recommended_action is a fixed if-ladder (309-332); `_risk_from_sentiment` (274-280) is defined and never called.

**Impact.** These numbers drive what a supervisor is told to do on a live call, and they carry no version stamp, so a change cannot be tied to a change in floor behaviour and cannot be A/B'd or rolled back. Adding a point for `dnd` conflates a consent flag with borrower risk - a customer who exercised a contact preference is scored as more dangerous. A model-risk reviewer will ask for the derivation and there is none.

**Fix.** Move the weights into versioned, tenant-configurable policy (the same pattern the treatment policy_version uses), stamp the version on every snapshot, remove dnd from the risk score (surface it separately as a constraint), and delete the dead helper.

### `ops-floor-returns-raw-transcript` — Raw borrower speech and a full customer profile go into the Floor payload with no redaction and no purpose gate

**backend/ops_screens.py:519** · privacy · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W03-workers`

`turns_by.setdefault(iid, []).append({"speaker": tr["speaker"] or "system", "text": (tr["text"] or "")[:240]})` and `last_line_by[iid] = (tr["text"] or "—")[:160]` (ops_screens.py:519-524), surfaced as `"recentTurns": turns` and `"lastLine": last_line` (697,690) alongside customer name, outstanding, risk, language and dnd (673-696). pii_redact.py exists in the backend and is not used here.

**Impact.** Live transcript fragments are the most sensitive content the platform holds - borrowers state account numbers, health reasons for non-payment, and family circumstances. They are returned to every user who can open the Floor, with no field masking, no role differentiation, and no record of who viewed them; if the response is cached or logged anywhere, the content escapes. Under DPDP this is processing without purpose limitation or access control, and the 2027 recording-retention rules make the handling of call content specifically examinable.

**Fix.** Run transcript text through pii_redact before it leaves the query, gate recentTurns behind an explicit supervisor role, log Floor transcript views to an access log, and let the tenant configure whether live text is shown at all.

### `ops-tenant-autocreation` — Ops screens mint tenant rows on demand to satisfy a foreign key

**backend/ops_screens.py:1150** · data-model · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W03-workers`

`# Ensure tenant exists for FK` then `INSERT INTO tenants (id, name, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (:id, :name, now(), now()) ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING` in create_webhook_endpoint (ops_screens.py:1149-1159) and again in patch_provider_enabled (1663-1671), with `{"id": tenant, "name": tenant}`.

**Impact.** Tenant provisioning in a bank is a governed action with an onboarding record, a data-processing agreement and a retention policy attached. A mistyped tenant header on an ops call silently creates a tenant whose name is its slug, and subsequent rows attach to it - producing orphan data that nobody provisioned and no DPA covers.

**Fix.** Fail with 404/409 when the tenant does not exist; provision tenants only through an explicit, audited onboarding path.

### `ops-delivery-log-retention` — Webhook delivery rows keep full event payloads and response bodies forever

**backend/ops_screens.py:1295** · privacy · missing-for-production · 1/1 confirm · reader `W03-workers`

_delivery_contract returns the whole stored payload and response_body (ops_screens.py:1298-1315); dispatch writes the business payload verbatim (payments.py:244-257 sends intentId, accountId, amount, allocated promise ids). Nothing in this module or in webhooks_dispatch purges old deliveries.

**Impact.** An operational queue table becomes an indefinite secondary store of customer financial data, replicated into every backup, outside whatever retention the primary records have. DPDP storage limitation and the bank's own record-retention schedule both require a defined life; today there is none, and a receiver's chatty error body can additionally echo customer data back into the log.

**Fix.** Add a retention job (e.g. purge settled deliveries after 30-90 days, keep a hashed summary for audit), truncate stored payloads to the identifiers needed to re-drive, and document the retention alongside the 6-month recording rule.

### `ops-simulated-rows-inflate-delivery-stats` — Simulated deliveries carry a fabricated 200 and latency into the same log real deliveries use

**backend/ops_screens.py:1369** · observability · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W03-workers`

`ok = bool(host) and ep["status"] == "active"; http_status = 200 if ok else 502; status = "success" if ok else "server_err"` with a digest-derived `latency` (ops_screens.py:1369-1377), persisted into webhook_deliveries; list_webhook_deliveries returns both modes with no filter (1322-1346) and only the per-row `mode` field distinguishes them (1318).

**Impact.** The delivery log is what an integration owner reads to decide whether their subscription works, and any aggregate over it (success rate, p95 latency) is inflated by rows that never left the process. The module docstring records that this is exactly how the platform previously came to have 'a delivery log full of 200s'; the mode flag mitigates it only for a reader who knows to look.

**Fix.** Default the list and any aggregate to delivery_mode='live', make the simulated rows visually distinct in the UI, and expire them after a short retention.

### `payments-intent-lookup-not-tenant-scoped` — Intent lookup has no tenant predicate, so one shared webhook secret can settle any tenant's intent

**backend/payments.py:135** · security · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W03-workers`

`SELECT * FROM payment_intents WHERE id = :id FOR UPDATE` and `... WHERE public_token = :token FOR UPDATE` (payments.py:135-142) - no tenant_id filter, although payment_intents carries tenant_id (alembic/versions/20260812_0065_payment_intents.py) and load_intent_by_token joins tenants without filtering either (397-412). webhook_secret() resolves from process-wide env (payments.py:62-66), so the secret is per-deployment, not per-tenant.

**Impact.** In a multi-tenant deployment any party holding the single PAYMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET can post a payment against another tenant's intent id, writing to that tenant's ledger. Even without an attacker, a mis-routed PSP callback settles the wrong book. Row-level security is being introduced elsewhere in this codebase precisely to prevent this class of cross-tenant write.

**Fix.** Scope every intent lookup by tenant, derive the tenant from the intent and set the tenant context before writing, and make the webhook secret per-tenant (or per-endpoint) rather than one process-wide value.

### `payments-expiry-write-rolled-back` — The 'mark this intent expired' write is always discarded by the exception raised two lines later

**backend/payments.py:158** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W03-workers`

```conn.execute(text("UPDATE payment_intents SET status = 'expired' WHERE id = :id AND status <> 'paid'"), {"id": intent["id"]}); raise ValueError("intent_expired")``` (payments.py:158-162). The raise propagates out of `with db.engine.begin() as conn:` at main.py:944, which rolls the transaction back - including the status update.

**Impact.** Expired intents never get their status set by this path, so render_pay_page's `expired = status == "expired"` (payments.py:442) is never true from time expiry and a stale link keeps showing 'Pay your promised amount'. A borrower can be shown a live-looking payment page for a link the system considers dead, and every webhook replay repeats the same wasted write.

**Fix.** Do the expiry transition in its own transaction (or a sweeper), and have the page compute expiry from expires_at rather than only from the persisted status.

### `payments-float-money-and-clamped-outstanding` — Money is bound to the database as Python floats, outstanding is clamped at zero, and the remainder of an over-payment is dropped

**backend/payments.py:186** · data-model · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W03-workers`

`UPDATE accounts SET outstanding = GREATEST(0, outstanding - :paid)` (payments.py:186-189) with `{"paid": float(paid)}` (191); the ledger row is written as `"amount": float(-paid)` (180); allocation writes `float(new_paid)` (358); and after the loop any unallocated `remaining` is simply discarded (payments.py:393-394 - the loop breaks and nothing records the residue).

**Impact.** Three separate problems a bank's finance team will catch: (1) Decimal amounts are converted to binary floats on the way into a numeric column, so the ledger no longer reconciles exactly with the PSP settlement file; (2) GREATEST(0, ...) silently absorbs an over-payment so accounts.outstanding and SUM(ledger_entries.amount) drift apart with no error and no reconciliation job to detect it; (3) an over-payment leaves no unapplied-credit record, so the excess is invisible to the borrower and to the ops team who must refund it.

**Fix.** Bind Decimal (psycopg handles numeric natively) and type the columns numeric(14,2); make accounts.outstanding a derived read of the ledger or add a nightly reconciliation that alerts on drift; post the unallocated residue as an explicit 'unapplied credit' ledger entry rather than dropping it.

### `payments-get-mutates-state` — An unauthenticated GET marks the intent 'opened', so link previews and scanners fabricate an engagement signal

**backend/payments.py:415** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W03-workers`

`def mark_opened(conn, intent_id)` sets `status = 'opened' WHERE id = :id AND status IN ('created','sent')` (payments.py:415-425), called from the GET handler at main.py:892 inside `db.engine.begin()`. The route is public (main.py:269).

**Impact.** WhatsApp, iMessage and enterprise mail gateways fetch URLs to build previews, and security scanners fetch them too. 'opened' therefore does not mean the borrower looked at the link - but it is exactly the kind of engagement signal a reco/treatment feature would use, and it is what an agent sees on the timeline before calling. Decisions and QA conversations get made on a fact that is not true.

**Fix.** Make GET side-effect free; record an 'open' from a client-side beacon or from the first POST interaction, and exclude known preview user-agents. Rate-limit the public route to stop token scanning.

### `pay-page-carries-no-statutory-disclosure` — The borrower-facing pay page carries none of the disclosure the message that links to it is forbidden to omit

**backend/payments.py:453** · compliance · missing-for-production · unverified (verifier-added) · reader `W03-workers`

render_pay_page (payments.py:453-481) emits tenant name, amount, account tail, status and expiry, and nothing else - no regulated-entity identification beyond a name, no loan reference, no grievance officer name, telephone or email.
