### `ohp-simulated-flag-hidden` — includesSimulated is fetched and never displayed; there is no window or simulated-data control

**Habibi/src/components/upsell/OfferHealthPanel.tsx:64** · compliance · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

Header renders `Offer engine · {data.window}` only. `data.includesSimulated` (api/offer-health.ts:36) is never read. `useOfferHealth(window, includeSimulated = false)` (offer-health.ts:211) supports 24h/7d/30d/90d and a simulated toggle; routes/upsell.tsx:196 renders `<OfferHealthPanel />` with no props, hard-pinning 30d and excluding simulated with no UI to change either.

**Impact.** Every artefact in this system is stamped `corpus: simulated` (treatment_{reach,timing,uplift}.json and propensity.json). A panel that is the org's answer to 'is the recommender helping?' must state on its face whether the numbers include synthetic rows — a screenshot of it will end up in a model-risk pack. A supervisor also cannot narrow to 24h to check whether a change this morning helped.

**Fix.** Render an amber 'includes simulated data' lozenge whenever includesSimulated is true, and an explicit 'live data only' otherwise. Add a window segmented control (24h/7d/30d/90d) and a supervisor-only includeSimulated toggle.

### `metrics-null-guard-defeated-in-mock` — computeMetrics returns 0, not null, for empty denominators — exactly what MetricsStrip's comment says must never happen

**Habibi/src/data/upsell-seed.ts:775** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `U02-nba-offer-ui`

`const conversionRate = capturedRecent.length === 0 ? 0 : Math.round((wonRecent / capturedRecent.length) * 100);` and at :778-780 `const avgDaysToClose = closed.length === 0 ? 0 : ...`. The type is plain `number` (api/types/upsell.ts:107-108), assigned into LeadMetrics' `number | null` fields at api/upsell.ts:193,196. MetricsStrip.tsx:70-73 asserts 'rendering both as 0% is how a quiet month looks identical to a broken pipeline'; its guards at :76 and :83 are unreachable on that path.

**Impact.** A quiet month renders 'Conversion (30d) 0%' and 'Avg time-to-close 0d' — the second reading as 'every lead closes the same day'. This is the mock/demo path, which is what a customer sees in a pilot; but it also means the invariant is enforced in exactly one of the two implementations the module claims are 'behaviourally identical' (api/upsell.ts:7-9), so any future live regression has no test to catch it.

**Fix.** Change Metrics.conversionRate and Metrics.avgDaysToClose to `number | null` in api/types/upsell.ts and return null from computeMetrics for zero denominators. Add a test asserting an empty lead list yields nulls on both the mock and live shapes.

### `clerk-one-job-per-case-forever` — The clerk job is keyed on (workflow, trigger_ref) only, so a case's second and later decisions never reach the executor

**backend/agent_core/clerk.py:63** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W01-triggers`

idempotency_key ignores decision_id (clerk.py:63-65); the payload carries decisionId but the key does not. enqueue_from_treatment is only ever called at case creation (payment_events.py:452, promise_fulfillment.py:842). Later re-decisions of the same case come from followthrough.advance and the sweep, which do not enqueue at all.

**Impact.** The ladder is the product: bounce -> WhatsApp -> bot call -> agent. Only the first rung ever produces a clerk work item under this key. If the first decision was 'wait' or suppressed (clerk._run returns {'skipped': True} at lines 151-152), the case never gets another job even once the reason for waiting is gone. On a 20-customer book with a manual floor this is invisible; on a real book it silently caps every case at one attempt.

**Fix.** Include the decision id (or a monotonically increasing rung number) in the idempotency key, and have followthrough/sweep enqueue on each new actionable decision. Alternatively make the executor poll due decisions and drop the clerk enqueue from the trigger sites entirely — one mechanism, not two.

### `plan-next-skipped-on-idempotent-paths` — _plan_next runs only on the brand-new-insert path; three other paths perform a first touch without ever asking the engine

**backend/payment_events.py:416** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W01-triggers`

`_first_touch(conn, event_d, ...); _plan_next(conn, event_d, now=instant)` (payment_events.py:415-416). The other three branches call _first_touch and return without _plan_next: the source_ref replay path (222-227), the open-EMI path (261-266) and the IntegrityError raced path (393-398).

**Impact.** Those branches exist precisely for the cases where an earlier ingest failed to complete a first touch. When the retry finally succeeds in reaching the borrower, the treatment engine is never asked what should follow — so the case gets a statutory notice and then nothing. On the raced path the concurrent transaction does plan, but on the replay path (a retried webhook after a partial failure) nobody does, and the case silently drops out of the ladder.

**Fix.** Call _plan_next wherever _first_touch newly succeeds, and make it idempotent per (case, rung) rather than relying on the caller's branch. followthrough already knows how to avoid duplicate rungs.

### `first-touch-suppression-reason-mislabelled` — When both channels are refused the SMS reason wins, hiding why WhatsApp was refused

**backend/payment_events.py:611** · observability · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W01-triggers`

`reason = sms_decision.reason or wa_decision.reason or "channel_opted_out"` (payment_events.py:611).

**Impact.** The suppression_reason stored on the event and shown to ops describes the last channel tried, not the binding constraint. 'daily_cap' gets reported when the real cause was a WhatsApp opt-out, so the fix an operator applies is the wrong one. Suppression breakdowns in /treatment/insights inherit the mislabelling.

**Fix.** Store a structured per-channel reason (e.g. jsonb {'whatsapp': 'consent_revoked', 'sms': 'daily_cap'}) and derive the display string from it.

### `reminder-error-stored-in-provider-delivery-id` — A failure reason is written into the provider_delivery_id column

**backend/promise_fulfillment.py:1074** · data-model · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W01-triggers`

`provider_delivery_id = COALESCE(:err, provider_delivery_id)` with `"err": (err or "")[:200] or None` (promise_fulfillment.py:1074, 1082), where err is a contact-policy reason or an exception class name from line 1067.

**Impact.** Delivery-receipt reconciliation joins on provider_delivery_id. Poisoning it with strings like 'outside_calling_hours' or 'ConnectionError' means those rows can never be matched against carrier receipts, and any report counting delivered messages by provider id silently mis-buckets them.

**Fix.** Add a `last_error TEXT` column to promise_reminders and write the reason there.

### `dead-duplicate-day-map` — _DAY_NAME_TO_NUM is defined here and in db.py and used in neither

**backend/contact_policy.py:73** · maintainability · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W02-contact-policy`

`_DAY_NAME_TO_NUM = {"sun": 0, ...}` at contact_policy.py:73 and again at db.py:1768; the canonical one is contact_window.DAY_NAME_TO_NUM (contact_window.py:87). Grep shows no read of either private copy.

**Impact.** Two dead copies of the constant whose divergence is the documented reason contact_window exists (contact_window.py:76-84). The next edit to the day rule has three plausible places to land, and two of them are silent no-ops that will look correct in review.

**Fix.** Delete both private copies and import contact_window.DAY_NAME_TO_NUM where a map is genuinely needed. Add a test that greps the tree for a second day-name mapping, the same way test_outbound_gate_contract policies the gate ordering.

### `midnight-crossing-window-unrepresentable` — A window whose end hour precedes its start blocks every hour of the day

**backend/contact_policy.py:520** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W02-contact-policy`

`if now_local.hour < start_h or now_local.hour >= end_h: return REASON_WINDOW` (line 520). For (start, end) = (20, 8) this is true for every hour. _preferred_hours guards the intersection case (line 271) but not an inverted single column, and window_hours returns whatever the regex found with no ordering check (contact_window.py:55).

**Impact.** A night-shift borrower's genuine preference, or a transposed data entry, makes the borrower permanently uncontactable with no error and no alert — the same silent-suppression failure mode the allowed_days drift note describes. It is fail-closed, so it presents as poor reach and is blamed on the model.

**Fix.** Validate ordering at parse time: if end <= start, either support the wrap (hour >= start or hour < end) or reject and fall back to the default, logging the raw value. Add a data-quality report counting borrowers whose effective window is empty.

### `evaluate-reports-a-meaningless-count-for-future-instants` — evaluate(now=<future>) returns today_count=0 and vacuous cap checks with no signal that they were vacuous

**backend/contact_policy.py:575** · observability · hidden-assumption · 1/1 confirm · reader `W02-contact-policy`

`today = _today_count(conn, cid, local.date())` (line 575) looks up contact_day_counters for the *future* local date, which has no row, so it returns 0; _week_counted's window `start = future_local_midnight - 6 days` (line 367) is likewise mostly empty. The comment at lines 597-601 acknowledges this for blocks_scheduling, but evaluate itself is the treatment engine's veto (treatment/policy.py:470, timing.py:16) and the UI's preview (db.py:2120).

**Impact.** Decision(True, today_count=0, daily_cap=3) for a slot next Tuesday is rendered as '0 of 3 used' on a screen and consumed as an allow by the planner, when in truth no volume limit was evaluated. It contributes to the gap between what the engine plans and what enact.py's admit permits — visible in the corpus as 84 cancelled outcomes.

**Fix.** Add a `volume_checked: bool` field to Decision, set False when `now` is not within the current local day, and have the UI and the planner render 'not yet assessable' rather than a zero. Or split evaluate into evaluate_now() and evaluate_at() with distinct return types.

### `refresh-used-this-week-ignores-the-injected-clock` — _refresh_used_this_week reads the wall clock while every other path threads `now`

**backend/contact_policy.py:850** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W02-contact-policy`

`local = datetime.now(tz)` (line 850), whereas admit computes `instant = _aware(now or datetime.now(timezone.utc))` (line 902) and passes it to _week_counted as `now=instant` (line 970). The refresh is called at line 1002 with no clock argument.

**Impact.** The enforcing count and the cached count are computed over different weeks whenever `now` is not the wall clock — replay, backfill, a scheduler that batches yesterday's work, and every test with a frozen clock. The Consent screen then shows a used_this_week that the gate does not agree with, and the disagreement is invisible because the cache is only ever read by the UI.

**Fix.** Pass `now` into _refresh_used_this_week and derive `local` from it, matching _week_counted exactly. Better still, delete the cache column and compute it in ledger_usage — it is a denormalisation of a query that is already indexed.

### `phone-number-in-related-id` — A borrower's phone number is written into contact_events.related_id as a correlation key

**backend/main.py:3918** · privacy · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W02-contact-policy`

`related_id=attempt["id"] if attempt else to` (main.py:3918), where `to` is the destination phone number. contact_events.related_id is a plain text column with an index on (customer_id, source, related_id) (migration lines 109-113) and no masking, no encryption and no retention policy.

**Impact.** Under DPDP, contact numbers are personal data with purpose limitation and erasure obligations. Putting them in a correlation column of an append-only ledger makes them un-erasable by design and spreads them into every index, backup and audit export that touches the table. It also makes the ledger un-shareable with an agency or a regulator without redaction.

**Fix.** Never fall back to the phone number. Mint a synthetic attempt id when outbound.reserve returns nothing, so related_id is always an internal reference. Add a check (or a CHECK constraint on a digit pattern) rejecting values that look like phone numbers, and scrub existing rows.

### `money-formatting-diverges-across-copies` — The same offer renders with three different money formatters depending on which copy produced it

**Habibi/src/lib/customerInsights.ts:137** · ux · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W04-reco-callsites-nba`

Python uses money_inr.inr, which carries the symbol and Indian grouping (`return money_inr.inr(n)` at customer_insights.py:53; test asserts '₹12,34,567'), and composes `f" · {_inr(amount)}"` (customer_insights.py:111). TS uses a bare `value.toLocaleString("en-IN")` with '₹' prepended by hand at each call site (customerInsights.ts:137-140, and e.g. line 285 `(₹${inr(openDispute.amount)})`), while the offer row uses a third function, fmtOfferAmount → `₹${Math.round(n).toLocaleString("en-IN")}` (offer-policy.ts:62-64), which additionally rounds.

**Impact.** The offline card and the served card show the same rupee amount differently — including rounding on the offer amount in one copy and not the other. On a screen a rep reads figures off before speaking to a borrower, an inconsistent or silently rounded amount is a quotation error waiting to happen, and it makes screenshot-based dispute handling ambiguous.

**Fix.** One formatter per side, symbol included, no rounding: export the equivalent of money_inr.inr from a single TS module and use it everywhere including offer-policy.ts. Assert the two agree in a shared fixture test the way test_money_formatting.py already does server-side.

### `dead-within-window-helper` — _within_window survives the ladder it served, still comparing a display string to the process clock

**backend/customer_insights.py:36** · maintainability · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W04-reco-callsites-nba`

`def _within_window(pref: str) -> bool: m = re.search(r"(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})[–-](\d{1,2}):(\d{2})", pref or "") ... now = datetime.now()` (customer_insights.py:36-44). Nothing in the repository calls it — the only other _within_window hit is an unrelated function in campaigns.py:15. The TS twin was deleted with an explicit tombstone explaining why (customerInsights.ts:150-154).

Left in the module, the next person adding a rule reaches for it, and the browser-clock-versus-statutory-window defect returns server-side.

### `activity-null-timestamp-divergence` — The server emits activity rows with a null timestamp that the client type says cannot exist

**backend/customer_insights.py:543** · data-model · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W04-reco-callsites-nba`

Python `items.sort(key=lambda x: x.get("at") or "", reverse=True); return items[:8]` (customer_insights.py:543-544) — no filter. TS filters them out: `.filter((item) => item.at)` (customerInsights.ts:486). The wire model permits null (`at: str | None = None`, schemas.py:328) but the TS type declares `at: string` (customerInsights.ts:69) and sorts with `b.at.localeCompare(a.at)` (customerInsights.ts:487).

**Impact.** A promise or document row with a missing timestamp reaches the client typed as a non-nullable string. Today the only consumer is fmtRelative, which handles null (customer360-seed.ts:1049-1050), so it renders '—' rather than crashing — but the type is a lie and the next consumer that calls a string method on it throws in the customer detail route.

**Fix.** Filter falsy timestamps in synthesize_activity to match the client, or make the TS type `at: string | null` and fix the comparator. Pick one and assert it in the shared API contract test.

### `decline-attributed-to-latest-decision-only` — A decline is recorded against whichever decision id happens to be current, not the offer that was refused

**backend/voice/tools.py:2087** · statistics · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W04-reco-callsites-nba`

`await asyncio.to_thread(decisions.record_response, state.offer_decision_id, "declined")` (voice/tools.py:2086-2088) and `decisions.record_response(ctx.offer_decision_id, "declined")` (bot_tools.py:518). state.offer_decision_id is overwritten by each recommend (voice/tools.py:2001, 2197; bot_tools.py:483), and the tool takes no offer_id argument (catalog.py:737-752 — args are `reason` only).

**Impact.** The engine's max_offers_per_call is greater than one on the chat path (offers_presented_this_call is incremented per recommend, bot_tools.py:494), so a customer who is offered A, ignores it, is offered B, and declines B has the decline written against B while A stays unlabelled forever. On a book where declines are the majority outcome, the label set the propensity model trains on is mis-assigned. The per-product cool-down the docstring promises ('feeds the per-product cool-down so we do not raise the same thing again', voice/tools.py:2071) is applied to the wrong product.

**Fix.** Add an optional offer_id argument to the decline_offer ToolSpec, parse '<decisionId>:<productId>' the way capture_lead already does (voice/tools.py:2296-2308), and fall back to the current decision only when absent. Label every un-responded decision from a completed call as 'no_response' at teardown so the absence itself is data.

### `close-probe-registry-miss-loses-offer` — If the pre_close node is missing, the probe has already marked an offer presented that can never be spoken

**backend/voice/tools.py:2266** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W04-reco-callsites-nba`

_close_probe_node calls `await _prepare_close_probe()` (2264) — which presents and consumes quota (2203, 2219-2226) — and only then `node = _node("pre_close"); if node is None: ... return None` (2265-2269). _record_close_probe (2270) is skipped on that branch, so the probe event is not even recorded.

**Impact.** A registry miss (tools built without a graph, a renamed node, a partial deploy) leaves a decision marked presented with no probe event and no possibility of a response — quota consumed, funnel polluted, and no trace explaining it. Low frequency, high confusion.

**Fix.** Resolve the node first and return early before preparing the probe, mirroring the ordering discipline already applied in _node ('Resolve first: an unknown name must not move current_node', voice/tools.py:425-427).

### `capture-lead-silently-rewrites-product` — When offer_id and product_id disagree, the call site rewrites the product and only logs a warning

**backend/voice/tools.py:2300** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `W04-reco-callsites-nba`

`if offer_product and offer_product != product_id: logger.warning("capture_lead offer/product mismatch: offer=%s product=%s — trusting the offer", ...); product_id = offer_product` (voice/tools.py:2300-2307; identical at bot_tools.py:560-566).

**Impact.** A mismatch means the model has lost track of which product it pitched — the strongest available signal that the turn is confused. Rewriting silently converts it into a confident lead for a product the customer may never have discussed, and the only record is a WARNING line in a process whose root logger configuration has historically been a problem. In a mis-selling complaint the CRM shows a clean lead and the reason it is wrong is in a log that has rolled over.

**Fix.** Refuse the capture on mismatch and return a soft error the model can correct, the same shape offer_sourcing_violation returns. If rewriting must be kept, record the discrepancy on the lead row (originalProductId) so it is queryable, not just loggable.

### `greediness-monotonicity-tested-only-on-the-top-rank` — The exploration dial's monotonicity is asserted for one action and never at the 1.0 discontinuity

**backend/tests/test_decision_intelligence_p0.py:177** · statistics · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `X01-tests-di`

p0:177-182 collects `explore.choose(...).distribution[A.WHATSAPP]` for g in (0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9) and asserts `tops == sorted(tops)`. g=1.0 is excluded, and that is where explore.choose takes a different branch entirely (explore.py:115-122) rather than going through _rank_weights.

**Impact.** 'A collections head is going to be shown this number, and a non-monotone control is not a control' (p0:175-176). The claim is about the whole distribution and about the full range of the dial; the test covers one action over five interior points. `sorted()` also passes on equal values, so a dial that stopped responding entirely would be green.

**Fix.** Assert stochastic ordering across the whole distribution and include g=1.0 and g just below it, and assert strict increase rather than non-decrease between distinct greediness values.

### `caplog-requested-and-never-asserted` — 'Capacity that cannot be met says so' never checks that it says anything

**backend/tests/test_decision_intelligence_p2.py:244** · testing · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `X01-tests-di`

p2:244 `def test_capacity_that_cannot_be_met_says_so(caplog) -> None:` and the only assertion is p2:253 `assert not solved.converged`. caplog is requested and never read. allocate.py:281-289 emits the warning that carries the prices, the demand and the capacity — the payload an SRE would page on.

**Impact.** The half of the behaviour that reaches a human is untested. A refactor that drops the logger.warning leaves the test green while the floor manager loses the only signal that tomorrow's plan is arithmetically impossible.

**Fix.** Assert on caplog: that a WARNING was emitted, that it names the oversubscribed resource, and that it carries both the demand and the capacity.

### `contract-defaults-to-the-softest-bucket-when-features-are-missing` — An envelope built without features authorises the 0-30 script for any borrower

**backend/tests/test_decision_intelligence_p2.py:450** · compliance · hidden-assumption · 1/1 confirm · reader `X01-tests-di`

p2:450-455 calls `contract.build(TreatmentResult(action="whatsapp", ...), features=None)` and asserts only the two prohibitions. contract.py:102 reads `bucket = getattr(features, "bucket", None) or A.B_0_30`, and every bucket-driven field — objective, strategy, maxDurationSec, allowedOffers — then follows from 0-30. p2:497-513 shows the objective is meant to follow the bucket ('61-90 is triage ... asking a bot to close there exceeds what the bucket policy already says it may own').

**Impact.** A feature build that partially fails — the exact failure p3:974-988 documents happening silently for 17% of a book — hands a voice bot a 0-30 'payment_commitment' objective for a 90+ DPD borrower, with the longest permitted call duration and the softest strategy. That is a conduct exposure, and it fails open rather than closed.

**Fix.** Refuse to build a contract without a bucket, or default to the most restrictive bucket rather than the least. Add a test asserting `contract.build(result, features=None)` either returns None or carries objective='triage' with no waiver.

### `segment-bands-agree-with-the-package-only-by-coincidence` — 'Bucket bands land on the buckets the rest of the package uses' never compares the two

**backend/tests/test_decision_intelligence_p3.py:52** · maintainability · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `X01-tests-di`

p3:52-57 asserts segments.key_for prefixes only: `assert segments.key_for({"dpd": 31.0}).startswith("b3160/")`. It never calls A.bucket_for. segments._BUCKETS (segments.py:55-61) and actions.bucket_for (actions.py:296-307) encode the same four edges independently, and they already diverge on the None case (bucket_for returns PRE_DUE, bucket_band returns None -> UNKNOWN).

**Impact.** The two ladders can drift apart with no test failing. If a client's bucket policy moves the 60-day edge, the segment partition silently keeps the old one, and every segment model is then fitted on a population its key no longer describes — the 'silent wrong' segments.py:40-43 says the version bump exists to prevent.

**Fix.** Assert the agreement directly: `for dpd in range(-5, 200): assert segments.bucket_band({'dpd': float(dpd)}) == _BAND_BY_BUCKET[A.bucket_for(dpd)]`, with the None case handled explicitly.

### `ladder-fit-cost-inside-the-unit-suite` — A minute of gradient descent runs inside the test suite, cached in module state

**backend/tests/test_decision_intelligence_p3.py:818** · testing · hidden-assumption · 1/1 confirm · reader `X01-tests-di`

p3:818-822: 'Fitting five thousand rows through four logistic halves takes about a minute, and every test below wants the same fit ... the alternative was a six-minute run for five assertions, which is the kind of cost that gets a test file deleted.' `_LADDER_CACHE: dict[str, Any] = {}` is module-level mutable state shared by three tests, and `_trainer()` is lru_cached.

**Impact.** The mitigation is sound but the shape is fragile: the three ladder tests receive the same dict objects, so any future test that mutates a report row silently corrupts its siblings, order-dependently. It also means the DI suite has a floor of roughly a minute of pure CPU, which is why it will be the first thing excluded from a pre-commit hook.

**Fix.** Return deep copies from _standard_ladder, or move the fit to a session-scoped fixture so pytest owns the lifecycle. Consider marking the ladder tests `slow` so they run in CI but not locally.

### `dead-veto-code-ratified-by-comment` — ACCOUNT_NOT_DELINQUENT is unreachable and the test comments on it approvingly instead of flagging it

**backend/agent_core/treatment/policy.py:174** · maintainability · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `X02-tests-engine-reco`

policy.py:170-176 `delinquent = bool((features.dpd or 0) > 0 or features.open_bounce_id or features.open_promise_id)` then `if not delinquent and spec.rung > 1: return ACCOUNT_NOT_DELINQUENT`. Every action with rung > 1 (VOICE_BOT 2, HUMAN_CALL 3, FIELD_VISIT 4, LEGAL_NOTICE 5, actions.py:113-125) is absent from the PRE_DUE allowed set (actions.py:183-191), and bucket_for returns PRE_DUE for dpd None or 0 (actions.py:298-301), so BUCKET_DISALLOWS at policy.py:157 always fires first. test_an_account_in_good_standing_gets_a_reminder_but_not_a_dial (test_treatment_engine.py:379-384) says so explicitly - 'Structurally blocked by the bucket before the delinquency test is reached, which is the stronger of the two guards' - and asserts BUCKET_DISALLOWS.

**Impact.** A veto code that can never appear is a category in the supervisor's suppression breakdown that will always read zero, and a reader auditing the compliance gates will count a guard that does no work. Minor on its own, but it is the second dead artefact found in this pass (RESOLVING at followthrough.py:65 is the other), which suggests the pattern is not isolated.

**Fix.** Either delete the branch and its constant, or keep it as a defensive assertion that raises rather than returning a reason, so it cannot silently be dead. Add a test that enumerates every veto constant and asserts each is reachable from some constructible feature vector - the same shape as the action-reachability test proposed above.

### `sweep-decided-today-ignores-mode-and-tenant` — The sweep's once-per-day guard matches any decision row for the case key, including a simulated one, so a simulated row against a real customer would silently skip that borrower's real sweep for the day

**backend/agent_core/treatment/sweep.py:195** · correctness · defect · unverified (verifier-added) · reader `X02-tests-engine-reco`

sweep._decided_today (sweep.py:195-207) is `SELECT 1 FROM treatment_decisions WHERE customer_id = :cid AND trigger_kind = :kind AND trigger_ref = :ref LIMIT 1` - no `mode <> 'simulated'` and no tenant_id, unlike every other reader of the same table that matters: claim_due (decisions.py:365-368), open_cases (followthrough.py:379) and attribute_outcomes (followthrough.py:108-110) all exclude simulated rows by name, and claim_due's comment calls that predicate 'the only thing standing between a generated borrower and a real outbound message'.

**Impact.** Today the harm is latent rather than live: scripts/simulate_treatment_corpus.py:567-577 selects only `WHERE a.id LIKE 'SIM-%'`, so generated decisions never share a customer id with a real borrower. The defect is that the guard's correctness depends on a filter in a script rather than on a predicate in the query. Any change that lets the simulator, a replay harness or a shadow backfill write a dpd_tick row against a real customer id silently removes that borrower from the day's sweep - no decision, no log line, no error, and the borrower is simply not worked that day. The same query with no tenant filter would also let one tenant's decision suppress another's sweep on a shared customer id.

**Fix.** Add `AND mode <> 'simulated' AND tenant_id = :tenant` to _decided_today so the guard matches the same row population every other reader uses, and add a test that a simulated dpd_tick row for today does not stop the real sweep from deciding.

### `reco-suppress-no-candidates-uncovered` — SUPPRESS_NO_CANDIDATES is the one reco gate with no test, and it is the one a fresh catalogue hits first

**backend/tests/test_reco_engine.py:163** · testing · missing-for-production · 1/1 confirm · reader `X02-tests-engine-reco`

agent_core/reco/arbitration.py:27-38 declares twelve SUPPRESS_ constants. test_every_gate_suppresses_with_its_own_reason (test_reco_engine.py:163-195) covers ten; SUPPRESS_BELOW_THRESHOLD is covered at line 210; `SUPPRESS_NO_CANDIDATES = "no_eligible_candidates"` (arbitration.py:37, returned at arbitration.py:109) is covered nowhere in the seven files. Unlike the treatment side there is also no reco equivalent of test_every_suppression_reason_renders_as_prose asserting each code has a label.

**Impact.** On a customer's first install the product catalogue is empty or entirely gated by eligibility, so no_eligible_candidates is the reason every rep sees for weeks. If the reason or its label regressed, nothing would catch it, and the rep would be told nothing at all about why the offer panel is blank.

**Fix.** Add the missing parametrised case with an empty offers list, and add the reco counterpart of the render-as-prose test asserting every SUPPRESS_ constant plus every `hold:` and `eligibility:` prefix has an explicit entry in _SUPPRESSION_LABELS.

### `reco-strip-fence-untested` — The reco reranker test monkeypatches away the fence stripper it should be exercising

**backend/tests/test_reco_models.py:366** · testing · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `X02-tests-engine-reco`

test_reranker_drops_ids_the_engine_never_approved (test_reco_models.py:366-368) does `monkeypatch.setattr(models, "_strip_fence", lambda raw: raw)` and then returns bare JSON from the fake Azure client. So the code path that handles a model wrapping its reply in a ```json fence - the single most common LLM output quirk - is disabled in the only test that reaches it. The treatment counterpart at rerank.py:39-41 has the same helper and no test at all.

**Impact.** A model that starts fencing its output (a deployment version bump is enough) would make json.loads raise, the except at models' _ask would swallow it, and the reranker would silently degrade to the base order forever with only a warning in logs that api logs discard. Low harm because the fallback is safe, but the feature would be silently off.

**Fix.** Remove the monkeypatch and have the fake client return a fenced payload, so the stripper is what makes the test pass. Add a unit test for _strip_fence over bare, ```-fenced and ```json-fenced inputs in both modules.

### `reco-split-band-too-wide` — The only proportion test in the set uses a band six standard deviations wide, so it cannot detect a 20% relative bias in the bucketing

**backend/tests/test_reco_models.py:546** · statistics · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `X02-tests-engine-reco`

test_variant_assignment_respects_the_split (test_reco_models.py:540-547) draws 4,000 customers against a 90/10 split and asserts `0.07 < share < 0.13`. For p=0.1, n=4000 the standard error is 0.0047, so the band is roughly ±6.3 sigma. A hash that systematically delivered 12% instead of 10% - a 20% relative error that would materially bias any comparison - passes comfortably. The comment concedes the looseness ('allow slack — this asserts "roughly 10%", not "exactly"') without noting how much.

**Impact.** Small in itself; significant as the only statistical assertion in the set. If the design doc holds this test up as evidence that randomisation is validated, it is over-claiming by a factor of six.

**Fix.** Replace the eyeballed interval with an explicit test at a stated significance - a binomial or chi-square check at, say, 4 sigma - and state the detectable effect size in the docstring. Apply the same shape to the treatment split test proposed above.

### `field-visit-sunday-uses-process-tz` — The Sunday-avoidance assertion converts to the process timezone, not the borrower's, so it tests a different property in a UTC container than on an IST developer machine

**backend/tests/test_treatment_engine.py:298** · correctness · defect · 1/1 confirm · reader `X02-tests-engine-reco`

test_treatment_engine.py:298 `assert timing._local_day_index(slot.at.astimezone()) != timing._SUNDAY`. `datetime.astimezone()` with no argument converts to the system local zone. timing._local_day_index (timing.py:73-75) documents that it expects a moment already in the borrower's zone, and timing.py:126 calls it as `_local_day_index(local)` where local is `cursor.astimezone(tz)` with tz from features.timezone_name. The test's features carry `timezone_name: "Asia/Kolkata"` (test_treatment_engine.py:62) which the assertion ignores.

**Impact.** IST is UTC+05:30, so the assertion only diverges for slots between 00:00 and 05:30 IST - which FIELD_VISIT_HOUR = 10 (timing.py:55) makes unreachable, so today the test passes for the wrong reason. Any future change that widens the field-visit window, or a tenant in a zone west of UTC, makes the test silently assert something else. A field visit on a Sunday is a fair-practices problem and is about to become a documented one under the 2027 circular's prior-intimation rule; the guard for it should not depend on the container's TZ env.

**Fix.** Assert against the borrower's zone explicitly: `timing._local_day_index(slot.at.astimezone(ZoneInfo("Asia/Kolkata")))`, or better expose a public `timing.local_day(slot.at, features)` and assert on that so the test does not reach into a private helper. Add a second case with a non-IST timezone_name.

### `reserve-and-floor-thresholds-unjustified` — The value floor and reserve margin are asserted by constructing an instalment that lands in the right band, which pins the test to the current constants rather than to the behaviour

**backend/tests/test_treatment_engine.py:702** · statistics · hidden-assumption · 1/1 confirm · reader `X02-tests-engine-reco`

test_the_last_contact_slot_is_reserved_for_something_better (test_treatment_engine.py:702-715) comments 'Sized so the best action clears the floor (₹2) but not the reserve margin (3×) — the band the reserve exists for' and uses `instalment_amount=300.0`. The floor comes from `min_expected_value=env_float("TREATMENT_MIN_EV", 2.0)` (config.py:248) and the reserve from `policy.min_expected_value * policy.reserve_margin` (arbitration.py:161). A ₹2 expected-value floor against Indian instalments, and a 3x reserve margin, are both planning numbers with no stated derivation, and the test encodes the arithmetic of hitting the band rather than the property.

**Impact.** Retuning TREATMENT_MIN_EV - which a collections head will absolutely want to do - breaks a test that is not about the value being tested, and the failure message will not say so. More importantly a ₹2 floor means almost nothing is ever below it on a real book, so SUPPRESS_BELOW_FLOOR will effectively never fire and the 'waiting is the decision' behaviour the design is proud of is unreachable at production ticket sizes.

**Fix.** Compute the fixture's instalment from the policy at test time rather than hard-coding 300.0, so the test survives retuning and states the property directly. Separately, derive the floor from the cheapest action's cost plus a stated margin rather than from a bare constant, and add a monitor for the realised suppression rate by reason so a floor that never fires is visible.
